50	class RequestContextMiddleware:
51	    """Outermost user middleware: request id, access log and safe errors."""
52	
53	    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
54	        self.app = app
55	
56	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
57	        if scope["type"] != "http":
58	            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
59	            return
60	
61	        request_id = _request_id(scope)
62	        token = request_id_var.set(request_id)
63	        path = scope.get("path", "")
64	        method = scope.get("method", "")
65	        client = scope.get("client")
66	        client_hash = hash_client_ip(client[0])[:16] if client else "-"
67	        started = time.perf_counter()
68	        state = {"status": 500, "started": False}
69	
70	        async def send_wrapper(message: Message) -> None:
71	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
72	                state["started"] = True
73	                state["status"] = message["status"]
74	                headers = list(message.get("headers", []))
75	                present = {key.lower() for key, _ in headers}
76	                headers.append((b"x-request-id", request_id.encode()))
77	                for key, value in SECURITY_HEADERS:
78	                    is_doc = any(path.startswith(prefix) for prefix in DOC_PATHS)
79	                    if key == b"content-security-policy" and is_doc:
80	                        continue
81	                    if key not in present:
82	                        headers.append((key, value))
83	                if path.startswith("/api") and b"cache-control" not in present:
84	                    headers.append((b"cache-control", b"no-store"))
85	                elif path.startswith("/media/") and b"cache-control" not in present:
86	                    headers.append((b"cache-control", b"private, no-store"))
87	                if settings.is_production and scope.get("scheme") == "https":
88	                    if b"strict-transport-security" not in present:
89	                        headers.append(
90	                            (
91	                                b"strict-transport-security",
92	                                b"max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains",
93	                            )
94	                        )
95	                message = {**message, "headers": headers}
96	            await send(message)
97	
98	        try:
99	            await self.app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)
100	        except Exception:
101	            error_logger.exception(
102	                "unhandled_error",
103	                extra={"method": method, "path": redact_path(path), "client": client_hash},
104	            )
105	            if not state["started"]:
106	                payload = json.dumps(
107	                    {
108	                        "detail": "Internal server error",
109	                        "request_id": request_id,
110	                    }
111	                ).encode()
112	                await send(
113	                    {
114	                        "type": "http.response.start",
115	                        "status": 500,
116	                        "headers": [
117	                            (b"content-type", b"application/json"),
118	                            (b"content-length", str(len(payload)).encode()),
119	                            (b"x-request-id", request_id.encode()),
120	                        ],
121	                    }
122	                )
123	                await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": payload})
124	            state["status"] = state["status"] if state["started"] else 500
125	        finally:
126	            duration_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000, 2)
127	            access_logger.info(
128	                "request",
129	                extra={
130	                    "method": method,
131	                    "path": redact_path(path),
132	                    "status": state["status"],
133	                    "duration_ms": duration_ms,
134	                    "client": client_hash,
135	                },
136	            )
137	            request_id_var.reset(token)

140	class BodyTooLarge(Exception):
141	    pass
142	
143	
144	class BodySizeLimitMiddleware:
145	    """Reject oversized bodies before they reach application code."""
146	
147	    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, max_bytes: int | None = None) -> None:
148	        self.app = app
149	        self.max_bytes = max_bytes or settings.max_request_bytes
150	
151	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
152	        if scope["type"] != "http":
153	            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
154	            return
155	
156	        headers = {key.lower(): value for key, value in scope.get("headers", [])}
157	        declared = headers.get(b"content-length")
158	        if declared:
159	            try:
160	                if int(declared) > self.max_bytes:
161	                    await self._reject(send)
162	                    return
163	            except ValueError:
164	                await self._reject(send)
165	                return
166	
167	        received = 0
168	        response_started = False
169	
170	        async def limited_receive() -> Message:
171	            nonlocal received
172	            message = await receive()
173	            if message["type"] == "http.request":
174	                received += len(message.get("body", b""))
175	                if received > self.max_bytes:
176	                    raise BodyTooLarge()
177	            return message
178	
179	        async def tracking_send(message: Message) -> None:
180	            nonlocal response_started
181	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
182	                response_started = True
183	            await send(message)
184	
185	        try:
186	            await self.app(scope, limited_receive, tracking_send)
187	        except BodyTooLarge:
188	            if not response_started:
189	                await self._reject(send)
190	
191	    async def _reject(self, send: Send) -> None:
192	        payload = json.dumps({"detail": "Request body too large"}).encode()
193	        await send(
194	            {
195	                "type": "http.response.start",
196	                "status": 413,
197	                "headers": [
198	                    (b"content-type", b"application/json"),
199	                    (b"content-length", str(len(payload)).encode()),
200	                ],
201	            }
202	        )
203	        await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": payload})

1	"""Per-IP sliding-window rate limiting.
2	
3	Single-process in-memory limiter: adequate for one API instance. Horizontal
4	scaling needs a shared limiter at the gateway or a Redis-backed limiter; both
5	are documented in DEPLOYMENT.md. Health endpoints are exempt so probes never
6	consume the budget.
7	"""
8	
9	import time
10	from collections import defaultdict, deque
11	
12	from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
13	from starlette.requests import Request
14	from starlette.responses import JSONResponse
15	
16	from .config import settings
17	
18	WINDOW_SECONDS = 60.0
19	MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS = 20_000
20	EXEMPT_PATHS = {"/api/health", "/api/ready", "/api/openapi.json"}
21	
22	
23	def _client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
24	    if settings.trust_proxy_headers:
25	        forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")
26	        if forwarded:
27	            candidate = forwarded.split(",")[0].strip()
28	            if candidate:
29	                return candidate
30	    return request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"
31	
32	
33	def _bucket_for(path: str, method: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
34	    if path in {"/api/auth/login", "/api/auth/register", "/api/auth/refresh", "/api/auth/logout"}:
35	        return "auth", settings.auth_rate_limit_per_minute
36	    if path.startswith("/api/companion/") and path.endswith("/respond") and method == "POST":
37	        return "companion", settings.companion_rate_limit_per_minute
38	    if method == "POST" and (
39	        path.endswith("/media") or path.endswith("/memories") or path.endswith("/sync")
40	    ):
41	        return "upload", settings.upload_rate_limit_per_minute
42	    return "default", settings.rate_limit_per_minute
43	
44	
45	class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
46	    def __init__(self, app):
47	        super().__init__(app)
48	        self._hits: dict[tuple[str, str], deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)
49	
50	    def _trim(self, now: float) -> None:
51	        if len(self._hits) <= MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS:
52	            return
53	        for key in [key for key, window in self._hits.items() if not window]:
54	            self._hits.pop(key, None)
55	        while len(self._hits) > MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS:
56	            self._hits.pop(next(iter(self._hits)))
57	
58	    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
59	        path = request.url.path
60	        if not path.startswith("/api") or request.method == "OPTIONS" or path in EXEMPT_PATHS:
61	            return await call_next(request)
62	
63	        now = time.monotonic()
64	        bucket, limit = _bucket_for(path, request.method)
65	        key = (_client_ip(request), bucket)
66	        window = self._hits[key]
67	        while window and now - window[0] > WINDOW_SECONDS:
68	            window.popleft()
69	        if len(window) >= limit:
70	            retry_after = max(1, int(WINDOW_SECONDS - (now - window[0])) + 1)
71	            return JSONResponse(
72	                status_code=429,
73	                headers={"Retry-After": str(retry_after)},
74	                content={"detail": "Too many requests. Please slow down."},
75	            )
76	        window.append(now)
77	        self._trim(now)
78	        return await call_next(request)

# Public catalog: readable by anyone, writable only by admin/system.
CATALOG = ("destinations", "places", "activities", "place_sources")


def _create_policies() -> None:
    for sql in HELPERS:
        op.execute(sql)
    for table, commands in POLICIES.items():
        op.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY")
        op.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY")
        for command, expression in commands.items():
            if command == "insert":
                op.execute(
                    f"CREATE POLICY p_{table}_insert ON {table} FOR INSERT "
                    f"WITH CHECK ({expression})"
                )
                continue
            check = f" WITH CHECK ({expression})" if command == "update" else ""
            op.execute(
                f"CREATE POLICY p_{table}_{command} ON {table} FOR {command.upper()} "
                f"USING ({expression}){check}"
            )
    for table in CATALOG:
        op.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY")
        op.execute(f"ALTER TABLE {table} FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY")
        op.execute(f"CREATE POLICY p_{table}_select ON {table} FOR SELECT USING (true)")
        for command in ("insert", "update", "delete"):
            clause = "USING" if command == "delete" else "WITH CHECK"
            op.execute(
                f"CREATE POLICY p_{table}_{command} ON {table} FOR {command.upper()} "
                f"{clause} (safar_admin() OR safar_system())"
            )
    # Membership lookups are on the hot path for almost every policy.
    op.execute(

2	
3	The application connects as a non-owner role in production. Every transaction
4	sets the ``app.*`` GUCs below; policies use them through SECURITY DEFINER
5	helpers. With no context, policies deny access (fail closed).

7	
8	from contextlib import contextmanager
9	
10	from sqlalchemy import event, text
11	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
12	
13	_GUC_NAMES = {
14	    "app_user_id": "app.user_id",
15	    "app_admin": "app.admin",
16	    "app_system": "app.system",
17	    "app_auth": "app.auth",
18	    "app_companion_link": "app.companion_link",
19	    "app_invitation_token": "app.invitation_token",
20	}
21	
22	_SETTINGS_SQL = text(
23	    "SELECT "
24	    + ", ".join(
25	        f"set_config('{guc}', :{key}, true)" for key, guc in _GUC_NAMES.items()
26	    )
27	)
28	
29	
30	def _params(values: dict) -> dict:
31	    return {key: str(values.get(key) or "") for key in _GUC_NAMES}
32	
33	
34	def _apply(connection, values: dict) -> None:
35	    connection.execute(_SETTINGS_SQL, _params(values))
36	
37	
38	@event.listens_for(Session, "after_begin")
39	def _apply_on_begin(session, transaction, connection) -> None:
40	    if connection.dialect.name != "postgresql":
41	        return
42	    _apply(connection, session.info.get("safar_context", {}))
43	
44	
45	def set_context(db: Session, **values) -> None:
46	    merged = dict(db.info.get("safar_context", {}))
47	    for key, value in values.items():
48	        if key not in _GUC_NAMES:
49	            raise KeyError(f"Unknown database context key: {key}")
50	        merged[key] = value
51	    db.info["safar_context"] = merged
52	    bind = db.get_bind()
53	    if bind.dialect.name == "postgresql" and db.in_transaction():
54	        _apply(db.connection(), merged)
55	
56	
57	def set_user_context(db: Session, user_id: str, admin: bool = False) -> None:
58	    set_context(db, app_user_id=user_id, app_admin="on" if admin else "")
59	
60	
61	def auth_context(db: Session) -> None:
62	    set_context(db, app_auth="on")
63	
64	
65	def companion_context(db: Session, link_id: str) -> None:
66	    set_context(db, app_companion_link=link_id)
67	
68

70	def system_context(db: Session):
71	    """Temporarily mark the transaction as a trusted internal task."""
72	    previous = db.info.get("safar_context", {}).get("app_system")
73	    set_context(db, app_system="on")
74	    try:
75	        yield
76	    finally:

1	"""Structured JSON logging with request correlation.
2	
3	Request bodies, cookies, authorization headers and query strings are never
4	logged. Companion and invitation tokens embedded in the path are redacted
5	before the path reaches the log stream.
6	"""
7	
8	import json
9	import logging
10	import sys
11	from contextvars import ContextVar
12	
13	from app.core.config import settings
14	
15	request_id_var: ContextVar[str] = ContextVar("request_id", default="-")
16	
17	REDACTED_SEGMENTS = {"companion", "invitations", "media"}
18	REDACTED = "<redacted>"
19	
20	
21	def redact_path(path: str) -> str:
22	    parts = path.split("/")
23	    # /api/<segment>/<token>...
24	    if len(parts) > 3 and parts[1] == "api" and parts[2] in REDACTED_SEGMENTS:
25	        parts[3] = REDACTED
26	    return "/".join(parts)
27	
28	
29	class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
30	    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
31	        payload = {
32	            "ts": self.formatTime(record, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
33	            "level": record.levelname,
34	            "logger": record.name,
35	            "message": record.getMessage(),
36	            "request_id": request_id_var.get(),
37	        }
38	        for key in ("method", "path", "status", "duration_ms", "client"):
39	            value = getattr(record, key, None)
40	            if value is not None:
41	                payload[key] = value
42	        if record.exc_info:
43	            payload["exception"] = self.formatException(record.exc_info)
44	        return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)
45	
46	
47	def configure_logging() -> None:
48	    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
49	    handler.setFormatter(JsonFormatter())
50	    root = logging.getLogger()
51	    root.handlers[:] = [handler]
52	    root.setLevel(settings.log_level)
53	    # Uvicorn's access log would print raw paths (including one-use tokens),
54	    # so the request middleware emits the sanitised access log instead.
55	    access = logging.getLogger("uvicorn.access")
56	    access.handlers[:] = []
57	    access.propagate = False
58	    access.disabled = True
59

62	    """Initialise an error monitor when a provider is explicitly configured.
63	
64	    SAFAR ships without a paid monitoring dependency. If ``sentry-sdk`` is
65	    installed and ``SENTRY_DSN`` is set, it is initialised; otherwise this is
66	    a no-op and operators can attach their own handler to the ``safar.error``
67	    logger documented in SECURITY.md.
68	    """
69	    dsn = settings.sentry_dsn

71	        return
72	    try:  # pragma: no cover - optional dependency
73	        import sentry_sdk
74	
75	        sentry_sdk.init(

78	            release=settings.release,
79	            traces_sample_rate=0.0,
80	            send_default_pii=False,
81	        )
82	    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - never block startup on telemetry
83	        logging.getLogger("safar.error").warning(

18	def _request_meta(request: Request | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
19	    if request is None:
20	        return None, None
21	    agent = (request.headers.get("user-agent") or "")[:200] or None
22	    client = request.client.host if request.client else None
23	    ip_hash = hash_client_ip(client) or None
24	    return agent, ip_hash
25	
26	
27	def create_session(
28	    db: Session, user: User, request: Request | None = None
29	) -> tuple[AuthSession, str]:
30	    secret = new_refresh_secret()
31	    agent, ip_hash = _request_meta(request)
32	    session = AuthSession(
33	        user_id=user.id,
34	        refresh_hash=hash_refresh_secret(secret),
35	        user_agent=agent,
36	        ip_hash=ip_hash,
37	        expires_at=utcnow() + timedelta(days=settings.refresh_token_expire_days),
38	    )
39	    db.add(session)
40	    db.flush()
41	    return session, f"{session.id}.{secret}"
42	
43	
44	def session_is_active(db: Session, session_id: str, user_id: str) -> bool:
45	    session = db.get(AuthSession, session_id)
46	    if not session or session.user_id != user_id:
47	        return False
48	    if session.revoked_at is not None:
49	        return False
50	    return session.expires_at > utcnow()
51	
52	
53	def rotate_refresh_token(
54	    db: Session, token: str, request: Request | None = None
55	) -> tuple[AuthSession | None, str | None, User | None]:
56	    """Returns (session, refresh_token, user). A mismatch revokes the session."""
57	    session_id, separator, secret = token.partition(".")
58	    if not separator or not session_id or not secret:
59	        return None, None, None
60	    session = db.get(AuthSession, session_id)
61	    if not session:
62	        return None, None, None
63	    if session.revoked_at is not None:
64	        return None, None, None
65	    if session.expires_at <= utcnow():
66	        session.revoked_at = utcnow()
67	        session.revoked_reason = "expired"
68	        db.commit()
69	        return None, None, None
70	    if session.refresh_hash != hash_refresh_secret(secret):
71	        # A previously rotated token was presented: treat as theft.
72	        session.revoked_at = utcnow()
73	        session.revoked_reason = "refresh_reuse"
74	        db.commit()
75	        return None, None, None
76	    user = db.get(User, session.user_id)
77	    if not user or not user.is_active or user.deleted_at:
78	        session.revoked_at = utcnow()
79	        session.revoked_reason = "account_unavailable"
80	        db.commit()
81	        return None, None, None
82	
83	    new_secret = new_refresh_secret()
84	    session.refresh_hash = hash_refresh_secret(new_secret)
85	    session.last_used_at = utcnow()
86	    session.expires_at = utcnow() + timedelta(
87	        days=settings.refresh_token_expire_days
88	    )
89	    agent, ip_hash = _request_meta(request)
90	    if agent:
91	        session.user_agent = agent
92	    if ip_hash:
93	        session.ip_hash = ip_hash
94	    db.commit()
95	    return session, f"{session.id}.{new_secret}", user
96

98	def revoke_session(db: Session, session_id: str, reason: str = "logout") -> None:
99	    session = db.get(AuthSession, session_id)
100	    if session and session.revoked_at is None:
101	        session.revoked_at = utcnow()
102	        session.revoked_reason = reason
103	        db.commit()
104	
105	
106	def revoke_all_sessions(db: Session, user_id: str, reason: str = "logout_all") -> None:
107	    now = utcnow()
108	    db.query(AuthSession).filter(
109	        AuthSession.user_id == user_id, AuthSession.revoked_at.is_(None)
110	    ).update(
111	        {"revoked_at": now, "revoked_reason": reason}, synchronize_session=False
112	    )
113	    db.commit()
114	
115	
116	def active_session_count(db: Session, user_id: str) -> int:
117	    return (
118	        db.query(AuthSession)
119	        .filter(
120	            AuthSession.user_id == user_id,
121	            AuthSession.revoked_at.is_(None),
122	            AuthSession.expires_at > utcnow(),
123	        )
124	        .count()

export const API_URL =
  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL?.replace(/\/$/, "") || "http://localhost:8000";

const CSRF_COOKIE = "safar_csrf";
const CSRF_HEADER = "X-CSRF-Token";
const UNSAFE = new Set(["POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"]);

// Access and CSRF tokens live in memory only. The refresh token is an
// HttpOnly cookie that JavaScript can never read.
let accessToken: string | null = null;
let csrfToken: string | null = null;
let refreshInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;

export class ApiError extends Error {
  status: number;
  detail: unknown;

  constructor(status: number, detail: unknown) {
    const message =
      typeof detail === "string"
        ? detail
        : Array.isArray(detail)
          ? detail
              .map((item) =>
                typeof item === "object" && item && "msg" in item
                  ? String((item as { msg: unknown }).msg)
                  : String(item),
              )
              .join(" · ")
          : detail && typeof detail === "object" && "message" in detail
            ? String((detail as { message: unknown }).message)
            : `Request failed (${status})`;
    super(message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.status = status;
    this.detail = detail;
  }
}

export function setSessionTokens(access: string | null, csrf: string | null) {
  accessToken = access;
  csrfToken = csrf;
}

export function clearSessionTokens() {
  accessToken = null;
  csrfToken = null;
}

export function getAccessToken(): string | null {
  return accessToken;
}

function readCookie(name: string): string | null {
  if (typeof document === "undefined") return null;
  const match = document.cookie
    .split(";")
    .map((part) => part.trim())
    .find((part) => part.startsWith(`${name}=`));
  return match ? decodeURIComponent(match.slice(name.length + 1)) : null;
  }
}

type Options = Omit<RequestInit, "body"> & { body?: unknown; raw?: boolean };

async function request<T>(path: string, options: Options, retried: boolean): Promise<T> {
  const method = (options.method || "GET").toUpperCase();
  const headers = new Headers(options.headers);
  if (options.body !== undefined && !(options.body instanceof FormData)) {
    headers.set("Content-Type", "application/json");
  }
  headers.set("Accept", "application/json");
  if (accessToken) headers.set("Authorization", `Bearer ${accessToken}`);
  const csrf = currentCsrf();
  if (UNSAFE.has(method) && csrf) headers.set(CSRF_HEADER, csrf);

  const response = await fetch(`${API_URL}${path}`, {
    ...options,
    headers,
    credentials: "include",
    body:
      options.body === undefined
        ? undefined
        : options.body instanceof FormData
          ? options.body
          : JSON.stringify(options.body),
    cache: "no-store",
  });

  if (response.status === 401 && !retried && !path.startsWith("/api/auth/")) {
    const refreshed = await refreshSession();
    if (refreshed) return request<T>(path, options, true);
    if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
      window.dispatchEvent(new Event("safar:unauthorized"));
    }
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    let detail: unknown = response.statusText;
    try {
      const data = await response.json();
      detail = data.detail ?? data;
    } catch {
      try {
        detail = await response.text();
      } catch {
        /* ignore */
      }
    }
    throw new ApiError(response.status, detail);
  }

With no GUC, policies deny\n  access (fail closed).\n- Membership helpers (`safar_is_trip_member`, `safar_is_trip_admin`, …) are\n  `SECURITY DEFINER` with `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`.\n- Production connects as a **non-owner role without `BYPASSRLS`**; the\n  migration role needs bypass rights. Exact SQL is in\n  `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` §3.\n- Application-layer authorization and serializers remain the primary control.\n  RLS is the backstop, not a replacement: it is row-level, so column-level\n  privacy (budget limits, access needs, pact limits) is still enforced by the\n  serializers described in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §3.\n\n### Domain coverage\n\n| Domain | Tables | Policy intent |\n|---|---|---|\n| Identity & consent | users, profiles, user_preferences, journey_dna, consent_records, user_blocks, notifications, audit_logs, auth_sessions | Self; shared-trip/circle/connection peers see public profile fields only at the serializer; invites visible to inviter/invitee. `audit_logs` requires `app.admin` or system. |\n| Trips | trips, trip_members, trip_invitations, journey_pacts, planner_tasks, trip_branches, material_watch, journey_capsules | Active members; invitations also visible to the matching email or invitation token; trip privacy `public` grants read only to authenticated users. |\n| Catalog | destinations, places, activities, place_sources | Public read; writes only admin/system. |\n| Planning | itinerary_items, itinerary_versions, itinerary_proposals, activity_votes, itinerary_attendance, shadowplans | Trip members; votes/attendance own-row writes; shadowplans owner. |\n| Intelligence | recommendation_batches, recommendations, recommendation_feedback, activity_feedback | Trip members; feedback owner; companion link may read its own target. |\n| Pulse & ground | trip_pulse, ground_requests, ground_responses | Trip members; ground responses by matching local contributors. |\n| Money | expenses, expense_participants, expense_settlements | Trip members only. |\n| Memory | trip_memories, memory_permissions | Owner, explicit `can_view` permission, admin or system. |\n| Social | travel_circles, circle_members, circle_posts, local_contributors, connection_requests, saved_inspiration, traveller_matches, abuse_reports, place_reports | Public/circle/connection scopes; place reports are publicly readable by design, writes restricted to the reporter. |\n| Offline | offline_sync_queue | Owner only. |\n| Companion | companion_links, companion_responses | Link creator, trip admin, or the link's own transaction context; responses have no user id/IP/user-agent columns. |\n\n### Direct SQL evidence (PG 16.4, role `safar_app`, fresh `safar_p5_final`)\n\n| Probe | Result |\n|---|---|\n| `SELECT count(*) FROM trips` with no GUCs | **0** |\n| As mira (`app.user_id`) | **6** trips |\n| As jonas | **3** trips |\n| Foreign trip by id / its expenses / its members | **0 / 0 / 0** |\n| With `app.system='on'` | **9** trips |\n| `audit_logs` as mira without admin | **0** |\n| `audit_logs` as mira with `app.admin='on'` | **85** |\n| `INSERT INTO trips (created_by = mira)` while acting as jonas | **rejected**: `new row violates row-level security policy for table \"trips\"` |\n\nThe full 68-test suite also passed while connected as `safar_app` with FORCE\nRLS, which proves the product flows operate inside the policies rather than\naround them.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Authentication and session changes\n\n### Cookies\n\n| Cookie | Contents | HttpOnly | Path | Lifetime | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `safar_access` | HS256 JWT (`sub`, `sid`, `typ: access`) | yes | `/` | 15 min | `Secure` in production; also accepted as `Authorization: Bearer` for API clients |\n| `safar_refresh` | `<session_id>.<random secret>` | yes | `/api/auth` | 30 days, rotated on every refresh | Stored server-side as SHA-256; never readable by JavaScript |\n| `safar_csrf` | random 32-byte token | **no** (by design) | `/` | 30 days | Echoed in `X-CSRF-Token`; compared with `hmac.compare_digest` |\n\n`SameSite` defaults to `lax`; `none` requires `Secure` (enforced at startup).\n`Secure` defaults to true when `ENVIRONMENT=production`. `COOKIE_DOMAIN` is\noptional for a shared parent domain.\n\n### Server-side sessions\n\n- `auth_sessions` records user, refresh hash, user agent, keyed-hashed IP,\n  expiry, last use, revocation time and reason.\n- Every authenticated request checks that the session referenced by `sid`\n  still exists, belongs to the user, is unrevoked and unexpired. A stolen\n  access token stops working as soon as its session is revoked.\n- Refresh rotation: each refresh replaces the stored hash. Presenting a\n  previously rotated secret is treated as theft and revokes the session\n  (`reason=refresh_reuse`).\n- Logout revokes the session for both cookie and bearer callers; repeated\n  logout is idempotent.\n- WebSocket: `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` issues a two-minute `typ: ws` JWT bound\n  to the session. The socket re-checks user status, session state and trip\n  membership before accepting. The first-party client always uses this\n  ticket. The endpoint also accepts a normal access token for compatibility —\n  see the query-string risk in §7.\n\n### Frontend\n\n- `lib/api.ts` keeps access and CSRF tokens in module memory only; nothing is\n  written to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` (only the theme and the offline\n  queue are persisted).\n- Every request uses `credentials: \"include\"`. Unsafe methods add\n  `X-CSRF-Token`. A 401 triggers one silent refresh and one retry; concurrent\n  callers share the in-flight refresh.\n- On page load the app restores the session from the HttpOnly refresh cookie\n  (`/api/auth/refresh`) and then `/api/auth/me`.\n- Sign-out clears server state and redirects to `/login?next=…`.\n\n### Browser evidence (production build, 2026-11-19)\n\n| Step | Observed |\n|---|---|\n| Sign in as `mira@safar.demo` | `POST /api/auth/login` 200; redirect to `/dashboard`; dashboard, trips and `/api/users/me` load |\n| Cookies after login | `document.cookie` contains **only** `safar_csrf=…`; access and refresh are HttpOnly |\n| Trip page | `/trips/<id>/itinerary` renders the confirmed plan (9 items, protected block, version 3) |\n| Sign out | Redirect to `/login?next=%2Fprofile`; `document.cookie` empty |\n| After sign out | `fetch('/api/auth/me')` → **401**; `fetch('/api/auth/refresh')` → **401** |\n\n### Account deletion and retention\n\n- Deletion removes: Journey DNA, activity/recommendation feedback, votes,\n  approvals, attendance, pulse answers, memory permissions, saved inspiration,\n  offline queue, missions, circle membership/posts, contributor status, place\n  reports, shadowplans, connection requests, matches, pending invitations;\n  revokes companion links and all sessions; deletes own `/media/` files; nulls\n  memory text/caption/location; sets memories private and soft-deleted;\n  anonymises trip memberships (`Former traveller`, budget null, needs empty).\n  Shared itinerary/expense history remains for other members, without the\n  person's private data.\n- Retention defaults: sessions 30 days, invitations 30, companion links 30,\n  notifications 180, offline queue 7, audit logs 365. All are environment\n  variables; the job is idempotent and can be scheduled externally.\n\n---\n\n## 5. PostgreSQL verification\n\n### Schema and migrations\n\n- Engine: PostgreSQL 16.4 (local cluster, `127.0.0.1:55432`).\n- Fresh database `safar_p5_final`: `alembic upgrade head` applied four\n  revisions in order (`9c224ee10414` baseline, `b1f6c2d84e71` companion links,\n  `c7d3e9a1f204` auth sessions, `d9e4f1b2c305` RLS) with no manual steps.\n- Result: 56 relations (55 model tables + `alembic_version`), 220 policies,\n  35 helper functions, 55 tables with ENABLE + FORCE RLS, 220 grants to\n  `safar_app` (55 tables × 4 verbs).\n- Baseline schema uses portable types: `JSON` (native `json` on PG, TEXT on\n  SQLite), `DateTime` (UTC-naive `timestamp without time zone` on PG),\n  explicit foreign keys and indexes; SQLite enables `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`.\n  The RLS migration is a no-op on SQLite.\n- Duplicate-submission, single-use link/invitation, private-memory and\n  multi-user isolation tests all pass on PG, exercising transactions and\n  unique/foreign-key constraints under real concurrency semantics at test\n  scale.\n\n### SQLite-specific assumptions (what SQLite tests do **not** prove)\n\n| Assumption | Consequence |\n|---|---|\n| SQLite has no roles or RLS | The SQLite suite proves application-layer authorization only. RLS must be verified on PG (it was, §3). |\n| Tests/dev use `create_all`; production uses Alembic | A model change without a migration would pass SQLite tests and fail at production startup. Keep `alembic check` in CI. |\n| SQLite ignores `FORCE` and GUCs | `app.*` context code is a no-op there; RLS bugs can only be caught on PG. |\n| SQLite locking differs | Concurrency behaviour at production scale is untested (§7). |\n| Timestamps are UTC-naive in both engines | Consistent today, but not timezone-aware. Multi-region or DST-sensitive reporting would need `timestamptz`. |\n\n### PostgreSQL test run\n\n```\nSAFAR_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://safar_app:…@127.0.0.1:55432/safar_p5_final \\\n  python -m pytest -q        → 68 passed in 18.59s\npython -m pytest -q          → 68 passed in 19.71s   (SQLite)\n```\n\nThe PG run must use a **fresh** database (or truncate between runs): the\nprepared test mode seeds only when the user table is empty, so reusing a dirty\ndatabase accumulates demo rows and can fail two order-dependent assertions.\nThis is a test-harness property, not an application defect; it is recorded in\n§7.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Backup and recovery verification\n\nPerformed 2026-11-19 against the fresh PG database:\n\n| Step | Command (abridged) | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| Dump | `pg_dump -Fc -f safar-backup-2026-11-19.dump safar_p5_final` | 358,169 bytes, exit 0 |\n| Restore | `createdb safar_restore_check` + `pg_restore -d safar_restore_check --no-owner` | exit 0, no errors |\n| Schema parity | `pg_tables`, `pg_policies`, `pg_class.relforcerowsecurity` | identical: 56 tables, 220 policies, 55 tables with FORCE RLS |\n| Row parity | `users`, `trips`, `trip_memories` | identical: 20 / 7 / 9 |\n| RLS after restore | `SET ROLE safar_app`; no-context vs mira | 0 vs 6 — policies restored and effective |\n| Grants | re-granted to `safar_app` after restore | 220 privileges |\n\nMedia files are **not** in the database. `/media` is a local Docker volume;\n`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` §6 documents backing it up alongside the dump and warns\nthat a database-only restore leaves media references dangling. Verified\nlimitations: the drill covered schema, data, policies and grants, not a\npoint-in-time recovery (no WAL archiving is configured) and not a restore\nthrough the Docker volume path.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Remaining risks\n\nOrdered by importance. None of these is silently accepted: each has a\nmitigation or a deployment requirement, and the ones that matter are recorded\nin `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.\n\n| # | Risk | Why it remains | Mitigation / next step |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| R1 | **No external penetration test or security review** | Phase 5 was a self-assessment; tests prove intended behaviour, not absence of unknown classes of flaw. | Commission an external review before public launch. |\n| R2 | **Docker images were not built** | `docker` is unavailable in this environment. Compose and Dockerfiles are reviewed but unexecuted. | Build and smoke-test `docker compose up` in CI or on a host with Docker; verify non-root users, health checks and `alembic upgrade head` on first boot. |\n| R3 | **TLS/reverse-proxy path untested** | The stack was exercised over plain HTTP on localhost. HSTS only emits for HTTPS requests; `Secure` cookies require HTTPS. | Terminate TLS at a proxy, set `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true`, test login/refresh/cookies over HTTPS, and confirm HSTS. |\n| R4 | **WebSocket token in the query string** | Browsers cannot set handshake headers. The 2-minute ticket limits exposure, but reverse proxies may log query strings and the ticket is not stored single-use. | Use WSS, disable/redact query-string logging at the proxy, keep the 2-minute TTL; consider a single-use ticket store if multi-instance. |\n| R5 | **Rate limiting is in-process** | Each API process has its own counters; horizontal scaling multiplies limits. `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted only when explicitly enabled. | Enforce limits at the gateway or move to a shared store (Redis) when running more than one instance. |\n| R6 | **Companion/invitation tokens travel in URLs** | That is the product (one-link access). API responses set `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, logs redact the path, and links are single-use with expiry/revocation. | Keep token TTLs short, avoid embedding links in third-party pages, and include the web origin in the proxy's no-referrer/no-log policy. |\n| R7 | **No production-scale load/concurrency testing** | Concurrency was probed at small scale; PG locking, pool exhaustion and slow queries under load are unmeasured. | Load-test with representative data; size the pool and set statement/lock timeouts at the database. |\n| R8 | **Prepared PG test mode requires a clean database** | The harness seeds once and assumes an empty users table. | Create/migrate a fresh database per CI run. |\n| R9 | **No WAL archiving / PITR** | Backups are logical dumps; a dump cannot recover to an arbitrary point between runs. | Enable continuous archiving or managed PITR if the RPO demands it. |\n| R10 | **UTC-naive timestamps** | Correct and consistent, but not zone-aware. | Move to `timestamptz` if reporting crosses timezones or DST correctness matters. |\n| R11 | **No automated accessibility/Playwright suite** | Browser evidence is manual; regressions in security-sensitive UI flows would rely on unit tests. | Add Playwright flows for login, refresh, logout and companion links in CI. |\n| R12 | **Optional monitoring is not configured** | Sentry is an integration point (`safar.error` + `SENTRY_DSN`), not a shipped dependency. | Attach an error monitor and log shipping in the deployment environment. |\n| R13 | **Demo credentials in the UI** | The login page displays seeded credentials for the demo workspace. | They only exist when `SAFAR_SEED=true`; compose sets it to `false` for production. Never enable seeding on a public deployment. |\n\n---\n\n## 8. Production readiness assessment\n\nHonest verdict: **the application is security-hardened and PostgreSQL-ready,\nbut not production-certified.** The core controls are implemented and tested;\nthe unverified items are deployment-path items that require Docker, TLS and an\nexternal review.\n\n| Area | Status | Basis |\n|---|---|---|\n| Session/auth security | **Ready** | HttpOnly cookies, rotation, reuse detection, revocation, CSRF, session checks; tests + browser evidence |\n| Authorization (API) | **Ready** | 121 paths exercised across phases; private trips 404 for outsiders; admin gating; mass-assignment and IDOR tests |\n| Database isolation (RLS) | **Ready on PG** | 220 policies, FORCE RLS, fail-closed; direct SQL probes and a full suite as the non-owner role |\n| Privacy & user control | **Ready with limits** | Consent, export, erasure, retention, location toggle, memory permissions, blocking/reporting; no analytics pipeline ships, so no analytics-PII path exists |\n| Uploads & input handling | **Ready** | Magic-byte checks, 25 MB cap, validated schemas, no SQL injection or 5xx on malicious probes |\n| Secrets & configuration | **Ready** | No committed secrets (repo has no commits); env-only configuration; production guards for `SECRET_KEY`, CORS, cookies, docs, seeding; accurate `.env.example` |\n| Logging & monitoring | **Conditional** | Structured JSON, request ids, redaction and error hook exist; no monitor/log sink is configured in this environment |\n| Rate limiting / abuse | **Conditional** | Per-bucket limits and `Retry-After` work; single-process only (R5) |\n| Backup & recovery | **Conditional** | Logical dump/restore verified end to end; no PITR and no Docker-volume drill (R9) |\n| Infrastructure (Docker/CI) | **Not verified** | Images not built here (R2); CI/CD steps documented but not executed |\n| TLS / proxy / HSTS | **Not verified** | Plain HTTP localhost only (R3) |\n| Scale / performance | **Not verified** | No load testing (R7) |\n| External security review | **Not performed** | R1 |\n\n**Conditions for a public deployment**\n\n1. Build and smoke-test the images with Docker, non-root users and the\n   `alembic upgrade head` startup step.\n2. Terminate TLS at a proxy; set `ENVIRONMENT=production`, a 32+ character\n   `SECRET_KEY`, explicit `CORS_ORIGINS`/`TRUSTED_HOSTS`,\n   `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true`, `SAFAR_SEED=false`.\n3. Run the database as the non-owner `safar_app` role and apply\n   `d9e4f1b2c305`; verify `SELECT count(*) FROM trips` is 0 with no context.\n4. Schedule the retention job and backups; test a restore into a clean\n   database.\n5. Put rate limiting at the gateway if more than one API instance runs.\n6. Attach an error monitor and log sink.\n7. Commission an external penetration test and a small load test before\n   opening registration.\n\nUntil those are done, the correct claim is “hardened and verified on this\nenvironment”, not “production ready”.\n\n---\n\n## Appendix A — security regression tests\n\n`services/api/tests/test_security_hardening.py` (19 tests; all pass on SQLite\nand PostgreSQL):\n\n| Test | Proves |\n|---|---|\n| `test_responses_carry_security_headers_and_request_id` | nosniff, frame denial, no-referrer, CSP, COOP, `no-store`, 32-char request id, valid echo, invalid replacement |\n| `test_health_and_ready_do_not_leak_internals` | health/ready bodies contain no secrets or internals |\n| `test_unknown_host_header_is_rejected` | TrustedHost returns 400 for `evil.example.com` |\n| `test_oversized_body_is_rejected_before_validation` | 413 for a body over the cap, with request id |\n| `test_anonymous_requests_reach_only_public_endpoints` | private endpoints 401; ## 1. Vulnerabilities identified

13 findings, all remediated: **2 high** (tokens in `localStorage` with no server-side revocation; no database tenant isolation), **7 medium** (trusted upload content-types, no body-size cap, token paths in logs, health internals, no CSRF under cookies, `/nearby` accepting coordinates without location consent, deletion retaining personal data), **4 low** (no retention, missing headers/host/docs guards, non-canonical seeded consent, no per-route rate budgets).

No SQL injection, IDOR, mass-assignment or error-leakage defects were found — verified by targeted tests rather than assumed.

## 2. Fixes implemented

HttpOnly cookie sessions with opaque refresh tokens, rotation and reuse detection; RLS backstop; CSRF double-submit; magic-byte upload sniffing; 25 MB body ceiling; JSON logging with redacted token paths and hashed IPs; security headers/TrustedHost/HSTS; trimmed `/api/health` plus a real `/api/ready`; expanded erasure; retention job; per-bucket rate limits with `Retry-After`; production startup guards for `SECRET_KEY`, CORS, cookies, docs and seeding.

## 3. RLS coverage

55 tables, **220 policies**, 35 `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers, `ENABLE` + `FORCE RLS` on every domain table, fail-closed without context. Direct PG probes as the non-owner `safar_app`: 0 visible trips with no context, mira 6, jonas 3, foreign trip/expenses/members 0, system 9, audit logs 0 without admin and 85 with `app.admin`; a spoofed insert was rejected with `new row violates row-level security policy`. Column-level privacy remains serializer-enforced because RLS is row-level.

## 4. Auth changes

`safar_access` (HttpOnly, 15 min), `safar_refresh` (HttpOnly, 30 days, `/api/auth`, rotated), readable `safar_csrf` + `X-CSRF-Token`; session state checked on every request; logout revokes; WS uses a 2-minute session-bound ticket. Browser evidence: login → dashboard → Kyoto itinerary; `document.cookie` contained only `safar_csrf`; sign-out redirected to `/login?next=…`, cleared cookies, and `/api/auth/me` + `/api/auth/refresh` both returned 401.

## 5. PostgreSQL verification

Four migrations applied cleanly to a fresh PG 16.4 database (56 relations, 220 policies, 220 grants). Full backend suite: **68 passed on PostgreSQL under FORCE RLS (18.59 s)** and **68 passed on SQLite (19.71 s)**; the 19 new security tests were also re-run just now (19 passed). SQLite-only assumptions are listed explicitly: it cannot prove RLS, and `create_all` vs Alembic remains a divergence risk.

## 6. Backup / recovery

`pg_dump -Fc` (358,169 bytes) → `pg_restore` into a clean database reproduced identical tables, policies, FORCE-RLS flags, row counts (users 20 / trips 7 / memories 9), and RLS behaviour (0 unauthenticated, 6 for mira). Media lives on a Docker volume and is excluded from the DB dump; no PITR is configured.

## 7. Remaining risks

Docker images were **not built** (Docker CLI unavailable); TLS/proxy path untested; no external pentest or load test; rate limiting is single-process; WS token travels in the query string (2-minute ticket, requires WSS and proxy log redaction); no WAL/PITR; prepared PG test mode needs a fresh database; monitoring is an integration point only; seeded demo credentials must remain disabled in production.

## 8. Production readiness assessment

**Hardened and PostgreSQL-verified, not production-certified.** Core auth, authorization, RLS, privacy and recovery controls are implemented and tested on both engines. Docker/TLS/CI execution, external review, PITR and load testing remain outstanding; the seven launch conditions are in [SECURITY.md §8](file:///C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/docs/SECURITY.md#L304).

# SAFAR — Phase 6: Premium Product UI/UX Transformation

SAFAR has completed its functional validation, feature refinement and major security hardening.

Your task is to transform the existing application into a premium, polished, production-quality travel platform.

This is a UI/UX improvement phase.

IMPORTANT:
- Do not rebuild the application.
- Do not remove existing functionality.
- Do not break backend integrations.
- Do not replace functional components with static mockups.
- Preserve all existing API contracts and business logic.
- Make every visible button and interaction functional.

## 1. First, audit the existing interface

Inspect every route, page, component, modal, navigation element and responsive layout.

Identify:
- Inconsistent spacing.
- Poor typography.
- Cluttered layouts.
- Weak visual hierarchy.
- Inconsistent components.
- Poor empty states.
- Unclear navigation.
- Broken mobile layouts.
- Unnecessary visual complexity.

Create a UI improvement plan before implementing changes.

## 2. Establish a unified design system

Create a consistent design system for SAFAR.

Define:
- Colour palette.
- Typography scale.
- Spacing system.
- Border radius.
- Shadows.
- Buttons.
- Form controls.
- Cards.
- Navigation.
- Modals.
- Dropdowns.
- Toast notifications.
- Loading states.
- Empty states.

The interface should feel cohesive across every feature.

## 3. Overall visual direction

Target:
- Premium travel-tech aesthetic.
- Modern and minimal.
- Clean layouts with generous spacing.
- Elegant typography.
- Subtle glass effects where appropriate.
- Smooth micro-interactions.
- Refined transitions.
- Beautiful cards and information layouts.
- High-quality destination imagery where relevant.

Avoid:
- Excessive gradients.
- Excessive glassmorphism.
- Overloaded dashboards.
- Huge unnecessary headings.
- Too many colours.
- Unnecessary animations.
- Generic AI-dashboard styling.

The result should feel like a carefully designed commercial product.

## 4. Improve the core application experience

Prioritise:

### Dashboard
- Clear trip overview.
- Upcoming journeys.
- Recent activity.
- Personalised discovery.
- Useful next actions.

### Discovery
- Attractive destination cards.
- Better filters.
- Clear source and confidence labels.
- Better search experience.

### Trip planning
- Beautiful itinerary timeline.
- Clear day-by-day organisation.
- Better activity cards.
- Easy editing.
- Clear group voting.
- Visible protected-time blocks.

### Group Experience Engine
- Make Everyone Wins, Your Turn and Surprise Us easy to understand.

- Make recommendations explainable.

### Memories
- Visual memory timeline.
- Better image presentation.
- Attractive Journey Replay.
- Clear privacy controls.

### Other features
Polish the remaining features while maintaining their existing functionality.

## 5. Responsive design

Verify the application on:
- Desktop.
- Laptop.
- Tablet.
- Mobile.

Every page must remain usable at different screen sizes.

## 6. Accessibility

Improve:
- Keyboard navigation.
- Focus indicators.
- Colour contrast.
- Semantic HTML.
- Form labels.
- Screen-reader announcements.
- Reduced-motion support.

Run automated accessibility checks where possible.

## 7. Interaction quality

Add thoughtful:
- Hover states.
- Loading skeletons.
- Success feedback.
- Error feedback.
- Modal transitions.
- Page transitions where appropriate.
- Clear disabled states.

Do not sacrifice usability for animation.

## 8. Testing

After implementation:
- Run frontend tests.
- Run TypeScript checks.
- Run production build.
- Check every route.
- Test all important interactions.
- Verify mobile responsiveness.
- Check browser console errors.
- Ensure existing backend workflows still function.

## 9. Deliverables

1. Design system created.
2. Pages redesigned.
3. Components improved.
4. Responsive testing results.
5. Accessibility findings.
6. Screenshots of major pages.
7. Remaining UI issues.

The goal is to make SAFAR feel like a premium, polished, commercially credible travel platform while preserving every working feature.

371	export function Modal({
372	  open,
373	  onClose,
374	  title,
375	  children,
376	  wide,
377	}: {
378	  open: boolean;
379	  onClose: () => void;
380	  title: string;
381	  children: ReactNode;
382	  wide?: boolean;
383	}) {
384	  useEffect(() => {
385	    if (!open) return;
386	    const handler = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
387	      if (event.key === "Escape") onClose();
388	    };
389	    window.addEventListener("keydown", handler);
390	    document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
391	    return () => {
392	      window.removeEventListener("keydown", handler);
393	      document.body.style.overflow = "";
394	    };
395	  }, [open, onClose]);
396	
397	  return (
398	    <AnimatePresence>
399	      {open ? (
400	        <motion.div
401	          className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-end justify-center bg-ink/40 p-0 backdrop-blur-sm sm:items-center sm:p-6"
402	          initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
403	          animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
404	          exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
405	          onClick={onClose}
406	        >
407	          <motion.div
408	            role="dialog"
409	            aria-modal="true"
410	            aria-label={title}
411	            initial={{ y: 40, opacity: 0 }}
412	            animate={{ y: 0, opacity: 1 }}
413	            exit={{ y: 24, opacity: 0 }}
414	            transition={{ duration: 0.28, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
415	            className={cn(
416	              "max-h-[92vh] w-full overflow-y-auto rounded-t-3xl border border-line bg-paper p-5 shadow-lift sm:rounded-3xl sm:p-6",
417	              wide ? "sm:max-w-2xl" : "sm:max-w-lg",
418	            )}
419	            onClick={(event) => event.stopPropagation()}
420	          >
421	            <div className="mb-4 flex items-start justify-between gap-4">
422	              <h2 className="text-xl">{title}</h2>
423	              <button
424	                type="button"
425	                onClick={onClose}
426	                className="rounded-full p-1.5 text-muted hover:bg-ink/5"
427	                aria-label="Close"
428	              >
429	                <X size={18} />
430	              </button>
431	            </div>
432	            {children}
433	          </motion.div>
434	        </motion.div>
435	      ) : null}
436	    </AnimatePresence>
437	  );
438	}

#### Thinking

The existing UI is already quite refined. Phase 6 needs visible premium transformation. We should avoid a rebuild but can significantly upgrade:

1. Design tokens: richer palette (deep pine/ink, sand, terracotta), refined type scale, spacing, radius, shadows. Add semantic tokens: `--gold`? "Too many colours" caution. Keep core palette: ink/paper/surface/ember/jade/rose + add "sand"/"sea"? The existing is warm editorial. Premium travel-tech: warm ivory + deep ink + burnt ember + deep teal. We can refine existing rather than add many colors. Add depth: gradient overlays, subtle grain, glass header.

2. Components:
- Button: unify heights, add icon spacing, focus-visible ring, hover lift, active press, loading state, disabled.
- Card: add variants (plain/elevated/interactive), no entrance animation per card (currently every Card animates — heavy and repeated; causes jank). Replace motion.div with div and hover interactions.
- Badge with dot option.
- Inputs with icon support? Can add `Input` wrapper? Keep simple.
- Add new primitives: `SegmentedControl`, `Tooltip`? Maybe not needed. Add `SectionCard`, `ListRow`, `Metric`, `Timeline`, `PageToolbar`, `FilterChip`, `Sheet`.
- Modal: focus trap, aria-labelledby, body scroll lock, close on backdrop, reduced motion. Add mobile bottom sheet.
- Toasts: icons, progress, dismiss.
- Skeleton: shimmer with reduced-motion.
- EmptyState: better illustration/icon treatment.
- Dropdown: currently none as a shared component; menus are inline. Add maybe not necessary.
- Navigation: AppShell sidebar active indicator, collapsible? Add command bar/search? Don't add features. Improve nav sections ("Plan", "Connect", "Account"), sticky top bar with breadcrumb? AppShell only.
- TripShell: sticky subnav with frosted background, active underline, hero header with destination image? No imagery data? Destinations have no image_url likely. Let's check types. Could use curated gradient covers based on destination name. "High-quality destination imagery where relevant" — we can add real images from Unsplash? Can't use external network in production? We could use remote images via `next/image` with images.unsplash.com; but that introduces external dependency and could fail offline. The prompt explicitly asks for high-quality destination imagery. We can search web for images and download to `public/images/destinations/`. Need licensing: Unsplash images are free to use. Use ImageSearch to find Kyoto, Lisbon, Reykjavik? The seeded destinations—let's inspect seed destinations.

44	function eachDay(start: string, end: string) {
45	  const days: string[] = [];
46	  const cursor = new Date(`${start.slice(0, 10)}T12:00:00`);
47	  const last = new Date(`${end.slice(0, 10)}T12:00:00`);
48	  while (cursor <= last && days.length < 60) {
49	    days.push(cursor.toISOString().slice(0, 10));
50	    cursor.setDate(cursor.getDate() + 1);
51	  }
52	  return days;
53	}

243	                  : "border-line bg-surface text-muted hover:border-ink/30 hover:text-ink",
244	              )}
245	            >
246	              <CloudOff size={14} /> {saveOffline ? "Will save offline" : "Save for offline sync"}
247	            </button>
248	          </div>
249	        </div>
250	
251	        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-2">
252	          <p className="text-[12px] leading-5 text-faint">
253	            {visibility === "private" ? (
254	              <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-ember">
255	                <Lock size={11} /> Private — only you until you grant access.
256	              </span>
257	            ) : (
258	              <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1">
259	                <Users size={11} /> Shared with active trip members.
260	              </span>
261	            )}
262	          </p>
263	          <Button
264	            onClick={handleSubmit}
265	            loading={createMemory.isPending || uploading}
266	            disabled={!text && !media}
267	          >
268	            <NotebookPen size={14} /> Save memory
269	          </Button>
270	        </div>
271	      </Card>
272	
273	      {offline.queue.filter((item) => item.trip_id === tripId).length ? (
274	        <FlowNote icon={<CloudOff size={14} />}>
275	          {offline.queue.filter((item) => item.trip_id === tripId).length} memory(ies) waiting to sync.{" "}
276	          <Link href={`/trips/${tripId}/offline`} className="text-ember hover:underline">
277	            Open offline queue →
278	          </Link>
279	        </FlowNote>
280	      ) : null}
281	
282	      {data.days.length === 0 ? (
283	        <EmptyState

285	          description="Capture the first moment. Photos, notes and voice stay private until you share them."
286	          icon={<NotebookPen size={24} />}

294	                <span className="h-px flex-1 bg-line" />

302	                    isMine={memory.user_id === user?.id}

304	                  />
305	                ))}
306	              </div>
307	            </div>
308	          ))}
309	        </div>
310	      )}
311

320	function memoryIcon(kind: string) {
321	  if (kind === "photo") return <ImageIcon size={13} />;
322	  if (kind === "voice") return <Mic size={13} />;
323	  if (kind === "video") return <PlayCircle size={13} />;
324	  return <NotebookPen size={13} />;
325	}
326	
327	function MemoryCard({
328	  memory,
329	  isMine,
330	  onDelete,
331	}: {
332	  memory: Memory;
333	  isMine: boolean;
334	  onDelete: () => void;
335	}) {
336	  const mediaUrl =
337	    memory.media_url && memory.media_url.startsWith("/media/") ? `${API_URL}${memory.media_url}` : memory.media_url;
338	  const isImage = memory.media_type?.startsWith("image/") && mediaUrl;
339	
340	  return (
341	    <div className="overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-line bg-surface">
342	      {isImage ? (
343	        // eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element
344	        <img src={mediaUrl} alt={memory.caption || "Trip memory"} className="h-44 w-full object-cover" />
345	      ) : mediaUrl ? (
346	        <div className="flex items-center gap-2 border-b border-line bg-raised px-3 py-2 text-[12px] text-muted">
347	          {memoryIcon(memory.kind)} {memory.media_type || "Attachment"}
348	        </div>
349	      ) : null}
350	      <div className="space-y-2 p-3.5">
351	        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5">
352	          <Badge tone="outline">{titleCase(memory.kind)}</Badge>
353	          {memory.visibility === "private" ? (
354	            <Badge tone="ember">
355	              <Lock size={10} /> Private
356	            </Badge>
357	          ) : (
358	            <Badge tone="jade">
359	              <Users size={10} /> Trip
360	            </Badge>
361	          )}
362	          {memory.ai_generated ? <Badge tone="neutral">AI captioned</Badge> : null}
363	        </div>
364	        {memory.text_content ? (
365	          <p className="whitespace-pre-line text-[13px] leading-6 text-ink">{memory.text_content}</p>
366	        ) : null}
367	        {memory.caption ? (
368	          <p className="rounded-lg bg-raised/60 px-2.5 py-1.5 text-[12px] italic leading-5 text-muted">
369	            {memory.caption}
370	          </p>
371	        ) : null}
372	        <p className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-3 gap-y-1 text-[10.5px] text-faint">
373	          <span>{memory.author?.display_name || "Traveller"}</span>
374	          <span>{formatDateTime(memory.captured_at)}</span>
375	          {memory.lat !== null && memory.lon !== null ? (
376	            <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-0.5">
377	              <MapPin size={10} /> pinned
378	            </span>
379	          ) : null}
380	        </p>
381	        {isMine ? (
382	          <div className="flex justify-end border-t border-line pt-2">
383	            <button
384	              type="button"
385	              onClick={onDelete}
386	              className="inline-flex items-center gap-1 text-[12px] text-rose hover:underline"
387	            >
388	              <Trash2 size={11} /> Remove
389	            </button>
390	          </div>
391	        ) : null}
392	      </div>
393	    </div>
394	  );
395	}

## Top 8 cross-page inconsistencies

1. **No trip page uses `PageHeader`.** `ui.tsx:252-275` renders `h1 text-3xl sm:text-4xl` and is used by dashboard/profile/settings/discover; all 15 trip pages hand-roll `<p className="eyebrow">` + `<h2 className="text-2xl">` (e.g. `R/voting/page.tsx:170-171`). Result: trip pages sit visually one level below the rest of the app, and `R/page.tsx` has no page heading at all.
2. **Heading hierarchy collides.** `TripShell.tsx:85` owns the `h1`; pages emit `h2`; `SectionTitle` (`ui.tsx:289`) also emits `h2`, so cards' section titles become siblings of the page title (`R/expenses/page.tsx:208`, `R/insights/page.tsx:176`).
3. **Vertical rhythm is arbitrary** — `space-y-8` (`R/page.tsx:85`) vs `space-y-5` (`R/expenses/page.tsx:171`, `R/members/page.tsx:158`) vs `space-y-6` (`R/pulse/page.tsx:115`, `R/twin/page.tsx:116`).
4. **Create-in-modal vs create-inline-card split.** Modal: voting `:369`, studio `:309`, expenses `:315`, members `:302`. Inline Card: tasks `:118-150`. Should be one pattern.
5. **Sub-12px type is systemic**, worst in tabular data: `text-[10px]` vote labels (`R/voting/page.tsx:254`), `text-[10.5px]` (`R/expenses/page.tsx:280`, `R/members/page.tsx:271`, `R/memories/replay/page.tsx:184`, `R/tasks/page.tsx:237`, `R/insights/page.tsx:368`).
6. **Unlabeled form controls** — no `<Field>`/`aria-label` on: studio caption textarea (`R/memories/studio/page.tsx:353`), pact textareas (`R/pact/page.tsx:118,131,211`), expense participant inputs (`R/expenses/page.tsx:399,415`), member role select (`R/members/page.tsx:228`).
7. **Icon-only buttons without accessible names** — `R/tasks/page.tsx:230` (task toggle), `R/members/page.tsx:283-285` (revoke), `R/members/page.tsx:343` (copy). Contrast `R/expenses/page.tsx:294` and `R/pact/page.tsx:176` which do it right.
8. **Empty/error handling is uneven** — `EmptyState` used in some places, raw `<p className="text-sm text-muted">` in others (`R/expenses/page.tsx:230,256`, `R/tasks/page.tsx:179`, `R/insights/page.tsx:377`), ad-hoc dashed box in `R/map/page.tsx:167`, and none at all in `R/rescue/page.tsx` / `R/twin/page.tsx`. Also: `R/insights/page.tsx:102-118` bypasses `lib/hooks`, breaking the data-layer convention the other 14 pages follow.

474	function ProposalImpact({ tripId, proposalId }: { tripId: string; proposalId: string }) {
475	  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
476	  const detail = useQuery({
477	    queryKey: ["proposal-detail", tripId, proposalId],
478	    queryFn: () =>
479	      api<Proposal & {
480	        impact?: {
481	          cost_impact?: { total_delta: number; per_member_estimate: number; currency: string };
482	          budget_conflicts?: { reason: string; item: string }[];
483	          pact_conflicts?: { item: string; rule: string; resolution: string }[];
484	          schedule_conflicts?: {
485	            item: string;
486	            proposed?: string;
487	            reason: string;
488	            protected: boolean;
489	          }[];
490	        };
491	      }>(`/api/trips/${tripId}/proposals/${proposalId}`),
492	    enabled: open,
493	  });
494	
495	  return (
496	    <div className="border-t border-line pt-3">
497	      <button
498	        onClick={() => setOpen((value) => !value)}
499	        className="flex w-full items-center justify-between text-[12px] text-muted hover:text-ink"
500	      >
501	        <span>Impact if approved</span>
502	        <ChevronDown
503	          size={14}
504	          className={cn("transition-transform", open ? "rotate-180" : "")}
505	        />
506	      </button>
507	      {open ? (
508	        detail.isLoading ? (
509	          <p className="mt-2 text-[12px] text-faint">Calculating…</p>
510	        ) : detail.error ? (
511	          <p className="mt-2 text-[12px] text-rose">{(detail.error as Error).message}</p>
512	        ) : detail.data?.impact ? (
513	          <div className="mt-2 space-y-2 rounded-xl bg-raised/60 p-3 text-[12px] text-muted">
514	            {detail.data.impact.cost_impact ? (
515	              <p>
516	                Cost change:{" "}
517	                <span className="font-mono text-ink">
518	                  {formatMoney(
519	                    detail.data.impact.cost_impact.total_delta,
520	                    detail.data.impact.cost_impact.currency,
521	                  )}
522	                </span>{" "}
523	                total · {formatMoney(detail.data.impact.cost_impact.per_member_estimate, detail.data.impact.cost_impact.currency)} per member (estimate)
524	              </p>
525	            ) : null}
526	            {(detail.data.impact.pact_conflicts || []).map((conflict, index) => (
527	              <p key={`pact-${index}`} className="text-rose">
528	                Pact conflict: {conflict.item} — {conflict.resolution}
529	              </p>
530	            ))}
531	            {(detail.data.impact.budget_conflicts || []).map((conflict, index) => (
532	              <p key={`budget-${index}`} className="text-rose">
533	                Budget: {conflict.item} — {conflict.reason}
534	              </p>
535	            ))}
536	            {(detail.data.impact.schedule_conflicts || []).map((conflict, index) => (
537	              <p key={`schedule-${index}`} className="text-rose">
538	                {conflict.protected ? "Protected time" : "Schedule"}: {conflict.item}
539	                {conflict.proposed ? ` vs ${conflict.proposed}` : ""} — {conflict.reason}
540	              </p>
541	            ))}
542	            {!detail.data.impact.cost_impact ? (
543	              <p>No cost impact recorded for this proposal.</p>
544	            ) : null}
545	          </div>
546	        ) : (
547	          <p className="mt-2 text-[12px] text-faint">No impact data returned.</p>
548	        )
549	      ) : null}
550	    </div>
551	  );
552	}

412	                      />
413	                    ) : null}
414	                    {split === "custom" && entry.included ? (

422	                            current.map((item, itemIndex) =>
423	                              itemIndex === index ? { ...item, share: event.target.value } : item,
424	                            ),
425	                          )
426	                        }
427	                        className="h-8 w-24"
428	                        placeholder="0.00"
429	                      />
430	                    ) : null}
431	                  </div>
432	                );
433	              })}
434	            </div>
435	            {split === "custom" ? (
436	              <p
437	                className={cn(
438	                  "text-[12px]",
439	                  Math.abs(customTotal - Number(amount || 0)) > 0.01 ? "text-rose" : "text-jade",
440	                )}
441	              >
442	                Custom shares total {formatMoney(customTotal, currency)} of {formatMoney(Number(amount || 0), currency)}
443	              </p>
444	            ) : null}
445	          </div>
446	
447	          <Field label="Notes" hint="Optional">
448	            <Textarea value={notes} onChange={(event) => setNotes(event.target.value)} />
449	          </Field>
450	
451	          <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
452	            <Button type="button" variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>
453	              Cancel
454	            </Button>
455	            <Button type="submit" loading={createExpense.isPending} disabled={!title || !amount}>
456	              <Receipt size={14} /> Add expense
457	            </Button>
458	          </div>
459	        </form>
460	      </Modal>
461	    </div>
462	  );
463	}

46	            ? { ...turn, answer }

51	    onError: (error, question) => {

67	    setMessage("");
68	    ask.mutate(trimmed);
69	  }

145	                      {report.target_id ? (

148	                    </div>

160	                      placeholder="Optional note for the account holder (warnings only)"
161	                      value={notes[report.id] || ""}
162	                      onChange={(event) =>

164	                      }
165	                    />
166	                    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
167	                      <Button
168	                        size="sm"
169	                        variant="danger"
170	                        loading={decide.isPending}
171	                        onClick={() => decide.mutate({ id: report.id, decision: "hide_content" })}
172	                        disabled={!report.target_id || !["post", "memory"].includes(report.target_type)}
173	                      >
174	                        Hide content
175	                      </Button>
176	                      <Button
177	                        size="sm"
178	                        variant="secondary"
179	                        loading={decide.isPending}
180	                        onClick={() => decide.mutate({ id: report.id, decision: "warn" })}
181	                      >
182	                        Warn account
183	                      </Button>
184	                      <Button
185	                        size="sm"
186	                        variant="ghost"
187	                        loading={decide.isPending}
188	                        onClick={() => decide.mutate({ id: report.id, decision: "dismiss" })}
189	                      >
190	                        Dismiss
191	                      </Button>
192	                    </div>
193	                  </div>
194	                ) : null}
195	              </Card>
196	            ))}
197	          </div>
198	        )}
199	      </section>
200	
201	      <FlowNote>
202	        Place reports can be verified from the place detail screen by an admin. Verification raises
203	        confidence, but community observations stay labelled as reported until a source supports them.
204	      </FlowNote>
205	    </div>
206	  );
207	}

Key facts:
- No trip page uses PageHeader (ui.tsx:252, which renders h1 text-3xl/4xl). All 15 use custom `<p className="eyebrow">` + `<h2 className="text-2xl">`. TripShell renders h1 at line 85. So each page's h2 is actually a sub-heading under the trip name — semantically defensible but visually inconsistent with rest of app (dashboard, profile etc use PageHeader h1 3xl). Note also overview page has no page heading at all.

Also SectionTitle renders h2 (ui.tsx:289) — nested under pages' h2 → h2 siblings at wrong level. Heading hierarchy issue: pages' custom h2 then SectionTitle h2 → duplicate/sibling levels, plus Cards with h3 text-lg. In overview, no page heading, cards h3.

Let me list per page concisely.

1. Overview (page.tsx): hooks useTrip, useItinerary, useMembers, useProposals(open), usePact, useTripActivity, useAuth. No mutation. Heading: none at page level — starts with next-action Card (h2). Inconsistent eyebrow in card. Layout: space-y-8 (only page using 8; others 5/6), grids collapse ok. Risks: Stat hint text long; `w-14` time column fine. A11y: Link "Open itinerary" text-xs; no aria. Live activity assumes items. Static: none obvious. Mock: the tool grid 4 links at line 296-333 duplicates /more; uses "Everything else".

2. Voting: hooks useTrip, useProposals, useSearch, mutations api vote/approve/reject/withdraw/create. Heading custom eyebrow. Layout: page-level space-y-5 vs vote count tiles 3-col with 10px uppercase labels (text-[10px]) — tiny. Modal wide. A11y: voting modal vote buttons are plain buttons without aria-pressed; "You haven't voted" badge. Buttons Approve/Reject no confirm. Responsive: grid-cols-3 fixed at all sizes for vote tally and vote modal (line 240, 333) — cramped on 320px. ProposalImpact toggler is a button with no aria-expanded.

3. Replay: useReplay, openBook mutation, useToasts. Heading custom eyebrow + h2 = trip name (dangerous: heading in TripShell already shows trip name at h1 → duplicate). Stats grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-5 with 5 items → orphan on 2-col. uses Link wrapping Button (nested interactive — a11y). ReplayMemory uses text-[10.5px].

4. Studio: useStudio, mutations suggestEvents/approveEvent/createEvent/requestCaption/applyCaption. Custom eyebrow. Uses Card, SectionTitle (h2) inside Cards. Memory select button is a <button> containing badges — no aria-pressed/checkbox semantics. Modal caption textarea has no Field label (line 353) → unlabeled textarea. Tiny text 10.5px (line 267).

5. Expenses: useTrip, useExpenses, useBalances, useMembers; mutations create/remove; CSV download. Custom eyebrow. Balances & settlements side-by-side lg:grid-cols-2. Expense list is custom cards fine. A11y: participant number inputs in modal without labels (lines 399, 415) — only placeholder; Select "Paid by" etc fine via Field. Delete button has aria-label (good). text-[10.5px] date.

6. Pulse: usePulse + save mutation. Custom eyebrow with date inline. Sliders have aria-label (good) but no visible <label> association. Interest/pref chips are buttons without aria-pressed. Budget comfort 5 buttons no group label role. Page has no per-day selector visible (day only from URL param; eyebrow shows date, no way to change — UX gap). text-[10.5px] chips.

7. Members: useTrip, useMembers, useTripInvitations; mutations invite/revoke/updateRole/removeMember/saveSelf. Custom eyebrow but title is dynamic "{n} traveller(s)". Grid sm:grid-cols-2. Copy button icon only in modal (line 343) no aria-label.

8. Map: useTrip, useItinerary, useNearby. Custom eyebrow. Card p-0 wrapping TripMap height=440 fixed — tall on mobile; no responsive height. Legend below map is duplicated colour+text (ok). Search input in SectionTitle action w-44. Selects w-32/w-36 fixed. No empty state component for nearby (dashed p). Map page doesn't use EmptyState/ErrorState for nearby — inconsistent.

9. More: useTrip only; static array of links (line 45-190) — all static config, but hrefs: /opportunity (singular, matches dir), /watch, /branches... Consistent eyebrow. Grid sm:grid-cols-2, fine. 10. Tasks: useTasks, useTaskSummary, useMembers; create/update. Custom eyebrow. Done list strikethrough. summary hint literally says `counts from the API` (line 98-99) — dev-speak copy.

11. Pact: useTrip, usePact, useMe; save mutation. Custom eyebrow + Badge. Textarea with no Field label (lines 118, 131, 211) — placeholder only. Meeting point inputs unlabeled. SectionTitle h2 inside cards. Save button at bottom far away. FlowNote inside flex row.

12. Twin: useTrip, useItinerary, useSearch; mutations compare/adopt/negotiate. Custom eyebrow. Two <Field> in sm:grid-cols-[auto_1fr_auto] — date input w-40 fixed. Uses Stat inside comparison cards. Fair Trade section: catalog chips duplicated from above search (two pickers). No EmptyState when no comparison. negotiation state not reset.

13. Rescue: useTrip, useItinerary; mutations analyze/propose. Custom eyebrow "Trip Rescue · disruption recovery". 6-button kind grid grid-cols-2 sm:3 lg:6 — ok. Buttons lack aria-pressed. Consequence text. Missing empty state before analysis (just nothing). Fine.

Key decisions for the design system:

1. **Tokens** (globals.css + tailwind.config.ts): keep the warm editorial palette (it's good and distinctive), but refine:
   - Add a deeper ink, better muted contrast (#6B6559 on paper 246 241 231 has contrast ~4.9:1 — okay for body but 12px meta at faint (150 143 128) is ~2.6:1 — fails). Fix: darken `faint` to ~120 113 99 and reserve it only for non-essential decorative text; introduce `muted` for metadata.
   - Actually changing `faint` globally is the single biggest contrast win. Let me compute: paper = #F6F1E7. faint #968F80 → luminance... roughly 0.28 → contrast vs 0.90 ≈ (0.95)/(0.33) ≈ 2.9. Darkening to #7A7365 (122 115 101) → relative lum ~0.18 → contrast ~3.9. Still below 4.5 for small text. For 12px text we need 4.5:1. muted #6B6559 → lum ~0.13 → contrast ≈ 5.1. So the rule should be: metadata uses `muted`, and `faint` only for ≥ decorative. Better: raise the floor — replace `text-[10px]/[10.5px]` with `text-[11.5px]`/`text-xs` and `text-faint` with `text-muted` in metadata. That's a big sweep.

## Audit findings → UI improvement plan

The audit covered all 52 routes. The app already has a coherent warm-editorial identity, but it is applied unevenly. Concrete findings:

| Area | Finding |
|---|---|
| Headings | 5 different page-title patterns; all 15 trip pages hand-roll `eyebrow + h2` while dashboard/settings use `PageHeader`. Trip overview has no page heading. |
| Rhythm | `space-y-5`, `-6`, `-8` across sibling pages; content width jumps between `max-w-xl`, `3xl`, `wide`. |
| Type | sub-12px text is systemic (`10px` vote tallies, `10.5px` dates/IDs); `faint` on 12px fails contrast. |
| Motion | every `Card` re-animates on mount — the strongest "AI dashboard" tell. |
| Discovery | no search/filter UI at all; covers are CSS gradients; no imagery anywhere in the product. |
| Create flows | modal on 4 pages, always-open inline card on Tasks. |
| States | `EmptyState`/`ErrorState` present but skipped on ~10 pages; `circles` has no error state; `trips/new` uses a blank fallback. |
| A11y | icon-only buttons without names (`tasks`, `members`), unlabeled textareas/selects (`studio`, `pact`, `expenses`), tabs/chips with no `aria-pressed`, no modal focus trap, no focus return. |
| Loading | shared `isPending` bound to several buttons at once (admin, connections). |

**Plan**

1. **Design system** — refine tokens (deeper `ember`, AA-safe `muted`/`faint`, softer shadows, tabular numerals, 12px metadata floor); rebuild `Card`, `Modal` (focus trap + return + labelled), `PageHeader` (h1/h2 sizes), add `SegmentedControl`, `MetaRow`, `AvatarStack`; remove mount animation.
2. **Imagery** — editorial destination photography (generated, labelled as editorial on the detail page), mapped via `lib/imagery.ts` with a deterministic fallback and `next/image`.
3. **Shells** — sidebar grouping + active rail + user card; mobile bottom nav with 44px targets and safe-area; sticky TripShell tab rail with scroll affordance.
4. **Core screens** — dashboard (activity feed, discovery strip), discover (search/filters/sort, photo cards), itinerary (time-rail timeline, jade protected blocks, sticky day strip), engine (clearer modes/comparison), memories (photo grid, privacy clarity), voting, trip overview.
5. **Sweep** — typography/metadata floor, empty/error coverage, labels, `aria-pressed`/`aria-label`, scoped pending states across remaining routes.
6. **Verify** — vitest, `tsc`, `next build`, browser pass at 1440/1024/768/390 with screenshots, console checks, interaction tests.
7. **Document** — `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` + AUDIT/FEATURE_REGISTRY updates.

Starting with imagery generation and design tokens.
