#### Thinking

Now write the app infrastructure. Need bottom nav shell. Which tabs? Dashboard, Discover, Trips, Assistant, Profile. Dashboard currently uses `context.go('/profile')`, `/notifications` etc. `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack` with branches:
- /dashboard -> DashboardScreen
- /discover -> DiscoverScreen
- /trips -> TripListScreen (but `/trips/new` is a sub-route? In shell branch for trips, route `/trips` with child `/trips/new`? `context.push('/trips/new')` from anywhere; it's better top-level route `/trips/new`. But with StatefulShellRoute, route `/trips` branch and top-level `/trips/new` conflict? `/trips/new` would match shell branch route `/trips` only if sub-route defined. If we define top-level `/trips/new`, GoRouter picks first matching route order. Let me define shell branch trips route path 'trips' with sub-route 'new'? However shell branch routes render inside shell (bottom nav visible) — acceptable. But TripCreateScreen pushes via `context.go('/trips/${trip.id}')`; top-level trip detail route exists. Fine.

Actually simpler: shell branches:
- `/dashboard`
- `/discover`
- `/trips` with child route `new`? If TripCreateScreen is within shell, bottom nav remains visible; fine but maybe not desired. The spec says trip creation screen; keeping shell is okay. But trip detail top-level full-screen (no bottom nav) for immersive. I'll put `/trips/new` top-level (outside shell) so it's full-screen, declared before shell? GoRouter route matching is positional; if shell branch defines `/trips` and top-level `/trips/new` declared after shell, request `/trips/new` would match `/trips` branch if it has no child "new" -> no match; GoRouter matches full path, so `/trips` route won't match `/trips/new` unless `path` with subroutes. StatefulShellBranch route `/trips` without children will not match `/trips/new`. Then top-level `/trips/new` matches. Good, no conflict.

- `/assistant` -> AssistantScreen (need to create)
- `/profile` -> ProfileScreen (need to create)

Profile tab includes Journey DNA link, Settings, notifications, privacy, logout.

Other top-level routes:
- `/splash`, `/welcome`, `/login`, `/register`
- `/trips/new` (TripCreateScreen)
- `/trips/:tripId` (TripOverviewScreen)
- `/trips/:tripId/itinerary|engine|proposals|expenses|pulse|rescue|memories|studio|replay|import|assistant`
- `/trips/:tripId/places/:activityId`
- `/destinations/:destinationId`
- `/notifications`
- `/journey-dna`
- `/settings`
- maybe `/circles` etc. Not required.

Auth redirect:
- if onboardingSeen == null or auth.status == unknown with no error → splash.
- if error at unknown → splash shows retry (already).
- if onboarding false → `/welcome`
- if signedOut and not on welcome/login/register → `/login`? Welcome is onboarding; after complete, route redirect to `/login`. If signedOut and on `/welcome` stay.

@router.post("/{trip_id}/rescue/propose", status_code=201)
async def rescue_propose(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: RescueProposeIn,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    if not payload.items:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="Select at least one replacement from the rescue analysis.",
        )
    items = []
    for entry in payload.items:
        _within_trip(trip, entry.day)
        item = db.get(ItineraryItem, entry.item_id)
        if not item or item.trip_id != trip.id or item.status != "confirmed":
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="A rescue target item was not found")
        if item.is_protected:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=409,
                detail=f"\"{item.title}\" is protected time and cannot be replaced by Trip Rescue.",
            )
        activity = _activity_in_trip(db, trip, entry.activity_id)
        start = parse_hhmm(entry.start_time)
        if start is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="start_time must use HH:MM")
        day_items = (
            db.query(ItineraryItem)
            .filter(
                ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id,
                ItineraryItem.day == entry.day,
                ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed",
            )
            .all()
        )
        conflict = find_conflict(
            db,
            day_items,
            start_minutes=start,
            duration_minutes=activity.duration_minutes or 90,
            ignore_item_ids={item.id},
        )
        if conflict:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=409,
                detail={
                    "message": (
                        f"The replacement would overlap protected time ({conflict['title']})."
                        if conflict["protected"]
                        else f"The replacement would overlap {conflict['title']}."
                    ),
                    "conflict": conflict,
                },
            )
        items.append(
            {
                "item_id": item.id,
                "activity_id": activity.id,
                "day": entry.day.isoformat(),
                "start_time": entry.start_time,
                "notes": f"Trip Rescue ({payload.kind}) replacement",
                "title": item.title,
            }
        )
    title = f"Trip Rescue: {payload.kind.replace('_', ' ').title()}"
    summary = (
        payload.note
        or "Replaces affected activities after a disruption. Shown as changes only; nothing is applied until approved."
    )
    pact = db.query(JourneyPact).filter(JourneyPact.trip_id == trip.id).first()
    proposal, impact = _create_proposal(
        db,
        trip,
        user,
        kind="rescue",
        title=title,
        summary=summary,
        day=payload.items[0].day,
        payload={
            "kind": payload.kind,
            "extra_minutes": payload.extra_minutes,
            "note": payload.note,
            "items": items,
        },
    )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id,
        event_payload("proposal.created", trip_id=trip.id, proposal_id=proposal.id),
    )
    response = {**proposal_out(db, proposal, user.id), "impact": impact}
    if pact:
        response["pact"] = {
            "must_do": pact.must_do or [],
            "flexible": pact.flexible or [],
            "note": "Pact conflicts block approval until the group adds an exception.",
        }
    return response


@router.post("/{trip_id}/negotiate")
def negotiate(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: NegotiateIn,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    for activity_id in set(payload.option_a + payload.option_b):
        _activity_in_trip(db, trip, activity_id)
    if payload.for_date:
        _within_trip(trip, payload.for_date)
    return rescue_service.compromise(
        db,
        trip,
        _active_members(db, trip.id),
        payload.option_a,
        payload.option_b,
        for_date=payload.for_date,
    )

"""Trip Rescue (F09) and Fair Trade negotiation (F45).

Rescue only produces a proposal. Nothing is applied until the group approves.
"""

from datetime import date

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import (
    Activity,
    ItineraryItem,
    JourneyPact,
    Place,
    Shadowplan,
    Trip,
    TripMember,
)
from app.services.common import normalize_tag
from app.services.engine import generate_recommendations
from app.services.geo import haversine_km, travel_minutes
from app.services.schedule import DAY_END_MINUTES, item_window, parse_hhmm

KIND_LABELS = {
    "rain": "Rain or bad weather",
    "closure": "Unexpected closure",
    "traffic": "Traffic delay",
    "fatigue": "Fatigue or low energy",
    "budget": "Budget change",
    "time": "Time constraint",
}


def _activity_map(db: Session, items: list[ItineraryItem]) -> dict[str, Activity]:
    ids = [item.activity_id for item in items if item.activity_id]
    if not ids:
        return {}
    return {a.id: a for a in db.query(Activity).filter(Activity.id.in_(ids)).all()}


def _place_coords(db: Session, activity: Activity | None) -> tuple[float, float]:
    if not activity or not activity.place_id:
        return (0.0, 0.0)
    place = db.get(Place, activity.place_id)
    return (place.lat, place.lon) if place else (0.0, 0.0)


def _pick_affected(db: Session, items: list[ItineraryItem], kind: str, item_id: str | None) -> list[dict]:
    if item_id:
        target = next((item for item in items if item.id == item_id), None)
        return [{"item": target, "reason": "The group flagged this item."}] if target else []

    if not items:
        return []
    day = sorted({item.day for item in items})[0]
    day_items = [item for item in items if item.day == day and not item.is_protected]
    activities = _activity_map(db, day_items)

    def activity_of(item: ItineraryItem) -> Activity | None:
        return activities.get(item.activity_id) if item.activity_id else None

@router.patch("/me/profile")
def update_profile(
    payload: ProfileUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    profile = db.query(Profile).filter(Profile.user_id == user.id).first()
    if not profile:
        profile = Profile(user_id=user.id)
        db.add(profile)
        db.flush()
    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    for field, value in data.items():
        setattr(profile, field, value)
    if "interests" in data and data["interests"] is not None:
        dna = _get_dna(db, user.id)
        scores = dict(dna.scores or default_dna())
        for interest in data["interests"]:
            key = normalize_tag(interest)
            if key in DNA_DIMENSIONS:
                scores[key] = max(float(scores.get(key, 5)), 7.0)
        dna.scores = scores
        dna.source = "profile+explicit"

@router.put("/me/dna")
def update_dna(
    payload: DNAUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    unknown = set(payload.scores) - set(DNA_DIMENSIONS)
    if unknown:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"Unknown DNA dimensions: {', '.join(sorted(unknown))}")
    dna = _get_dna(db, user.id)
    scores = dict(dna.scores or default_dna())
    for dimension, value in payload.scores.items():
        scores[dimension] = clamp(float(value), 0, 10)
    dna.scores = scores
    dna.source = "explicit"
    audit(db, action="dna.update", entity_type="journey_dna", entity_id=dna.id, user_id=user.id)
    db.commit()
    return {"scores": dna.scores, "source": dna.source, "updated_at": dna.updated_at}

    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    unknown = set(payload.consents) - CONSENT_KINDS
    if unknown:

@router.post("/{trip_id}/memory-events", status_code=201)
def create_event(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: MemoryEventCreate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    start_at = _naive_utc(payload.start_at)
    end_at = _naive_utc(payload.end_at) if payload.end_at else None
    if end_at and end_at < start_at:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="End time must be after the start time")
    memory_ids = []
    for memory_id in payload.memory_ids:
        memory = _memory_for_trip(db, trip, memory_id, user.id)
        memory_ids.append(memory.id)
    event = MemoryEvent(
        trip_id=trip.id,
        title=payload.title,
        summary=payload.summary,
        start_at=start_at,
        end_at=end_at,
        member_ids=[user.id],
        memory_ids=memory_ids,
        status=payload.status,
        created_by=user.id,
    )
    db.add(event)
    audit(
        db,
        action="memory_event.create",
        entity_type="memory_event",
        entity_id=event.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    return {
        "id": event.id,
        "title": event.title,
        "status": event.status,
        "memory_ids": event.memory_ids,
        "note": "Review AI-suggested events before approving them for the travel book.",
    }

def _media_path_for_trip(trip: Trip, media_url: str | None) -> Path | None:
    """Resolve a signed local media URL to a file inside this trip's folder."""
    if not media_url:
        return None
    parts = urlsplit(media_url)
    if parts.scheme or parts.netloc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Media must be a local SAFAR upload")
    prefix = f"/media/{trip.id}/"
    if not parts.path.startswith(prefix):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Media does not belong to this trip")
    filename = parts.path[len(prefix):]
    if not _MEDIA_NAME_PATTERN.match(filename):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Invalid media name")
    query = {key: values[0] for key, values in parse_qs(parts.query).items()}
    if not verify_media_request(parts.path, query):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Media link is missing or expired")
    candidate = (MEDIA_ROOT / trip.id / filename).resolve()
    if MEDIA_ROOT.resolve() not in candidate.parents or not candidate.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Media not found")
    return candidate


@router.post("/trips/{trip_id}/inspirations", status_code=201)
def import_inspiration(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: InspirationIn,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    if payload.trip_id and payload.trip_id != trip.id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Trip mismatch")
    content = (payload.content or "").strip()
    if payload.source_type == "image_url":
        if not content and not payload.media_url:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=422, detail="Attach an image or describe what it shows"
            )
    elif len(content) < 2:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="Inspiration text is too short")
    media_path = _media_path_for_trip(trip, payload.media_url)
    stored_content = content or "Uploaded image"
    inspiration = SavedInspiration(
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        source_type=payload.source_type,
        content=stored_content,
        status="pending",
    )
    db.add(inspiration)
    db.flush()
    extraction = discovery_service.dream_import(
        db, user.id, inspiration, media_path=media_path
    )
    inspiration.status = "extracted"
    audit(
        db,
        action="inspiration.import",
        entity_type="saved_inspiration",
        entity_id=inspiration.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={
            "source_type": payload.source_type,
            "media": bool(media_path),
            "candidates": len(extraction.get("matches", [])),
        },
    )
    db.commit()
    return {
        "id": inspiration.id,
        "source_type": inspiration.source_type,
        "status": inspiration.status,
        "extraction": extraction,
        "disclosure": (
            "Candidates are suggestions only. Confirm them before adding anything to the itinerary."
        ),
    }


@router.post("/trips/{trip_id}/inspirations/{inspiration_id}/review")
def review_inspiration(
    trip_id: str,
    inspiration_id: str,
    payload: InspirationReviewIn,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    row = (
        db.query(SavedInspiration)
        .filter(
            SavedInspiration.id == inspiration_id,
            SavedInspiration.trip_id == trip.id,
            SavedInspiration.user_id == user.id,
        )
        .first()
    )
    if not row:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Inspiration not found")
    extraction = json.loads(json.dumps(row.extracted or {}))
    matches = extraction.get("matches", [])
    target = next(
        (
            match
            for match in matches
            if match.get("candidate_id") == payload.candidate_id
        ),
        None,
    )
    if not target:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Candidate not found")
    target["decision"] = payload.decision
    decisions = extraction.setdefault("decisions", {})
    decisions[payload.candidate_id] = {
        "decision": payload.decision,
        "decided_at": utcnow().isoformat(),
    }
    accepted = sum(1 for match in matches if match.get("decision") == "accept")
    rejected = sum(1 for match in matches if match.get("decision") == "reject")
    pending = len(matches) - accepted - rejected
    extraction["review"] = {
        "pending": pending,
        "accepted": accepted,
        "rejected": rejected,
    }
    if pending == 0:
        row.status = "reviewed" if accepted else "rejected"
    else:
        row.status = "extracted"
    row.extracted = extraction
    audit(
        db,
        action="inspiration.review",
        entity_type="saved_inspiration",
        entity_id=row.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"candidate_id": payload.candidate_id, "decision": payload.decision},
    )
    db.commit()
    return {
        "id": row.id,
        "status": row.status,
        "extraction": extraction,
        "disclosure": (
            "Accepted candidates are still suggestions. Turn an activity into a "
            "proposal so the group can vote before the plan changes."
        ),
    }

24	        : error.response?.data;

/// Formats an ISO timestamp or `HH:MM` value as a 12-hour clock time.
String formatClock(String? raw) {
  if (raw == null || raw.isEmpty) return '';
  final date = DateTime.tryParse(raw);
  if (date != null && raw.contains('T')) return clockLabel(date.toLocal());
  return formatTime(raw);
}
```

Check clockLabel returns DateFormat.Hm() — 24-hour. Hmm, we want consistent style. Use manual: `formatTime` with `${date.hour}:${date.minute}` padded. Let's implement:

```dart
String formatClock(String? raw) {
  if (raw == null || raw.isEmpty) return '';
  final date = raw.contains('T') ? DateTime.tryParse(raw) : null;
  if (date == null) return formatTime(raw);
  final local = date.toLocal();
  return formatTime(
    '${local.hour.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}:'
    '${local.minute.toString().padLeft(2, '0')}',
  );
}
```

#### Thinking

The lint is because `mounted` refers to State, and the analyzer wants `context.mounted` for BuildContext across async gaps. Actually in a StatefulWidget's State, `mounted` is legitimate. The message says "guarded by an unrelated 'mounted' check" — because `showSafarSheet` receives `context` from build param, not `this.context`, so analyzer considers unrelated. Fix by using `if (!context.mounted) return;`. Since this is build's context in a ConsumerState, it's fine.

But note inside the sheet builder it uses `context.texts` from the outer build context inside builder — after await, guarded. Use `context.mounted`.

#### Thinking

On web, Dio's browser adapter uses XHR; withCredentials defaults to false unless `withCredentials: true` is set in BaseOptions. So cookies won't be sent on web → auth login would still work (login response includes access token in body plus sets cookies), and Bearer token used thereafter. But CSRF cookie is HttpOnly=false readable; the app doesn't read document.cookie. The login response contains csrf_token per `_refresh`; login response likely includes csrf_token too. Let's check auth_controller login and backend response.

More important for native correctness: withCredentials on web. For proper "HttpOnly cookie auth where supported by target platform", set `withCredentials: true` on web (and it's ignored native?). Dio BaseOptions has `extra`? Actually `BaseOptions` doesn't have withCredentials; the browser adapter's `BrowserHttpClientAdapter` has `withCredentials` property. Use:

```dart
if (kIsWeb) {
  dio.httpClientAdapter = BrowserHttpClientAdapter(withCredentials: true);
}
```
But importing `dio/browser_adapter.dart` might not be supported on all platforms? It is web-only; need conditional import. Actually `BrowserHttpClientAdapter` is in `package:dio/browser.dart`. Importing that on native may still compile? dio's browser.dart is conditionally... likely it imports dart:html / package:web, breaking native compile. Use conditional import file.

We can defer; web verification only. But the Phase 8 requirement is mobile (Android/iOS) where CookieManager handles cookies. Web is only verification. Still, enabling withCredentials improves the web build and allows testing HttpOnly cookie auth. Let's implement conditional adapter:

#### Thinking

Intent "vote" keywords: vote, proposal, decision, approve, pending. The message "Summarise the open votes" contains "votes" — keyword boundary regex `(?<![a-z0-9])vote(?![a-z0-9])` doesn't match "votes" (plural). "open votes" not matched, "summarise" irrelevant. Hence fallback. That's a real backend gap (plural/word variants), but Phase 7 claimed validated. The mobile suggestion should use a phrasing that matches ("Summarise the open proposals" — "proposals" also fails; "Summarise open decisions" fails plural). Hmm, all keywords singular and exact. "Summarise the open proposal" would match.

Better fix backend keyword matching to allow simple English plurals/verb forms (e.g., strip trailing s/es/ed/ing?). But requirement says backend logic remains authoritative; we can improve backend. Alternatively change the mobile suggestion to "What proposals are pending?" — "pending" matches exactly (no plural). That's a one-word suggestion fix on the Flutter side. But this exposes a real backend weakness for natural plural phrasing; likely affects many user messages. However, modifying backend is allowed (preserve, not rewrite). A safe improvement: in `_keyword_seen`, for ASCII keywords also match if folded token equals keyword + "s"/"es" or keyword stems? Risky false positives (e.g., "approve" vs "approves", "decision" vs "decisions").

Given the user's current phase is Flutter, minimal change: set the suggestion to "Which proposals are pending?" Wait "proposals" plural fails, "pending" matches → intent vote. Good: "What decisions are pending?" → "decisions" fails but "pending" matches. Use "What is pending a group decision?" — "pending" matches.

But the deeper issue: "Summarise the open votes" was my own suggestion; better to fix backend matching for plurals since real users will say "votes". Let's examine tests around assistant to see intended intents. Maybe there are tests for "any pending votes".

"Which activities are protected?" — "activities" not in itinerary keywords, but "protected" not either; words "which"? no. "itinerary" intent order after recommend; no match → fallback. So that suggestion also fails. "What should we do tomorrow" matches "what should" (recommend) and "tomorrow" (itinerary), recommend checked before itinerary → recommend. Fine.

Let me fix these two.

But wait — maybe the assistant endpoint handles protected via context, and the search matched intent "itinerary". The answer may not address protected specifically. Still better.

Actually a broader question: should we improve backend token matching for plurals? This is a real quality issue, but phase says preserve backend; a targeted, tested improvement is allowed. Adding plural tolerance for ASCII keywords ("vote" matches "votes") is low-risk and improves natural language. The regex currently requires exact word. We could match keyword + optional s/es. E.g.:

```python
if keyword.isascii():
    pattern = rf"(?<![a-z0-9]){re.escape(keyword)}(?:s|es)?(?![a-z0-9])"
```
But "spend" + s = "spends" fine; "rain" + s = "rains" fine; "plan" + s = "plans" fine; "members" + s = "memberss" no. "who is" contains space; adding s to the phrase end: "who is" + s → "who iss" — harmless since exact phrase still matches. But "when is" +? no.

This makes "votes" work, "proposals" work, "decisions" work, "activities" still not (activity → activities irregular y→ies). Could also add y→ies: if keyword ends with y, allow keyword[:-1]+"ies". And "itineraries" from itinerary. This improves natural language significantly with little risk. Need to run backend tests.

However, the user's Phase 8 focus is Flutter; modifying backend mid-verification risks introducing regressions and requires restarting APIs. But tests exist. It's a genuine bug in the assistant semantics, and the user's directive earlier: "Do not simply report problems. Investigate, fix, test and verify them." I'll implement the plural tolerance and a backend test, then fix the suggestion phrasing as well (belt and braces).

Let's implement in `_keyword_seen`:

```python
def _keyword_seen(keyword: str, folded: str) -> bool:
    if keyword.isascii():
        variants = [re.escape(keyword)]
        if keyword.isalpha() and " " not in keyword:
            if keyword.endswith("y"):
                variants.append(re.escape(keyword[:-1]) + "ies")
            variants.append(re.escape(keyword) + "s")
            variants.append(re.escape(keyword) + "es")
        pattern = "|".join(variants)
        return re.search(rf"(?<![a-z0-9])(?:{pattern})(?![a-z0-9])", folded) is not None
    return keyword in folded
```

Careful: keywords like "who is" (not alpha? contains space → skip). "group members" contains space. "days" (overview has "how many days") skip. "is" no.

But adding "es" to "vote" → "votees"? harmless. "cost"+"s" = "costs" good.

"approve"+"s" = "approves" good. "pending"+"s" weird but harmless.

One risk: "plan"+"s" matches "plans", intended. "share"+"s" = "shares" privacy intent fine. "rain"+"s" fine.

Irregular: "activity" y→ies: matches "activities". "itinerary" → "itineraries". Good.

Add a regression test in test_phase7_multilingual.py for "Summarise the open votes" → intent vote (or whichever). Need to know trip fixture has open proposals. kyoto fixture seeded has open proposals. Add test:

```python
def test_plural_phrasing_matches_intent(client, mira, kyoto):
    body = _ask(client, mira, kyoto, "Summarise the open votes")
    assert body["intent"] == "vote"
    assert body["answer"]
```

But test DB fixture might have no proposals? It asserts answer regardless. If intent vote with none open, answer is "no open proposals". Good.

Also test "Which activities are protected?" → "activities" plural now matches "activity"? Activity isn't in itinerary lexicon; itinerary has "when is", "agenda", "doing", "today", "tomorrow", "plan", "schedule", "itinerary". So no.

Let's do the backend fix + test, then mobile suggestion change to natural phrasing. Then restart api 8020 and Flutter to verify.

Before editing backend, run existing assistant tests to ensure environment. Use pytest with venv. Command: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_phase7_multilingual.py -q. Might be slow but fine.

I found a real assistant intent gap: plural phrasing like "open votes" doesn't match the backend's singular keywords. I'll add plural tolerance in the backend lexicon matcher with a regression test, rather than papering over it in the UI.

70	/// A cookie jar that keeps the refresh token across app restarts.
71	///
72	/// The backend rotates the refresh token and only accepts it from the
73	/// `safar_refresh` cookie scoped to `/api/auth`. Access and CSRF tokens stay in
74	/// memory; only cookies are persisted, and only in secure storage.
75	class SafarCookieJar implements CookieJar {
76	  SafarCookieJar(this._store);
77	
78	  final JsonStore _store;
79	  final Map<String, _StoredCookie> _cookies = {};
80	  bool _loaded = false;
81	
82	  @override
83	  bool get ignoreExpires => false;
84	
85	  Future<void> load() async {
86	    if (_loaded) return;
87	    _loaded = true;
88	    final raw = await _store.read(_storageKey);
89	    if (raw == null || raw.isEmpty) return;
90	    try {
91	      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw);
92	      if (decoded is! List) return;
93	      for (final entry in decoded) {
94	        if (entry is! Map<String, dynamic>) continue;
95	        final cookie = _StoredCookie.fromJson(entry);
96	        if (cookie.name.isEmpty || cookie.isExpired) continue;
97	        _cookies[cookie.key] = cookie;
98	      }
99	    } on FormatException {
100	      await _store.delete(_storageKey);
101	    }
102	  }
103	
104	  Future<void> _persist() async {
105	    final live = _cookies.values.where((cookie) => !cookie.isExpired).toList();
106	    _cookies
107	      ..clear()
108	      ..addEntries(live.map((cookie) => MapEntry(cookie.key, cookie)));
109	    await _store.write(
110	      _storageKey,
111	      jsonEncode(live.map((cookie) => cookie.toJson()).toList()),
112	    );
113	  }

115	  @override
116	  Future<void> saveFromResponse(Uri uri, List<Cookie> cookies) async {
117	    final now = DateTime.now();
118	    for (final cookie in cookies) {
119	      final path = cookie.path?.isNotEmpty == true ? cookie.path! : '/';
120	      int? expiresAt;
121	      final maxAge = cookie.maxAge;
122	      if (maxAge != null) {
123	        if (maxAge <= 0) {
124	          _cookies.remove('${cookie.domain ?? uri.host}|$path|${cookie.name}');
125	          continue;
126	        }
127	        expiresAt = now.add(Duration(seconds: maxAge)).millisecondsSinceEpoch;
128	      } else if (cookie.expires != null) {
129	        expiresAt = cookie.expires!.millisecondsSinceEpoch;
130	      }
131	      final stored = _StoredCookie(

135	        domain: cookie.domain,

137	        expiresAt: expiresAt,

# SAFAR — Phase 8: Flutter Application Development & Backend Integration

SAFAR is an AI-powered collaborative travel application.

The previous development phases have established the backend, database, authentication, security, AI/ML systems and product functionality.

**Important architectural correction: SAFAR must be developed as a Flutter application, not as a React/Next.js web application.**

Your task is to build the actual Flutter frontend while preserving the existing backend and all completed functionality.

## 1. Audit Before Implementation

Inspect the entire existing repository.

Identify:
- Existing React/Next.js frontend.
- FastAPI backend.
- PostgreSQL database and migrations.
- Authentication and session management.
- All API endpoints.
- Existing feature registry (F01–F49).
- AI/ML services and provider integrations.
- Existing design system and UI screenshots.

Create a migration plan before implementation.

Do not delete or rewrite working backend functionality.

## 2. Flutter Architecture

Create a properly structured Flutter application.

Use:
- Flutter and Dart.
- Material 3 with a customised SAFAR design system.
- Riverpod for state management.
- GoRouter for navigation.
- Dio for API communication.
- Secure storage for sensitive client-side session data, where appropriate.
- Freezed or equivalent typed models where useful.

Use a maintainable feature-first folder structure.

Separate:
- Core configuration.
- API clients.
- Authentication.
- Shared widgets.
- Design system.
- Feature modules.
- Data models.
- Repositories.
- State management.

## 3. Backend Integration

166	    if (options.extra['skipAuth'] != true) {
167	      final token = client.accessToken;
168	      if (token != null && token.isNotEmpty) {
169	        options.headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $token';
170	      }
171	      final csrf = client.csrfToken;
172	      if (_unsafeMethods.contains(options.method.toUpperCase()) &&
173	          csrf != null &&
174	          csrf.isNotEmpty) {
175	        options.headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = csrf;
176	      }
177	    }
178	    handler.next(options);
179	  }
180	
181	  @override
182	  Future<void> onError(
183	    DioException err,
184	    ErrorInterceptorHandler handler,
185	  ) async {
186	    final options = err.requestOptions;
187	    final status = err.response?.statusCode;
188	    final isAuthPath = options.path.startsWith('/api/auth/');
189	    final retried = options.extra['retried'] == true;
190	    if (status == 401 && !retried && !isAuthPath) {
191	      try {
192	        final refreshed = await client.refreshSession();
193	        if (refreshed) {
194	          final headers = Map<String, dynamic>.from(options.headers);
195	          final token = client.accessToken;
196	          if (token != null) headers['Authorization'] = 'Bearer $token';
197	          final csrf = client.csrfToken;
198	          if (_unsafeMethods.contains(options.method.toUpperCase()) &&
199	              csrf != null) {
200	            headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = csrf;
201	          }
202	          final retryOptions = options.copyWith(
203	            headers: headers,
204	            extra: {...options.extra, 'retried': true},
205	          );
206	          final response = await client.dio.fetch<dynamic>(retryOptions);
207	          return handler.resolve(response);
208	        }
209	        client.notifyUnauthorized();
210	      } on Object {
211	        // A network failure while refreshing must not sign the user out.
212	      }
213	    }
214	    handler.next(err);
215	  }

3	class ApiException implements Exception {
4	  ApiException({
5	    required this.message,
6	    this.statusCode,
7	    this.detail,
8	    this.isNetwork = false,
9	    this.isTimeout = false,
10	  });
11	
12	  final String message;
13	  final int? statusCode;
14	  final dynamic detail;
15	  final bool isNetwork;
16	  final bool isTimeout;
17	
18	  bool get isUnauthorized => statusCode == 401 || statusCode == 403;
19	
20	  factory ApiException.fromDio(DioException error) {
21	    final status = error.response?.statusCode;
22	    final detail = error.response?.data is Map
23	        ? (error.response!.data as Map)['detail'] ?? error.response!.data
24	        : error.response?.data;
25	    final message = _messageFor(detail) ?? _fallback(error, status);
26	    final type = error.type;
27	    return ApiException(
28	      message: message,
29	      statusCode: status,
30	      detail: detail,
31	      isNetwork:
32	          type == DioExceptionType.connectionError ||
33	          type == DioExceptionType.badCertificate,
34	      isTimeout:
35	          type == DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout ||
36	          type == DioExceptionType.sendTimeout ||
37	          type == DioExceptionType.receiveTimeout,
38	    );
39	  }
40	
41	  static String? _messageFor(dynamic detail) {
42	    if (detail == null) return null;
43	    if (detail is String) return detail;
44	    if (detail is List) {
45	      final parts = detail
46	          .map((item) {
47	            if (item is Map && item['msg'] != null) return '${item['msg']}';
48	            return '$item';
49	          })
50	          .where((part) => part.trim().isNotEmpty)
51	          .toList();
52	      if (parts.isNotEmpty) return parts.join(' · ');
53	      return null;
54	    }
55	    if (detail is Map) {
56	      final message = detail['message'] ?? detail['detail'];
57	      if (message != null) return '$message';
58	    }
59	    return null;
60	  }
61	
62	  static String _fallback(DioException error, int? status) {
63	    switch (error.type) {
64	      case DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout:
65	      case DioExceptionType.sendTimeout:
66	      case DioExceptionType.receiveTimeout:
67	        return 'The server took too long to respond. Check your connection and try again.';
68	      case DioExceptionType.connectionError:
69	        return 'Could not reach SAFAR. Check the API address and your network.';
70	      case DioExceptionType.badCertificate:
71	        return 'The secure connection could not be verified.';
72	      case DioExceptionType.cancel:
73	        return 'The request was cancelled.';
74	      default:
75	        if (status == 401) return 'Your session has expired. Sign in again.';
76	        if (status == 403) return 'You do not have access to this action.';
77	        if (status == 404) return 'This item could not be found.';
78	        if (status == 409) return 'That conflicts with the current plan.';
79	        if (status == 422) return 'Please check the information you entered.';
80	        if (status != null && status >= 500) {
81	          return 'SAFAR had a problem completing that request.';
82	        }
83	        return 'The request could not be completed.';
84	    }
85	  }
86

Now I'll write the live integration test. Note: Flutter test using `dart:io` HttpClientAdapter (default) supports cookies via CookieManager. But Dio's default adapter for VM uses `HttpClient` with a per-instance cookie jar; CookieManager interceptor manages cookies explicitly, so that's fine.

The CSRF test: with cookie-only session (no Authorization), logout requires CSRF. Our client always sends access token (Authorization header) plus cookies. `_token_from_request` prefers bearer header presumably, so source == "bearer" bypasses CSRF. To test CSRF, we need to craft a raw request without Authorization but with cookies. We can use the jar's loadForRequest to build a Cookie header manually via a bare Dio instance.

"""Per-IP sliding-window rate limiting.

Single-process in-memory limiter: adequate for one API instance. Horizontal
scaling needs a shared limiter at the gateway or a Redis-backed limiter; both
are documented in DEPLOYMENT.md. Health endpoints are exempt so probes never
consume the budget.
"""

import time
from collections import defaultdict, deque

from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.requests import Request
from starlette.responses import JSONResponse

from .config import settings

WINDOW_SECONDS = 60.0
MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS = 20_000
EXEMPT_PATHS = {"/api/health", "/api/ready", "/api/openapi.json"}


def _client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    if settings.trust_proxy_headers:
        forwarded = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")
        if forwarded:
            candidate = forwarded.split(",")[0].strip()
            if candidate:
                return candidate
    return request.client.host if request.client else "unknown"


def _bucket_for(path: str, method: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    if path in {"/api/auth/login", "/api/auth/register", "/api/auth/refresh", "/api/auth/logout"}:
        return "auth", settings.auth_rate_limit_per_minute
    if path.startswith("/api/companion/") and path.endswith("/respond") and method == "POST":
        return "companion", settings.companion_rate_limit_per_minute
    if method == "POST" and (
        path.endswith("/media") or path.endswith("/memories") or path.endswith("/sync")
    ):
        return "upload", settings.upload_rate_limit_per_minute
    return "default", settings.rate_limit_per_minute


class RateLimitMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    def __init__(self, app):
        super().__init__(app)
        self._hits: dict[tuple[str, str], deque[float]] = defaultdict(deque)

    def _trim(self, now: float) -> None:
        if len(self._hits) <= MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS:
            return
        for key in [key for key, window in self._hits.items() if not window]:
            self._hits.pop(key, None)
        while len(self._hits) > MAX_TRACKED_CLIENTS:
            self._hits.pop(next(iter(self._hits)))

    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        path = request.url.path
        if not path.startswith("/api") or request.method == "OPTIONS" or path in EXEMPT_PATHS:
            return await call_next(request)

        now = time.monotonic()
        bucket, limit = _bucket_for(path, request.method)
        key = (_client_ip(request), bucket)
        window = self._hits[key]
        while window and now - window[0] > WINDOW_SECONDS:
            window.popleft()
        if len(window) >= limit:
            retry_after = max(1, int(WINDOW_SECONDS - (now - window[0])) + 1)
            return JSONResponse(
                status_code=429,
                headers={"Retry-After": str(retry_after)},
                content={"detail": "Too many requests. Please slow down."},
            )
        window.append(now)
        self._trim(now)
        return await call_next(request)

apps/mobile/README.md
# SAFAR

**The Living Journey Network** — *Every Person. Every Moment. One Intelligent Journey.*

SAFAR is a collaborative travel platform where a group experience engine
recommends and the group decides. It plans around real hard constraints
(budget, accessibility, time, travel radius), protects private member data,
labels every estimate and report honestly, and turns the finished journey into
a story worth keeping.

- Feature-by-feature honesty: [`docs/FEATURE_REGISTRY.md`](docs/FEATURE_REGISTRY.md)
- Architecture and trust model: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

---

## 1. Project architecture

```
apps/web        Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind
                TanStack Query · Zustand · React Hook Form + Zod · Framer Motion
                Lucide · Leaflet/OpenStreetMap · PWA (manifest + service worker)
services/api    FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Pydantic 2 + PyJWT
                Routers → services → models; Alembic migrations; pytest
docker-compose  web + api + PostgreSQL/PostGIS (production-like)
```

The frontend talks to the API over JSON and one WebSocket channel per trip.
The intelligence layer lives inside the API as separate deterministic services;
there is no external LLM, weather, routing or translation provider wired in.
See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full diagram, data model groups and the
enforcement points for every privacy invariant.

```
apps/web/app/(app)/trips/[tripId]/   itinerary · voting · pulse · engine ·
                                     twin · rescue · insights · map · places ·
                                     memories · expenses · members · pact ·
                                     tasks · branches · watch · ground ·
                                     missions · offline · assistant · more
```

## 2. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Frontend | Next.js 15.5 (App Router), React 19.3, TypeScript 5.7 (strict), Tailwind 3.4 |
| Client state | TanStack Query 5, Zustand 5 (persisted auth), React Hook Form 7 + Zod 3 |
| UI | Custom editorial design system, Framer Motion, Lucide, Leaflet + OSM |
| Backend | FastAPI 0.115, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic 2.10, PyJWT, uvicorn |
| Database | SQLite for development/tests; PostgreSQL (Supabase-compatible) in production |
| Migrations | Alembic (baseline revision committed; 52 tables) |
| Tests | pytest + FastAPI TestClient; Vitest + jsdom |
| Realtime | In-process WebSocket hub, token-verified per trip |

## 3. Installation

Prerequisites: Python 3.12+, Node.js 20+, npm.

# SAFAR — Flutter migration plan (Phase 8)

Status: implementation in progress (2026-11-20). The FastAPI backend in
`services/api` is the system of record. The Next.js app in `apps/web` stays in
place and remains the reference implementation until the Flutter app is
verified.

## 1. Audit findings that constrain the migration

### 1.1 Stack and ownership of logic

| Layer | Location | Phase 8 treatment |
|---|---|---|
| API, auth, authorisation, RLS context | `services/api` | Reused unchanged. No endpoint or contract changes. |
| Group Experience Engine, assistant, forecasting, Dream Import, Memory Studio | `services/api/app/services` | Reused unchanged. Flutter never re-implements ranking, NLU, extraction or privacy filtering. |
| PostgreSQL schema and migrations | `services/api/alembic` | Reused unchanged. |
| Reference UI and design system | `apps/web` | Kept available; used as the visual and workflow reference. |
| Flutter client | `apps/mobile` (new) | Built in this phase. |

### 1.2 Authentication contract (verified in `app/routers/auth.py`, `app/core/cookies.py`, `app/core/deps.py`)

- Login/register return `{access_token, csrf_token, user, expires_in, token_type}` and set three cookies:
  - `safar_access` — HttpOnly, 15 minutes, path `/`.
  - `safar_refresh` — HttpOnly, 30 days, path `/api/auth`.
  - `safar_csrf` — readable, 30 days, path `/`.
- `POST /api/auth/refresh` reads **only** the refresh cookie. A bearer-only
  client cannot refresh. The Flutter client therefore persists the cookie jar
  (all `Set-Cookie` values) in `flutter_secure_storage` on native platforms.
- Bearer requests bypass CSRF in `deps.py`; cookie-sourced unsafe requests
  require `X-CSRF-Token` equal to `safar_csrf`. Flutter sends both the bearer
  token and the CSRF header, so behaviour is correct in either mode.
- Session revocation is checked through the `sid` claim on every request.
- `COOKIE_SECURE` defaults to true only in production. Development cookies work
  over plain HTTP for emulators and local verification.

### 1.3 Platform networking

- Native apps are not subject to CORS. They are subject to
  `TrustedHostMiddleware`: add the emulator host (for example `10.0.2.2`) to
  `TRUSTED_HOSTS` when pointing an Android emulator at a host machine.
- The API base URL is a compile-time `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=...`.
  There is no localhost default in release builds; a release build without the
  define fails fast with a configuration error.
- Flutter web is used only as a local verification target in this environment
  (no iOS host, no Windows C++ toolchain). Its origin must be added to
  `CORS_ORIGINS` for that verification run.

### 1.4 Design system extracted from Phase 6 (`docs/UI_DESIGN.md`, `app/globals.css`)

- Paper/surface/raised/ink/muted/faint/line/ember/ember-soft/jade/jade-soft/rose,
  with light and dark values.
- Serif display face for headings, system sans for body, uppercase 0.14em
  eyebrows, tabular numerals for prices and times.
- 1.5rem cards, 2rem hero panels, 1px hairlines, soft card shadows, 200–300 ms
  `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` transitions.
- Trust language is part of the UI: provenance labels
  (`VERIFIED`/`REPORTED`/`ESTIMATED`/`PREDICTED`), confidence, limitations and
  "nothing changes until approved" notes.

- **State**: Riverpod 3 (`Provider`, `FutureProvider.autoDispose.family`,
  `AsyncNotifier` for session and mutating flows).
- **Routing**: GoRouter with an auth redirect gate, deep links to trips and
  destinations, and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar for Home / Discover / Ask /
  You.
- **HTTP**: one Dio instance with `dio_cookie_manager` and a persisted
  `cookie_jar`; an auth interceptor attaches bearer + CSRF, refreshes once on
  401, serialises concurrent refreshes and emits an unauthorised event after a
  failed refresh.
- **Models**: immutable Dart classes with explicit `fromJson` factories
  (equivalent to Freezed for this read-heavy client, without a codegen step in
  CI). Unknown/extra JSON fields are ignored; no model invents defaults that
  would turn missing data into a fact.
- **Errors**: `ApiException` carries status + server detail; repositories map
  network failures to typed failures; widgets render loading, empty, error and
  retry states from real request state.
- **Backend remains authoritative**: no AI, ranking, forecasting, extraction or
  authorisation logic in Dart. The client only renders and submits.

## 3. Endpoint → screen matrix

| Screen | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Splash / onboarding | `POST /api/auth/refresh`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Login / register | `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/register` |
| Dashboard | `GET /api/users/me`, `GET /api/trips`, `GET /api/users/me/dna`, `GET /api/users/me/notifications` |
| Discover | `GET /api/destinations`, `GET /api/destinations/{id}`, `GET /api/activities/search` |
| Place detail | `GET /api/trips/{id}/places/{activityId}`, `POST /api/trips/{id}/place-reports` |
| Trip creation | `POST /api/trips` |
| Trip overview | `GET /api/trips/{id}`, members, `GET /api/trips/{id}/next-action`, itinerary summary |
| Itinerary | `GET /api/trips/{id}/itinerary`, item create/update/delete, attendance |
| Group Experience Engine | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/engine/*`, feedback, propose |
| Group voting | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/proposals*`, vote, approve/reject |
| Group expenses | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/expenses`, `GET /balances` |
| Journey DNA | `GET/PUT /api/users/me/dna`, `PATCH /api/users/me/profile` |
| Memories / Studio | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/memories`, `GET /memory-studio`, `POST /memory-events` |
| Journey Replay | `GET /api/trips/{id}/replay` |
| Dream Import | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/inspirations`, `POST .../review` |
| Trip Rescue | `POST /api/trips/{id}/rescue/analyze`, `POST .../rescue/propose` |
| AI assistant | `POST /api/assistant/chat`, `POST /api/trips/{id}/assistant`, `GET /api/assistant/capabilities` |
| Profile / settings | `GET /api/users/me`, profile/consents/settings update, blocks, export |
| Notifications | `GET /api/users/me/notifications`, read / read-all |

Secondary web routes (circles, contributors, connections, missions, tasks,
branches, twin, companion links, offline sync, opportunity clock) are reached
from the trip "More" surface where their endpoints exist. They are not
re-implemented as static placeholders.

## 4. Migration order

1. Scaffold and core infrastructure (config, cookie jar, Dio, theme, router, shell).
2. Splash/onboarding, login and register; session restore, refresh and logout.
3. Dashboard, discover, trip creation.
4. Trip overview, itinerary, engine, voting, expenses, pulse, DNA.
5. Assistant, Dream Import, Rescue, memories/studio/replay, place detail.
6. Profile/settings, notifications, error/offline states.
7. Analysis, unit/widget tests, live API integration test, Android build, docs.

## 5. Verification plan

- `flutter analyze` clean.
- Unit tests: cookie persistence/path matching, auth refresh single-flight,
  error mapping, date/currency helpers, model parsing for representative payloads.
- Widget tests: splash gate, login validation, dashboard loading/error/empty,
  itinerary timeline, engine explanation rendering, assistant provenance labels.
- Live API integration test (Dart VM, real HTTP): register/login, refresh,
  trip create, itinerary read, engine generate, assistant answer, logout, session
  revoked. Run against the local FastAPI instance.
- `flutter build apk --debug` (Android SDK 36.1.0 is installed). iOS cannot be
  built on this Windows host; that limitation is reported rather than claimed.
- Visual verification on Flutter web (Chrome) and/or Android if an emulator is
  available, against the live API with CORS configured.

## 6. Explicit non-goals and limits

- No backend behaviour is changed to make the client easier.
- No mock API layer, seeded fake responses or static feature screens.
- No secrets in the Flutter bundle; only the API base URL is configured.
- Private budgets, accessibility needs, pulse notes and private memories are
  rendered only where the API returns them to the current user.
- The Next.js app is not removed in this phase.

## 1. System overview

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  apps/web — Next.js 15 (App Router, React 19, TypeScript)         │
│                                                                  │
│  Public:  /  /login  /register                                   │
│  App:     (app)/layout  → RequireAuth + AppShell                 │
│           (app)/trips/[tripId]/layout → TripShell + WebSocket     │
│                                                                  │
│  State:   Zustand (auth token, theme, toasts, offline queue)      │
│  Server:  TanStack Query (queries + mutations + invalidation)     │
│  Forms:   React Hook Form + Zod                                   │
│  Motion:  Framer Motion · Icons: Lucide · Map: Leaflet (OSM)      │
│  PWA:     manifest + service worker (public/sw.js)                │
└───────────────▲──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                │ HTTPS/JSON + WebSocket (/ws/trips/{id})
┌───────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  services/api — FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Pydantic 2               │
│                                                                  │
│  Routers   auth · users · trips/invitations · itinerary · pulse   │
│            engine · expenses · places · memories · assistant      │
│            admin · ws                                             │
│  Services  engine · ranking · place intelligence · discovery ·    │
│            expenses · memory · assistant · feedback · twin ·      │
│            rescue · fairness · impact · governance · safety       │
│  Security  JWT (HS256) · rate limit middleware · audit log        │
│  Storage   local /media (static) — object storage not configured  │
│  DB        SQLite (dev/test) · PostgreSQL/Supabase (production)   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The API also exposes OpenAPI at `/api/docs` and `/api/openapi.json`, a
machine-readable capability disclosure at `/api/ai/capabilities` (also
`/api/assistant/capabilities`), and a key-free provider snapshot that includes
weather, link metadata, OCR, translation, LLM, email and storage states.

## 8. Running ML services

There is no separate ML service to run. The intelligence layer is in-process and
deterministic: `services/engine.py`, `ranking.py`, `places.py`, `memory.py`,
`assistant.py`, `feedback.py`, `twin.py`, `rescue.py`, `optimizer.py`,
`fairness.py`, `impact.py`. Each service is testable through the HTTP API and
emits its own labels, uncertainties and provenance. If an external model is
added later, it must go behind one of these service interfaces so the API's
capability disclosure stays truthful.

  lib/
    api.ts                     fetch wrapper; token from Zustand; 401 event
    hooks.ts                   TanStack Query hooks per endpoint
    realtime.ts                WebSocket client with heartbeat + invalidation

    utils.ts                   formatting, phase, DNA labels
  tests/                       Vitest unit tests
```

Every trip page is a client component that reads `useParams()` and fetches
through `lib/hooks.ts`. Mutations invalidate the relevant query keys, and the
WebSocket channel additionally invalidates on server events.

Native builds persist the cookie\njar in Keychain / encrypted preferences instead. Never add the web origin to a\nproduction CORS list unless the deployment truly serves a browser client.\n\n## Session model\n\n- Login/register return an access token, a CSRF token and three cookies:\n  `safar_access` (HttpOnly, 15 min, `/`), `safar_refresh` (HttpOnly, 30 days,\n  `/api/auth`) and `safar_csrf` (readable, `/`).\n- Native: `SafarCookieJar` stores cookies in `flutter_secure_storage` and\n  `CookieManager` attaches them. The refresh cookie survives app restarts;\n  access and CSRF tokens stay in memory only.\n- Web: the browser owns the cookies.\n- Requests send `Authorization: Bearer` plus `X-CSRF-Token` for unsafe methods.\n  Cookie-only unsafe requests without CSRF are rejected by the API (403).\n- A 401 triggers one single-flight `POST /api/auth/refresh`, a token rotation\n  and an automatic retry. A failed refresh clears the local session and sends\n  the user to sign-in. Logout calls the API (revoking the session server-side)\n  and clears local state even if the call fails.\n- No secrets are bundled in the app; only the public API base URL is configured.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\nlib/\n  main.dart\n  app/            app root, GoRouter, bottom-navigation shell\n  core/\n    config/       compile-time environment (API base URL)\n    network/      Dio client, auth interceptor, persisted cookie jar, errors\n    storage/      JsonStore abstraction (secure storage + in-memory test store)\n    models/       typed immutable models with explicit fromJson\n    repositories/ one per domain; transport only, no business rules\n    theme/        SAFAR design tokens and Material 3 theme (light/dark)\n    widgets/      shared cards, buttons, headers, chips, states, skeletons\n    utils/        date, time, currency and text formatting\n  features/\n    auth/         splash, onboarding, login, register, session controller\n    home/         dashboard\n    discover/     destinations, destination detail, place detail + crowd forecast\n    trips/        trip list and creation\n    trip/         overview, itinerary, engine, proposals, expenses, pulse,\n                  rescue, memories, studio, replay, import\n    assistant/    grounded travel assistant\n    profile/      profile, settings, consents, notifications\n```\n\nState: Riverpod 2.6.1 (`StateNotifier` for the session, `FutureProvider.family`\nfor reads, `ref.invalidate` after mutations). Routing: GoRouter with an auth\ngate and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar (Home, Discover, Trips, Ask, You).\nHTTP: a single Dio instance with an auth interceptor, timeouts (12 s connect,\n45 s receive) and typed `ApiException`s.\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\nflutter analyze\nflutter test                                   # unit + widget tests\nSAFAR_LIVE_API=http://localhost:8010 \\\n  flutter test test/integration/live_api_test.dart\n```\n\nThe live suite needs a seeded database. It performs roughly ten auth calls, so\ngive the verification instance headroom, for example\n`AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100`. It covers login, refresh-cookie persistence\nacross restarts, transparent token refresh with rotation, logout revocation,\nCSRF rejection of cookie-only writes, wrong credentials and network failure.\n\n## Builds\n\n```bash\nflutter build apk --debug\nflutter build appbundle --release \\\n  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host\n```\n\niOS builds require macOS with Xcode: `flutter build ios --release`.\n\n## Troubleshooting “Failed to fetch”\n\nThis error is the browser’s generic network failure; it is not a Flutter\nexception. The causes found during Phase 8 were:\n\n1. The web build called `http://localhost:8000` while the API ran on `:8010`.\n   Fix: pass `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL` matching the running API.\n2. The API’s CORS list did not include the Flutter web origin, so the browser\n   blocked the response. Fix: add the exact origin to `CORS_ORIGINS` (native\n   apps are unaffected by CORS).\n3. ## 1. Project architecture

```
apps/web        Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind
                TanStack Query · Zustand · React Hook Form + Zod · Framer Motion
                Lucide · Leaflet/OpenStreetMap · PWA (manifest + service worker)
services/api    FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Pydantic 2 + PyJWT
                Routers → services → models; Alembic migrations; pytest
docker-compose  web + api + PostgreSQL/PostGIS (production-like)
```

The frontend talks to the API over JSON and one WebSocket channel per trip.
The intelligence layer lives inside the API as separate deterministic services;
there is no external LLM, weather, routing or translation provider wired in.
See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full diagram, data model groups and the
enforcement points for every privacy invariant.

```
apps/web/app/(app)/trips/[tripId]/   itinerary · voting · pulse · engine ·
                                     twin · rescue · insights · map · places ·
                                     memories · expenses · members · pact ·
                                     tasks · branches · watch · ground ·
                                     missions · offline · assistant · more
```

## 2. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Frontend | Next.js 15.5 (App Router), React 19.3, TypeScript 5.7 (strict), Tailwind 3.4 |
| Client state | TanStack Query 5, Zustand 5 (persisted auth), React Hook Form 7 + Zod 3 |
| UI | Custom editorial design system, Framer Motion, Lucide, Leaflet + OSM |
| Backend | FastAPI 0.115, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic 2.10, PyJWT, uvicorn |
| Database | SQLite for development/tests; PostgreSQL (Supabase-compatible) in production |
| Migrations | Alembic (baseline revision committed; 52 tables) |
| Tests | pytest + FastAPI TestClient; Vitest + jsdom |
| Realtime | In-process WebSocket hub, token-verified per trip |

## 3. Installation
====
## 10. Testing

```bash
# Backend — 16 API/rule tests on a temporary seeded SQLite database
cd services/api
python -m pytest tests -q

# Frontend — 12 unit tests (formatting, offline queue, toasts)
cd apps/web
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

The backend tests assert the non-negotiable product rules: engine recommends
without changing the plan, approval gates, member privacy, provenance labels,
idempotent sync, private memories, pact limits, ground-answer labelling, circle
member privacy, and WebSocket membership.

Browser verification: every `(app)` route was loaded in a production build
against the seeded data and checked for runtime errors and rendered content.
See `docs/FEATURE_REGISTRY.md` for per-feature evidence.

Phase 8 is complete for the primary Flutter application. Final report:

## 1. Flutter architecture

Feature-first app in `apps/mobile` (`safar_mobile`): `app/` (GoRouter, shell), `core/` (config, Dio client, cookie jar, secure storage, typed models, repositories, design system, widgets, formatters) and `features/` (auth, home, discover, trips, trip, assistant, profile). State is Riverpod 2.6 (`StateNotifier` session, `FutureProvider.family` reads); HTTP is one Dio instance with a single-flight refresh interceptor. All business rules, ranking, extraction and privacy filtering remain server-side.

Key entry points: [env.dart](file:///C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/config/env.dart), [api_client.dart](file:///C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/network/api_client.dart), [cookie_jar.dart](file:///C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/network/cookie_jar.dart).

## 2. Implemented screens

All 18 priority screens: splash/onboarding, login, register, dashboard, discover + destination detail, trip creation, trip overview, itinerary, engine, voting, expenses, Journey DNA, memories, Memory Studio, Journey Replay, Dream Import, Trip Rescue, assistant, profile/settings, notifications. Place detail (reports, crowd forecast, access chain) is also implemented. Every screen calls real endpoints through repositories; no mock data or static feature screens.

## 3. API integration status

Live-verified against the seeded Kyoto trip and a newly created trip: session restore, reads, trip creation, itinerary edits, attendance, proposals/votes, expenses, engine recommendations with sources/uncertainty, rescue alternatives, memories/studio/replay, Dream Import review, grounded assistant answers, DNA, settings, notifications mark-all-read, dark theme. Loading, empty, error, retry and network-failure states come from real request state; timeouts are 12 s connect / 45 s receive.

The “Failed to fetch” investigation identified the causes as a mismatched API port/base URL and a missing CORS origin for the browser target. Both are documented with fixes; native clients are unaffected by CORS. Base URL is compile-time only: debug defaults to `10.0.2.2:8010` on Android and `localhost:8010` elsewhere; release builds fail fast without `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL`.

## 4. Authentication implementation

Native persists only the cookie jar in secure storage; access/CSRF tokens stay in memory. Web uses credentialed browser cookies. A 401 triggers one refresh with token rotation and one retry; a rejected refresh signs the user out; logout revokes the server session and always clears local state. No secrets are bundled.

## 5. Feature-by-feature migration

**26 migrated, 1 partial, 22 web-only** (full table in [FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md](file:///C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md)). ## 4. Native Mobile Capabilities

- Authenticated connections.
- Session-bound connection lifecycle.
- Reconnection with exponential backoff.
- Duplicate event protection.
- State reconciliation after reconnecting.
- Proper subscription cleanup.
- Polling or manual refresh fallback.

Do not expose authentication tokens in logs or URLs.

## SAFAR API contracts (all paths relative to `services/api`)

Key files: `app/routers/{engine,itinerary,trips,places,companion,memories,admin,users,assistant,auth,ws}.py`, `app/schemas/schemas.py`, `app/services/{twin,optimizer,rescue,opportunity,discovery,places,companion,assistant}.py`, `app/services/serializers.py`.

**Auth helper (applies everywhere):** `get_trip_and_member()` — non-member / deleted trip returns **404** (deliberately, not 403); wrong role returns **403**. All endpoints below require `Authorization: Bearer`.

**1. Trip Twin** (`routers/engine.py:474,508`; `services/twin.py`)
- `POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/twin/compare` — body `TwinCompareIn`: `activity_ids: list[str]` (default `[]`, max 16; empty → 422), `day: date|None` (defaults today). No query params. Response: `day`, `confirmed_plan` / `alternative_plan` (each: `name` + `total_cost: float`, `total_duration_minutes: int`, `total_travel_minutes: int`, `average_group_fit: float|None`, `minimum_member_fit: float|None`, `items: [{activity_id,name,cost,duration,distance_km,travel_minutes,eligible}]`), `diff{added[],removed[],kept[]}` (items `{activity_id,name}`), `trade_offs: list[str]`, `requires_approval: true`, `disclosure`, `generated_at` (ISO string). Read-only.
- `POST .../twin/propose` — body `TwinProposeIn`: `activity_ids` **required** (1–16), `day?`. Creates proposal `kind="twin_adopt"`, broadcasts `proposal.created`. Response = `proposal_out` + `impact` (see 22). Tests: `test_audit_fixes.py` (compare), `test_phase4.py::test_f39_twin_adoption_cannot_remove_protected_block`, `test_audit_fixes.py` (propose).

**2. Shadowplans** (`itinerary.py:1159,1194`)
- `POST` body `{item_id, backup_activity_id, notes?}` → `{id, backup_activity_id, readiness{status, checked_at}}`. Mutates.
- `GET` → `{items: [{id, item_id, backup_activity_id, notes, readiness, created_at}]}`.
Any member. No pytest coverage.

**3. Opportunity Clock** (`opportunity.py:13`, `services/opportunity.py`)
- `GET .../opportunity-clock?on=YYYY-MM-DD` (`on: date|None`; out of trip range → 422). Response: `date`, `available`, `weekday`, `now`, `planned_count`, `planned_titles[]`, `free_windows[{start,end,minutes}]`, `items[{activity_id,name,place_name,duration_minutes,price_estimate,currency,opening_hours_today,opening_source,last_verified_at,travel_minutes_estimate,status,next_start,explanation,provenance}]` (`status` ∈ open_now/later_today/no_window/window_missed/closed_today/unknown), `summary{candidates,open_now,later_today,closed_today,unknown_hours}`, `explanation`, `disclosure`, `plan_unchanged`, `confirmed_version`. Read-only. Test: `test_stabilisation.py`.

**4. Branches** (`trips.py:986,1015`)
- `GET` → `{items: [{id,name,member_ids,activity_id,reunion_at,reunion_place,status}]}`.
- `POST` body `{name, member_ids[], activity_id?, reunion_at?, reunion_place?}` → `{id, feasibility{status, note, distance_km?, travel_minutes?}}`. Mutates. No tests.

Nearby** (`places.py:228`) — `GET .../nearby?lat&lon&radius_km&category&limit`. `lat/lon` both-or-neither (giving them without `profile.location_sharing` → 403); `radius_km` default 5 (0–50); `category` ≤60 chars; `limit` 1–60 default 20. Response `{base{lat,lon,source}, radius_km, items[{activity(activity_out), distance_km, travel_minutes, provenance}], disclosure}`. `activity_out` keys: `id, place_id, destination_id, name, description, tags[], price_estimate, currency, duration_minutes, effort, indoor, wheelchair_accessible, iconic, popularity, fragile, opening_hours{}, access_chain{}, image_url, source_type, last_verified_at, place, destination`. Read-only. Test: `test_security_hardening.py`.

- `GET` → `{items[{id,question,place_id,activity_id,status,created_at,responses[{id,observation,observed_at,confidence,verified,provenance,contributor_id}]}]}`.
- `POST` body `{place_id?, activity_id?, question(5–1000)}` — at least one of place/activity else 422 → `{id,status}`. Mutates.
- `POST .../{request_id}/responses` body `{observation(5–2000), confidence(0–1, default .5)}`. **Permission is contributor-based, not membership**: caller must be a `LocalContributor` with `accepts_requests=true` for this trip's destination (else 403). → `{id, provenance, note}`. Test: `test_api.py`.

- `POST .../join` → `{ok,joined:true,member_count}`; `DELETE .../join` → `{ok,joined:false}`. Mutating.
- `POST .../posts` (must have joined, else 403) body `{title(2–160), body(2–4000), activity_id?}` → `{id,title,body,status,created_at,moderation}`. Mutating.

Mutating. Test: `test_api.py` (circles).

- `POST .../{mission_id}/join` → `{ok,status}`; `/complete` → `{ok,status,self_reported}`; `/disable` requires **owner/admin** → `{ok}`. Mutating. No tests.

- `POST .../companion-links` body `{purpose: vote|checkin, target_id, ttl_minutes(5–10080, default 1440)}` → `{link{id,purpose,target,status,expires_at,max_uses,used_count,anonymous_responses,response_values{value:count},created_at}, token, url:"/companion/{token}", disclosure}`. `target` for vote `{kind,id,title,status}`; for checkin adds `day`.
- `GET .../companion-links` — members see only their own links unless owner/admin.
- `POST .../{link_id}/revoke` → `{id,status}`; `GET .../{link_id}/responses` (creator/owner-admin, else 403) → `{items[{id,value,comment,created_at}], anonymous:true, disclosure}`.
- Public: `GET /api/companion/{token}` → `{purpose, trip{name,destination_name}, expires_at, remaining_uses, disclosure, anonymous_responses, target(...+summary,registered_votes for vote; +day,start_time for checkin), question, options[]}`; `POST /api/companion/{token}/respond` body `{value, comment?}` (vote: yes|no|abstain; checkin: in|out|join_later) → `{ok,recorded,anonymous,remaining_uses,message}`. 410 when expired/revoked/used. Ticket: `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` (Bearer or cookie) → `{ticket, expires_in: 120}`; 400 if session id missing. Close codes: **4401** invalid/expired token, inactive user, dead session; **4404** trip missing/deleted or caller not an active member. Envelope: `{"event": str, "at": iso8601, ...data}`. Event types: `connected{trip_id,user,note}`, `pong{trip_id}`, `proposal.created{trip_id,proposal_id}`, `proposal.withdrawn`, `proposal.rejected`, `itinerary.updated`, `expenses.updated`, `member.joined`, `member.removed`, `trip.updated`, `trip.deleted`, `engine.updated`. Heartbeat: client sends the text frame `"ping"`, server replies `pong`. Tests: `test_api.py`, `test_audit_fixes.py` (no ws-ticket test).

**24. Assistant** (`assistant.py:76`) — `POST /api/assistant/chat` body `{message(1–2000), trip_id?, language?}`; per-trip variant `POST /api/trips/{trip_id}/assistant`. Response: `intent`, `answer`, `citations[{label,type,id,provenance}]`, `grounding`, `limitations[]`, `suggested_actions[{label,href}]`, `generated_by`, `context`, `language{code,name,source,detected,confidence,mixed[],unsupported}`, `mutation:"none"`, `requires_approval`, `trip_id`. Status: idle → connecting → live → closed; header shows Live / Connecting / Solo view. Heartbeat "ping" every 30s, server replies `pong`. On message: parse JSON, `type` defaults to "update"; ignore `connected`/`pong`; then **invalidate everything** — any query whose key[1] === tripId, or key[0] in `trips`, `notifications` (no per-event routing). Reconnect: on close, retry counter +1 (max 5), delay `1500 * retry` ms; success resets to 0; cleanup clears timers and sets idle. Server event types: `connected`, `pong`, `itinerary.updated`, `proposal.created|voted|approved|rejected|withdrawn`, `engine.updated`, `expenses.updated`, `pulse.updated`, `trip.updated`, `trip.deleted`, `member.joined`, `member.removed`, `member.role_updated`. No realtime events exist for branches, twin, insights, ground, missions, tasks, watch, companion, or offline — those rely on mutation-driven invalidation/refetch. Optional tripId means no socket (solo view).

# SAFAR mobile — implementation guide for new trip screens/repositories

## 1. Repositories and provider wiring

Repositories are plain classes: constructor takes `ApiClient`, private `_api` field, methods are `Future<Model>` / `Future<List<Model>>` with no state, no codegen, no caching. File: `C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/repositories/trip_repository.dart`

```dart
class TripRepository {
  TripRepository(this._api);
  final ApiClient _api;

  Future<List<TripActivityEvent>> activity(String tripId) async {
    final data = await _api.get('/api/trips/$tripId/activity');
    final raw = data is Map ? data['items'] : data;
    return jsonObjects(raw, TripActivityEvent.fromJson);
  }
}
```

Conventions worth copying exactly:
- Single-object endpoints: `Future<X> get(...) async => X.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.get('/api/...')));`
- List endpoints: tolerant envelope unwrap `data is Map ? data['items'] : data` then `jsonObjects(raw, X.fromJson)`.
- Nullable payloads: `final pact = jsonMap(data['pact']); return pact.isEmpty ? null : Pact.fromJson(pact);` (see `pact()` in `trip_repository.dart`).
- Write bodies omit empty strings with `if (description != null && description.isNotEmpty) 'description': description,`; newer code uses the Dart 3 null-aware map entry `'item_id': ?itemId` (see `engine_repository.dart` lines 29-34). Both styles exist; prefer `?value` for optional scalars, the `if` form for "skip when empty".
- Mutations return `Future<void>` and just `await _api.post/patch/put/delete(...)`.
- Query params: `query: day == null ? null : {'day': day}`.

Registration in `C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/providers.dart` (add import + one line, alphabetically near the other repositories ~line 57-83):

```dart
final tripRepositoryProvider = Provider<TripRepository>(
  (ref) => TripRepository(ref.watch(apiClientProvider)),
);
```

`ApiClient` API: `get(path, {query, raw})`, `post(path, {data, query, raw})`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, plus `mediaUrl(String?)`. Errors surface as `ApiException` (`lib/core/network/api_exception.dart`) with `.message` and `.statusCode`; the interceptor handles 401 refresh + CSRF automatically.

## 2. Models

Pure Dart, `const` constructors, all `final` fields, `factory X.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json)`, no `toJson`, no json_serializable. Helpers in `lib/core/models/json.dart`:

`jsonMap`, `jsonList`, `jsonString`, `jsonText(value,[fallback])`, `jsonInt(value,[fallback])`, `jsonIntOrNull`, `jsonDouble`, `jsonDoubleOrNull`, `jsonBool`, `jsonStringList`, `jsonObjects(raw, X.fromJson)`, `jsonDate`, `shortDate`.

Representative model — `C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/core/models/memories.dart`:

```dart
factory Memory.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) {
  final authorJson = jsonMap(json['author']);
  return Memory(
    id: jsonText(json['id']),
    kind: jsonText(json['kind'], 'text'),           // server default fallback
    aiGenerated: jsonBool(json['ai_generated']),
    author: authorJson.isEmpty ? null : User.fromJson(authorJson),
    textContent: jsonString(json['text_content']),   // nullable => jsonString
    lat: jsonDoubleOrNull(json['lat']),
  );
}
```

Rules: required scalars use `jsonText`/`jsonInt` with a sensible default; genuinely optional use `jsonString`/`jsonIntOrNull`/`jsonDoubleOrNull`; lists-of-objects use `jsonObjects`; `List<String>` uses `jsonStringList`; list fields get `= const []` defaults in the constructor; nested objects are decoded via `jsonMap` + `.isEmpty ? null :` guard; maps of scalars loop over `jsonMap(...).forEach` (see `Pact.fromJson`, `trip.dart` lines 184-198). Dates are kept as `String` and formatted at the UI edge; `shortDate()` exists for timezone-free `YYYY-MM-DD`.

## 3. Trip screen structure

Two shapes, both `ConsumerStatefulWidget`/`ConsumerWidget` with `const XScreen({super.key, required this.tripId}); final String tripId;`.

- Read-only screen (`trip_overview_screen.dart`): `ConsumerWidget`, `Scaffold(body: AsyncView(...))`.
- Interactive screen (`itinerary_screen.dart`, `rescue_screen.dart`): `ConsumerStatefulWidget` with local `_busy` / `_error` / selection fields, `AppBar` + `SafeArea` + `AsyncView` or `ListView`.

Header pattern (`rescue_screen.dart` lines 123-140) — no custom header widget:

```dart
return Scaffold(
  appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Trip Rescue')),
  body: SafeArea(top: false, child: ListView(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(20, 8, 20, 32),
    children: [
      const Eyebrow('When plans break'),
      const SizedBox(height: 8),
      Text('Find a way through.', style: context.texts.headlineLarge),
      ...
```

Data pattern (`itinerary_screen.dart`):

```dart
final itinerary = ref.watch(itineraryProvider(widget.tripId));
...
body: SafeArea(child: AsyncView(
  value: itinerary,
  onRetry: () => ref.invalidate(itineraryProvider(widget.tripId)),
  builder: (data) => RefreshIndicator(onRefresh: _refresh, child: ListView(...)),
))
```

Widget names in `lib/core/widgets/safar_widgets.dart`: `AsyncView` (`.when` + skeleton + `SafarErrorView`), `SkeletonList`, `SkeletonBox`, `SafarErrorView`, `SafarEmpty` (empty state), `InfoBanner` for inline errors/messages, `SafarCard`, `SafarActionTile`, `SectionHeader`, `Eyebrow`, `StatusChip`, `StatTile`, `SafarAvatar`, `SafarImage`, `SourceLabel`, `SafarSheetHeader`, `showSafarSheet`.

Form sheets — copy `_addItem` in `itinerary_screen.dart` lines 46-176: `showSafarSheet<bool>` + `StatefulBuilder` + `Form` + `SingleChildScrollView` + `SafarSheetHeader`, controllers created locally and `dispose()`d after the await, submit returns `Navigator.of(sheetContext).pop(true)`.

```dart
final submitted = await showSafarSheet<bool>(context,
  builder: (sheetContext) => StatefulBuilder(
    builder: (sheetContext, setSheetState) => Form(key: formKey,
      child: SingleChildScrollView(child: Column(mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start, children: [
          const SafarSheetHeader(title: 'Add an item', subtitle: '...'),
```

Mutation feedback: `setState(() => _busy = true)` → await repo → `ref.invalidate(...)` (or `await _refresh()`) → `if (!mounted) return;` → `ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(const SnackBar(content: Text('Item added.')))` on success, `SnackBar(content: Text(error.toString()))` or `error.message` on `ApiException`; `finally { if (mounted) setState(() => _busy = false); }`. Destructive confirmation uses `showDialog<bool>` + `AlertDialog` with `FilledButton.styleFrom(backgroundColor: context.safar.rose)`.

## 4. Routing

`C:/Users/siddharth/Documents/Qoder/2026-11-19/7c4196d9/apps/mobile/lib/app/router.dart` lines 106-188: `/trips/:tripId` is a top-level `GoRoute` (root navigator) with child routes. Add a sibling block and an import at the top:

```dart
GoRoute(
  path: 'memories',                       // relative => /trips/:tripId/memories
  parentNavigatorKey: _rootNavigator,
  builder: (context, state) =>
      MemoriesScreen(tripId: state.pathParameters['tripId']!),
),
```

Parameterised child: `path: 'places/:activityId'` + `state.pathParameters['activityId']!`. All trip subroutes live on the **root** navigator (they cover the bottom shell). Navigation: `context.push('/trips/$tripId/studio')` for drill-in from overview/sheets; `context.pop()` for back; `context.go(...)` only for tab resets (`/dashboard`). Back buttons guard with `context.canPop() ? context.pop() : context.go('/dashboard')` (overview) or plain `context.pop()` (sub-screens). The shell tabs live in `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack` at lines 211-261 (`/dashboard`, `/discover`, `/trips`, `/assistant`, `/profile`).
