```dart
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> upload(
  String path, {
  required List<int> bytes,
  required String filename,
  required String contentType,
}) async {
  final form = FormData.fromMap({
    'file': MultipartFile.fromBytes(bytes, filename: filename, contentType: DioMediaType.parse(contentType)),
  });
  try {
    final response = await dio.post<dynamic>(path, data: form, options: Options(contentType: 'multipart/form-data'));
    return response.data is Map ? Map<String,dynamic>.from(response.data as Map) : const {};
  } on DioException catch (e) { throw ApiException.fromDio(e); }
}
```
Dio sets multipart automatically; don't set contentType manually or boundary breaks. Use Options() default.

import 'package:dio/dio.dart';

class ApiException implements Exception {
  ApiException({
    required this.message,
    this.statusCode,
    this.detail,
    this.isNetwork = false,
    this.isTimeout = false,
  });

  final String message;
  final int? statusCode;
  final dynamic detail;
  final bool isNetwork;
  final bool isTimeout;

  bool get isUnauthorized => statusCode == 401 || statusCode == 403;

  factory ApiException.fromDio(DioException error) {
    final status = error.response?.statusCode;
    final detail = error.response?.data is Map
        ? (error.response!.data as Map)['detail'] ?? error.response!.data
        : error.response?.data;
    final message = _messageFor(detail) ?? _fallback(error, status);
    final type = error.type;
    return ApiException(
      message: message,
      statusCode: status,
      detail: detail,
      isNetwork:
          type == DioExceptionType.connectionError ||
          type == DioExceptionType.badCertificate,
      isTimeout:
          type == DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout ||
          type == DioExceptionType.sendTimeout ||
          type == DioExceptionType.receiveTimeout,
    );
  }

  static String? _messageFor(dynamic detail) {
    if (detail == null) return null;
    if (detail is String) return detail;
    if (detail is List) {
      final parts = detail
          .map((item) {
            if (item is Map && item['msg'] != null) return '${item['msg']}';
            return '$item';
          })
          .where((part) => part.trim().isNotEmpty)
          .toList();
      if (parts.isNotEmpty) return parts.join(' · ');
      return null;
    }
    if (detail is Map) {
      final message = detail['message'] ?? detail['detail'];
      if (message != null) return '$message';
    }
    return null;
  }

  static String _fallback(DioException error, int? status) {
    switch (error.type) {
      case DioExceptionType.connectionTimeout:
      case DioExceptionType.sendTimeout:
      case DioExceptionType.receiveTimeout:
        return 'The server took too long to respond. Check your connection and try again.';
      case DioExceptionType.connectionError:
        return 'Could not reach SAFAR. Check the API address and your network.';
      case DioExceptionType.badCertificate:
        return 'The secure connection could not be verified.';
      case DioExceptionType.cancel:
        return 'The request was cancelled.';
      default:
        if (status == 401) return 'Your session has expired. Sign in again.';
        if (status == 403) return 'You do not have access to this action.';
        if (status == 404) return 'This item could not be found.';
        if (status == 409) return 'That conflicts with the current plan.';
        if (status == 422) return 'Please check the information you entered.';
        if (status != null && status >= 500) {
          return 'SAFAR had a problem completing that request.';
        }
        return 'The request could not be completed.';
    }
  }

  @override
  String toString() => message;
}

def _trip(db, trip_id, user, roles=None):
    return get_trip_and_member(trip_id, db, user, roles)


def _naive_utc(value: datetime | None) -> datetime:
    if value is None:
        return utcnow()
    if value.tzinfo is None:
        return value
    return value.astimezone(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)


def _validate_memory_content(kind: str, text: str | None, media_url: str | None) -> None:
    if not text and not media_url:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="A memory needs text or a media upload.",
        )
    if kind in {"photo", "video", "voice"} and not media_url:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail=f"A {kind} memory needs an uploaded media file.",
        )
    if media_url and not (
        media_url.startswith("/media/")
        or media_url.startswith("https://")
    ):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="Media must be an uploaded SAFAR file or an HTTPS URL.",
        )


def _memory_for_trip(db: Session, trip: Trip, memory_id: str, viewer_id: str) -> TripMemory:
    memory = db.get(TripMemory, memory_id)
    if not memory or memory.trip_id != trip.id or memory.deleted_at is not None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Memory not found")
    if not memory_service.can_view_memory(db, memory, viewer_id):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Memory not found")
    return memory

@router.get("/trips/{trip_id}/nearby")
def nearby(
    trip_id: str,
    lat: float | None = Query(default=None, ge=-90, le=90),
    lon: float | None = Query(default=None, ge=-180, le=180),
    radius_km: float = Query(default=5, gt=0, le=50),
    category: str | None = Query(default=None, max_length=60),
    limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=60),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    if lat is not None or lon is not None:
        profile = db.query(Profile).filter(Profile.user_id == user.id).first()
        if not profile or not profile.location_sharing:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=403,
                detail=(
                    "Enable precise location in your privacy settings to use "
                    "your current position for nearby suggestions."
                ),
            )
        if lat is None or lon is None:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=422, detail="Provide both lat and lon, or neither"
            )
    base_lat = lat if lat is not None else trip.base_lat
    base_lon = lon if lon is not None else trip.base_lon
    activities = (
        db.query(Activity).filter(Activity.destination_id == trip.destination_id).all()
        if trip.destination_id
        else []
    )
    place_map, destination_map = _activity_place_maps(db, activities)
    items = []
    for activity in activities:
        place = place_map.get(activity.place_id)
        if not place:
            continue
        if category and place.category.lower() != category.lower():
            continue
        distance = haversine_km(base_lat, base_lon, place.lat, place.lon)
        if distance > radius_km:
            continue
        items.append(
            {
                "activity": activity_out(
                    activity, place, destination_map.get(activity.destination_id)
                ),
                "distance_km": round(distance, 2),
                "travel_minutes": travel_minutes(distance),
                "provenance": "ESTIMATED",
            }
        )
    items.sort(key=lambda item: item["distance_km"])
    return {
        "base": {"lat": base_lat, "lon": base_lon, "source": "shared trip base" if lat is None else "requested point"},
        "radius_km": radius_km,
        "items": items[:limit],
        "disclosure": (
            "Distances are straight-line estimates and travel time is not a live routed ETA. "
            "No live member location is exposed."
        ),
    }


def _activity_for_trip(db: Session, trip: Trip, activity_id: str) -> Activity:
    activity = db.get(Activity, activity_id)
    if not activity:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Activity not found")
    if activity.destination_id != trip.destination_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Activity not found for this trip")
    return activity

`companionPathFrom(Uri uri)`:
```dart
String? companionPathFrom(Uri uri) {
  final segments = uri.pathSegments.where((s)=>s.isNotEmpty).toList();
  if (uri.scheme == 'safar' && uri.host == 'companion' && segments.length == 1) return '/companion/${segments.first}';
  if ((uri.scheme=='https'||uri.scheme=='http') && segments.length==2 && segments[0]=='companion') return '/companion/${segments[1]}';
  return null;
}
```

class UserRepository {
  UserRepository(this._api);

  final ApiClient _api;

  Future<Me> me() async =>
      Me.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.get('/api/users/me')));

  Future<Profile> updateProfile(Map<String, dynamic> changes) async =>
      Profile.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.patch('/api/users/me/profile', data: changes)));

  Future<Dna> updateDna(Map<String, int> scores) async =>
      Dna.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.put('/api/users/me/dna', data: {'scores': scores})));

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> updateConsents(Map<String, bool> consents) async =>
      jsonMap(await _api.put('/api/users/me/consents', data: {'consents': consents}));

  Future<User> updateSettings(Map<String, dynamic> changes) async =>
      User.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.patch('/api/users/me/settings', data: changes)));

  Future<NotificationFeed> notifications() async =>
      NotificationFeed.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.get('/api/users/me/notifications')));

  Future<void> markRead(String id) async {
    await _api.post('/api/users/me/notifications/$id/read');
  }

  Future<void> markAllRead() async {
    await _api.post('/api/users/me/notifications/read-all');
  }

  Future<ThreadResponse> thread() async =>
      ThreadResponse.fromJson(jsonMap(await _api.get('/api/users/me/thread')));

  Future<String> exportData() async =>
      (await _api.get('/api/users/me/export', raw: true)).toString();

  Future<void> deleteAccount() async {
    await _api.delete('/api/users/me');
  }
}

import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';

import 'package:safar_mobile/core/utils/format.dart';

void main() {
  group('date and time formatting', () {
    test('formats calendar dates', () {
      expect(formatDate('2026-03-08'), '8 Mar 2026');
      expect(formatDateShort('2026-03-08'), '8 Mar');
      expect(formatWeekday('2026-03-08'), 'Sunday');
    });

    test('returns fallbacks for missing values', () {
      expect(formatDate(null), '—');
      expect(formatDate(''), '—');
      expect(formatDateShort(null, fallback: 'TBD'), 'TBD');
      expect(formatWeekday(null), '');
    });

    test('formats 24-hour strings as 12-hour clock times', () {
      expect(formatTime('09:05'), '9:05 AM');
      expect(formatTime('13:45'), '1:45 PM');
      expect(formatTime('00:00'), '12:00 AM');
      expect(formatTime('12:30'), '12:30 PM');
    });

    test('formatClock accepts ISO timestamps and plain times', () {
      expect(formatClock('13:45'), '1:45 PM');
      final iso = DateTime(2026, 3, 8, 18, 5).toIso8601String();
      expect(formatClock(iso), '6:05 PM');
      expect(formatClock(null), '');
    });

    test('tripDays lists inclusive calendar days', () {
      final days = tripDays('2026-03-08', '2026-03-10');
      expect(days.map(isoDate), ['2026-03-08', '2026-03-09', '2026-03-10']);
    });

    test('tripDays handles inverted ranges', () {
      expect(tripDays('2026-03-10', '2026-03-08'), hasLength(1));
    });

    test('timeAgo describes recent timestamps', () {
      final now = DateTime.now().toUtc();
      expect(timeAgo(now.toIso8601String()), 'just now');
      expect(
        timeAgo(now.subtract(const Duration(minutes: 5)).toIso8601String()),
        '5m ago',
      );
      expect(
        timeAgo(now.subtract(const Duration(hours: 3)).toIso8601String()),
        '3h ago',
      );
      expect(timeAgo(null), '');
    });

    test('titleCase normalises separators', () {
      expect(titleCase('group_experience-engine'), 'Group Experience Engine');
      expect(titleCase('rain'), 'Rain');
    });

import 'package:flutter_secure_storage/flutter_secure_storage.dart';

/// Small key/value contract so the cookie jar and session logic are testable
/// without platform plugins.
abstract class JsonStore {
  Future<String?> read(String key);
  Future<void> write(String key, String value);
  Future<void> delete(String key);
}

/// Native storage uses Keychain (iOS) and encrypted shared preferences
/// (Android). The refresh cookie is never written to plain shared preferences.
class SecureJsonStore implements JsonStore {
  SecureJsonStore([FlutterSecureStorage? storage])
    : _storage = storage ?? const FlutterSecureStorage();

  final FlutterSecureStorage _storage;

  @override
  Future<String?> read(String key) => _storage.read(key: key);

  @override
  Future<void> write(String key, String value) =>
      _storage.write(key: key, value: value);

  @override
  Future<void> delete(String key) => _storage.delete(key: key);
}

/// Used by unit tests and by the web verification target, where the browser
/// owns HttpOnly cookies and the Dart layer must not persist them.
class MemoryJsonStore implements JsonStore {
  final Map<String, String> _values = {};

  @override
  Future<String?> read(String key) async => _values[key];

  @override
  Future<void> write(String key, String value) async => _values[key] = value;

  @override
  Future<void> delete(String key) async => _values.remove(key);
}

import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:math';

import 'json_store.dart';

/// A memory captured on the device while the API was unreachable. The queue
/// lives in secure storage; entries are removed only after the server reports
/// them applied or already known.
class OfflineCapture {
  const OfflineCapture({
    required this.clientId,
    required this.tripId,
    required this.text,
    required this.capturedAt,
  });

  final String clientId;
  final String tripId;
  final String text;
  final String capturedAt;

  Map<String, dynamic> get payload => {
    'kind': 'text',
    'text_content': text,
    'visibility': 'trip',
    'captured_at': capturedAt,
  };

  Map<String, dynamic> toJson() => {
    'client_id': clientId,
    'trip_id': tripId,
    'text': text,
    'captured_at': capturedAt,
  };

  factory OfflineCapture.fromJson(Map<String, dynamic> json) => OfflineCapture(
    clientId: '${json['client_id'] ?? ''}',
    tripId: '${json['trip_id'] ?? ''}',
    text: '${json['text'] ?? ''}',
    capturedAt: '${json['captured_at'] ?? ''}',
  );
}

class OfflineQueue {
  OfflineQueue(this._store);

  static const _key = 'safar.offline.captures';

  final JsonStore _store;

  /// Server contract: client ids are 6–80 characters.
  static String newClientId() {
    final time = DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch.toRadixString(36);
    final salt = Random.secure().nextInt(1 << 32).toRadixString(36);
    return 'm$time$salt';
  }

  Future<List<OfflineCapture>> load() async {
    final raw = await _store.read(_key);
    if (raw == null || raw.isEmpty) return const [];
    try {
      final decoded = jsonDecode(raw);
      if (decoded is! List) return const [];
      return decoded
          .whereType<Map>()
          .map((item) => OfflineCapture.fromJson(
                item.map((key, value) => MapEntry('$key', value)),
              ))
          .where((capture) => capture.clientId.isNotEmpty && capture.text.isNotEmpty)
          .toList();
    } on FormatException {
      return const [];
    }
  }

  Future<List<OfflineCapture>> add(OfflineCapture capture) async {
    final current = await load();
    final next = [...current, capture];
    await save(next);
    return next;
  }

  Future<List<OfflineCapture>> remove(Iterable<String> clientIds) async {
    final settled = clientIds.toSet();
    final next =
        (await load()).where((capture) => !settled.contains(capture.clientId)).toList();
    await save(next);
    return next;
  }

  Future<void> save(List<OfflineCapture> captures) => _store.write(
    _key,
    jsonEncode(captures.map((capture) => capture.toJson()).toList()),
  );
}

1	# SAFAR — Flutter migration plan (Phase 8)
2	
3	Status: primary screens implemented and verified; secondary modules remain
4	web-only (see §7). Last updated 2026-11-20. The FastAPI backend in
5	`services/api` is the system of record. The Next.js app in `apps/web` stays in
6	place and remains the reference implementation until the Flutter app is
7	verified.
8	
9	## 1. Audit findings that constrain the migration
10	
11	### 1.1 Stack and ownership of logic
12	
13	| Layer | Location | Phase 8 treatment |
14	|---|---|---|
15	| API, auth, authorisation, RLS context | `services/api` | Reused unchanged. No endpoint or contract changes. |
16	| Group Experience Engine, assistant, forecasting, Dream Import, Memory Studio | `services/api/app/services` | Reused unchanged. Flutter never re-implements ranking, NLU, extraction or privacy filtering. |
17	| PostgreSQL schema and migrations | `services/api/alembic` | Reused unchanged. |
18	| Reference UI and design system | `apps/web` | Kept available; used as the visual and workflow reference. |
19	| Flutter client | `apps/mobile` (new) | Built in this phase. |
20	
21	### 1.2 Authentication contract (verified in `app/routers/auth.py`, `app/core/cookies.py`, `app/core/deps.py`)
22	
23	- Login/register return `{access_token, csrf_token, user, expires_in, token_type}` and set three cookies:
24	  - `safar_access` — HttpOnly, 15 minutes, path `/`.
25	  - `safar_refresh` — HttpOnly, 30 days, path `/api/auth`.
26	  - `safar_csrf` — readable, 30 days, path `/`.
27	- `POST /api/auth/refresh` reads **only** the refresh cookie. A bearer-only
28	  client cannot refresh. The Flutter client therefore persists the cookie jar
29	  (all `Set-Cookie` values) in `flutter_secure_storage` on native platforms.
30	- Bearer requests bypass CSRF in `deps.py`; cookie-sourced unsafe requests
31	  require `X-CSRF-Token` equal to `safar_csrf`. Flutter sends both the bearer
32	  token and the CSRF header, so behaviour is correct in either mode.
33	- Session revocation is checked through the `sid` claim on every request.
34	- `COOKIE_SECURE` defaults to true only in production. Development cookies work
35	  over plain HTTP for emulators and local verification.
36	
37	### 1.3 Platform networking
38	
39	- Native apps are not subject to CORS. They are subject to
40	  `TrustedHostMiddleware`: the dev default now includes the emulator alias
41	  `10.0.2.2`. A physical device or another host still needs to be added to
42	  `TRUSTED_HOSTS`.
43	- The API base URL is a compile-time `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=...`.
44	  There is no localhost default in release builds; a release build without the
45	  define fails fast with a configuration error.
46	- Flutter web is used only as a local verification target in this environment
47	  (no iOS host, no Windows C++ toolchain). Its origin must be added to
48	  `CORS_ORIGINS` for that verification run.
49	
50	### 1.4 Design system extracted from Phase 6 (`docs/UI_DESIGN.md`, `app/globals.css`)
51	
52	- Paper/surface/raised/ink/muted/faint/line/ember/ember-soft/jade/jade-soft/rose,
53	  with light and dark values.
54	- Serif display face for headings, system sans for body, uppercase 0.14em
55	  eyebrows, tabular numerals for prices and times.
56	- 1.5rem cards, 2rem hero panels, 1px hairlines, soft card shadows, 200–300 ms
57	  `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` transitions.
58	- Trust language is part of the UI: provenance labels
59	  (`VERIFIED`/`REPORTED`/`ESTIMATED`/`PREDICTED`), confidence, limitations and
60	  "nothing changes until approved" notes.
61	
62	## 2. Flutter architecture
63	
64	```
65	apps/mobile/
66	  lib/
67	    main.dart
68	    app/                 # app root, router, shell, theme wiring
69	    core/
70	      config/            # compile-time environment and base URL
71	      network/           # Dio client, persisted cookie jar, auth interceptor, errors
72	      storage/           # secure storage abstraction (+ in-memory test store)
73	      models/            # typed immutable models with fromJson
74	      repositories/      # API repositories per domain (no business rules)
75	      theme/             # SAFAR tokens, Material 3 theme, typography
76	      widgets/           # buttons, cards, headers, badges, states, skeletons
77	      utils/             # dates, currency, formatting
78	    features/
79	      auth/              # splash, onboarding, login, register, session controller
80	      dashboard/
81	      discover/          # destinations, destination detail, place detail + crowd forecast
82	      trips/             # trip list and creation
83	      trip/              # overview, itinerary, engine, voting, expenses, pulse, DNA
84	      assistant/
85	      inspirations/      # Dream Import
86	      rescue/
87	      memories/          # memories, studio, replay
88	      notifications/
89	      profile/           # profile, settings, consents, sign out
90	```
91	
92	- **State**: Riverpod 2.6.1 (`Provider`, `FutureProvider.autoDispose.family`,
93	  `StateNotifier` for the session, `ref.invalidate` after mutations).
94	- **Routing**: GoRouter with an auth redirect gate, deep links to trips and
95	  destinations, and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar for Home / Discover / Ask /
96	  You.
97	- **HTTP**: one Dio instance with `dio_cookie_manager` and a persisted
98	  `cookie_jar`; an auth interceptor attaches bearer + CSRF, refreshes once on
99	  401, serialises concurrent refreshes and emits an unauthorised event after a
100	  failed refresh.
101	- **Models**: immutable Dart classes with explicit `fromJson` factories
102	  (equivalent to Freezed for this read-heavy client, without a codegen step in
103	  CI). Unknown/extra JSON fields are ignored; no model invents defaults that
104	  would turn missing data into a fact.
105	- **Errors**: `ApiException` carries status + server detail; repositories map
106	  network failures to typed failures; widgets render loading, empty, error and
107	  retry states from real request state.
108	- **Backend remains authoritative**: no AI, ranking, forecasting, extraction or
109	  authorisation logic in Dart. The client only renders and submits.
110	
111	## 3. Endpoint → screen matrix
112	
113	| Screen | Endpoints |
114	|---|---|
115	| Splash / onboarding | `POST /api/auth/refresh`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
116	| Login / register | `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/register` |
117	| Dashboard | `GET /api/users/me`, `GET /api/trips`, `GET /api/users/me/dna`, `GET /api/users/me/notifications` |
118	| Discover | `GET /api/destinations`, `GET /api/destinations/{id}`, `GET /api/activities/search` |
119	| Place detail | `GET /api/trips/{id}/places/{activityId}`, `POST /api/trips/{id}/place-reports` |
120	| Trip creation | `POST /api/trips` |
121	| Trip overview | `GET /api/trips/{id}`, members, `GET /api/trips/{id}/next-action`, itinerary summary |
122	| Itinerary | `GET /api/trips/{id}/itinerary`, item create/update/delete, attendance |
123	| Group Experience Engine | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/engine/*`, feedback, propose |
124	| Group voting | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/proposals*`, vote, approve/reject |
125	| Group expenses | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/expenses`, `GET /balances` |
126	| Journey DNA | `GET/PUT /api/users/me/dna`, `PATCH /api/users/me/profile` |
127	| Memories / Studio | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/memories`, `GET /memory-studio`, `POST /memory-events` |
128	| Journey Replay | `GET /api/trips/{id}/replay` |
129	| Dream Import | `GET/POST /api/trips/{id}/inspirations`, `POST .../review` |
130	| Trip Rescue | `POST /api/trips/{id}/rescue/analyze`, `POST .../rescue/propose` |
131	| AI assistant | `POST /api/assistant/chat`, `POST /api/trips/{id}/assistant`, `GET /api/assistant/capabilities` |
132	| Profile / settings | `GET /api/users/me`, profile/consents/settings update, blocks, export |
133	| Notifications | `GET /api/users/me/notifications`, read / read-all |
134	
135	Secondary web routes (circles, contributors, connections, missions, tasks,
136	branches, twin, companion links, offline sync, opportunity clock) are reached
137	from the trip "More" surface where their endpoints exist. They are not
138	re-implemented as static placeholders.
139	
140	## 4. Migration order
141	
142	1. Scaffold and core infrastructure (config, cookie jar, Dio, theme, router, shell).
143	2. Splash/onboarding, login and register; session restore, refresh and logout.
144	3. Dashboard, discover, trip creation.
145	4. Trip overview, itinerary, engine, voting, expenses, pulse, DNA.
146	5. Assistant, Dream Import, Rescue, memories/studio/replay, place detail.
147	6. Profile/settings, notifications, error/offline states.
148	7. Analysis, unit/widget tests, live API integration test, Android build, docs.
149	
150	## 5. Verification plan
151	
152	- `flutter analyze` clean.
153	- Unit tests: cookie persistence/path matching, auth refresh single-flight,
154	  error mapping, date/currency helpers, model parsing for representative payloads.
155	- Widget tests: splash gate, login validation, dashboard loading/error/empty,
156	  itinerary timeline, engine explanation rendering, assistant provenance labels.
157	- Live API integration test (Dart VM, real HTTP): register/login, refresh,
158	  trip create, itinerary read, engine generate, assistant answer, logout, session
159	  revoked. Run against the local FastAPI instance.
160	- `flutter build apk --debug` (Android SDK 36.1.0 is installed). iOS cannot be
161	  built on this Windows host; that limitation is reported rather than claimed.
162	- Visual verification on Flutter web (Chrome) and/or Android if an emulator is
163	  available, against the live API with CORS configured.
164	
165	## 6. Explicit non-goals and limits
166	
167	- No backend behaviour is changed to make the client easier.
168	- No mock API layer, seeded fake responses or static feature screens.
169	- No secrets in the Flutter bundle; only the API base URL is configured.
170	- Private budgets, accessibility needs, pulse notes and private memories are
171	  rendered only where the API returns them to the current user.
172	- The Next.js app is not removed in this phase.

219	
220	- Native cookie jar persisted in secure storage; web uses credentialed
221	  browser cookies. Access and CSRF tokens stay in memory.
222	- Single-flight refresh on 401, automatic retry, rotation of the refresh token,
223	  and sign-out on a rejected refresh.

227	  restart, transparent refresh with refresh-token rotation, logout revocation,

106	### Known external dependencies that are intentionally absent
107	
108	| Dependency | Effect | Product behaviour |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| LLM provider | No generative answers, no AI captions | Deterministic grounded retrieval; caption drafts are template-based and require approval |
111	| Weather API | Real forecast only when `SAFAR_WEATHER_PROVIDER=open-meteo` (off by default) | Otherwise the assistant and rescue state that weather is unknown; rescue remains user-driven |
112	| Translation service | No remote translation provider | Eight languages answered with in-repo lexicons and templates; unsupported input falls back to English with a note |
113	| Link metadata | Off unless `SAFAR_LINK_FETCH_ENABLED=true` | Dream Import inspects the supplied URL string only and says the link was not read |
114	| Image OCR | Local Tesseract only; no cloud vision | Uploaded trip images are read on-server or reported as unavailable; never uploaded to a vendor |
115	| Live routing/traffic | No routed ETAs | Travel times are estimates, always labelled |
116	| Live availability/ticketing | No booking | Catalog is curated seed data, labelled ESTIMATED unless a verified source exists |
117	| Object storage | Media on local disk | Type/size validation; media served via expiring HMAC-signed URLs |
118	| Email/SMS delivery | No outbound messages | Invitations are shareable links; in-app notifications only |

120	## Deep audit addendum (2026-11-19)
121	
122	Defects found by runtime probes and fixed, each now pinned by a regression test:
123	
124	| Defect | Impact | Fix |
125	|---|---|---|
126	| Invitation tokens were reusable and not bound to the invited email | An intercepted link let any account join the trip | accept returns 409 after first use and 403 for a different email; preview reports `accepted_by_you` |
127	| `/media/...` was served unauthenticated to anyone who guessed a path | Private trip media could leak | HMAC-signed URLs with 12 h expiry; unsigned/tampered requests 403 |
128	| Memory Studio events leaked metadata of private memories | Other members saw event titles/dates referencing hidden memories | `visible_events()` filters events unless every referenced memory is visible (studio and replay) |
129	| Default budget comfort was treated as a hard budget cap | Members who never stated a limit silently lost affordable results | only a stated `budget_limit` filters; comfort is a soft preference used for ranking |
130	| Expense currency was required | Expenses failed when the trip currency should apply | currency defaults to the trip's currency |
131	| Completed-trip next action linked to a non-existent route | Dead link from the dashboard | links to `/trips/{id}/memories/replay` |
132	| OpenAI settings existed but nothing used them | Risk of implying generative AI | health/capabilities report `external_ai: false`; key is inert (now documented) |
133	
134	Verification added in `services/api/tests/test_audit_fixes.py`: invite single-use and
135	email binding, signed media, private event metadata, engine budget semantics,
136	expense currency, rescue proposal validation and non-mutation, trip-scoped
137	inspiration import, admin rejection for non-admins, anonymising deletion with token
138	revocation, Journey DNA consent gating, three engine modes, explicit no-destination
139	failure, Trip Twin read-only adoption, constraint compass, reason-free independent
140	time, WebSocket broadcast to other members, and replay link correctness.

207	## Phase 5 — Production security & infrastructure hardening (2026-11-19)
208	
209	No new travel features. The 49 product features keep their status; this phase
210	changes how they are protected, persisted and operated. Full report:
211	`docs/SECURITY.md`; audit trail: `docs/AUDIT.md` §15; runbook:
212	`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.
213	
214	| Area | Implementation | Evidence |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| Sessions | HttpOnly access/refresh cookies, server-side `auth_sessions`, rotation with reuse detection, revocation, 2-minute WS ticket | `test_refresh_rotation_rejects_a_replayed_token`, `test_logout_revokes_the_session_for_existing_tokens`; browser login/logout |
217	| CSRF | Double-submit `safar_csrf` + `X-CSRF-Token`, constant-time compare | `test_cookie_sessions_require_csrf_for_writes` |
218	| Database isolation | RLS on 55 tables, 220 policies, FORCE, fail-closed GUCs, non-owner role | direct SQL probes; 68 tests on PG |
219	| API hardening | Security headers, TrustedHost, body limit, per-bucket rate limits, harmless errors, docs off in production | 19 hardening tests |
220	| Uploads | Magic-byte sniffing; oversized/spoofed files rejected | `test_media_upload_rejects_a_spoofed_content_type` |
221	| Privacy | Erasure expanded, retention job, location consent required for precise coordinates | `test_account_deletion_erases_personal_data`, `test_retention_removes_only_expired_rows`, `test_precise_location_requires_the_privacy_toggle` |
222	| Secrets/config | No committed secrets; production guards for `SECRET_KEY`, CORS, cookies, docs, seeding; accurate `.env.example` | config review; `.env.example` |
223	| Recovery | `pg_dump -Fc` / `pg_restore` drill with schema, policy, row and RLS parity | `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` §6 |
224	
225	Phase 5 totals: `pytest` **68 passed on SQLite** and **68 passed on PostgreSQL
226	16.4 under FORCE RLS** · `vitest` 12 · `tsc` clean · `next build` clean.
227	
228	Status note: the product is hardened and PostgreSQL-verified, but **not
229	declared production-ready**. Docker images were not built in this environment,
230	TLS/proxy behaviour was not exercised, no load test or external review was
231	performed, and backup/PITR coverage is logical-dump only. The explicit
232	conditions are in `docs/SECURITY.md` §8.

235	
236	No feature was added, removed or re-scoped; this phase changes presentation and
237	interaction quality only. F01–F49 keep the states recorded above. Design system:

247	| A11y | `aria-pressed` chips, `role="switch"` toggles, live regions, labelled icon buttons, dialog focus/trap/restore, skip link, visible focus, reduced motion | DOM inspection; `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` §6 |

## 8. Phase 9 — complete feature migration (2026-11-20)

### 8.1 Method and audit corrections

Phase 9 re-derived the migration status from the code instead of trusting the
Phase 8 table:

- Every FastAPI router under `services/api/app/routers` was checked for the
  client contract (path, method, request/response shape, permissions) before a
  Flutter screen was written.
- Contracts that differed from the Phase 8 assumption and were corrected:
  - the offline sync envelope is a bare JSON array (max 100) with a 6–80
    character `client_id` and per-item `operation`/`payload`;
  - the task summary is `{totals:{open|done|total}, ...}`, not a flat total;
  - companion links are single-use and require an open proposal (vote) or a
    confirmed itinerary item (check-in);
  - the WS endpoint authenticates with a 120-second ticket from
    `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`, not the access token.
- No backend route, schema, service or migration needed to change. Phase 9 is a
  client migration; `services/api` and `apps/web` were not modified.

### 8.2 New Flutter modules

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| More hub | `features/trip/more_hub_screen.dart` |
| Journey Pact | `features/trip/pact_screen.dart` |
| Trip Twin / Negotiator | `features/trip/twin_screen.dart`, `negotiate_screen.dart` |
| Plan intelligence (effort, fragility, domino, shadowplans, capsules) | `features/trip/plan_intelligence_screen.dart` |
| Opportunity Clock / Branches | `opportunity_screen.dart`, `branches_screen.dart` |
| Map & nearby + consent-gated GPS | `nearby_screen.dart` |
| Ask the Ground / Local Context | `ground_screen.dart` |
| Missions / Tasks / Material Watch | `missions_screen.dart`, `tasks_screen.dart`, `watch_screen.dart` |
| Social (circles, contributors, serendipity connections, Journey Thread) | `circles_screen.dart`, `contributors_screen.dart`, `connections_screen.dart`, `thread_screen.dart` |
| One-Link Companion + public responder | `features/trip/companion_screen.dart`, `features/companion/companion_public_screen.dart` |
| Offline capture, queue and sync | `offline_screen.dart`, `core/storage/offline_queue.dart` |
| Photos in memories | `memories_screen.dart`, `memory_repository.dart` |
| Real-time transport | `core/realtime/trip_channel.dart`, `trip_realtime.dart`, `live_status_chip.dart` |
| Native helpers | `core/native/share_links.dart`, `core/native/deep_links.dart`, `app/app.dart` |

Repositories were extended for the same domains; no screen contains a static
list, fabricated response or duplicate ranking/NLU logic.

### 8.3 Feature classification (brief §9)

Legend:
**Complete** — Flutter surface is API-backed, every visible control calls the
real contract, loading/empty/error/retry states exist, and the flow was exercised
(automated test or live API smoke check).
**Partial** — a real subset ships, a named capability is still web-only.
**Web-only** — no Flutter surface.
**Blocked** — a platform/environment prevents verification.

| ID | Feature | Flutter route(s) | Status | Evidence |
...

Totals.

### 8.4 Surfaces that remain web-only

- **F04 — invitations and member administration.** Flutter can create a trip and
  read the member roster with roles (overview). Creating/revoking single-use
  invitation tokens, accepting `/invite/{token}`, changing roles, and removing
  members remain in the web member screen. The backend contract is unchanged;
  only the Flutter screen is pending. This is the reason F04 is **Partial**.
- **F10 — basemap.** Nearby, distances and the consent-gated origin are in
  Flutter; the map is a geometric relative-position canvas, not slippy tiles.
  Leaflet tiles remain web-only. This is the reason F10 is **Partial**.
- **Admin console** (`/admin`) is an operator surface, not one of F01–F49, and
  stays web-only.
- The printable HTML travel book is rendered on the web; Flutter shows the same
  server-generated travel-book text as selectable text. The content is complete;
  the print-specific delivery is not duplicated.

### 8.5 Real-time collaboration

- Transport: `TripChannel` opens `GET /ws/trips/{trip_id}?token=<ticket>` with a
  120 s ticket from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` (session-bound, invalid without a
  live session). No long-lived credential is placed in a URL.
- Connection lifecycle: connect → subscribe → 30 s ping; states `idle /
  connecting / live / reconnecting / closed`; exponential backoff 1, 2, 4, 8,
  15, 30 s; reconnect on app resume, stop on pause; explicit `stop()` clears the
  socket, timers and stream controller.
- Events consumed: `itinerary.updated`, `proposal.*`, `trip.updated/deleted`,
  `member.*`, `expenses.updated`, `engine.updated`, `pulse.updated` (plus
  `connected`/`pong` control frames).
- Dedupe: a bounded 50-entry key of `event|at|proposal_id|member_id|voter`
  prevents double invalidation when the server and a local mutation arrive
  together.
- Reconciliation: any successful reconnection triggers a one-shot invalidation
  of every trip-scoped provider (itinerary, proposals, engine, expenses,
  balances, pulse, tasks, summary, pact, branches, missions, watches, memories,
  studio, snapshot, sync queue, companion links, ground, inspirations,
  notifications) so the UI rebuilds from server truth.
- Fallback: pull-to-refresh and post-mutation `ref.invalidate` remain the
  authoritative refresh path; the WS layer is an accelerator, not a data source.
  Ticket failures (400/401/403) close the channel instead of retrying forever.
- UI: `TripLiveChip` on overview, itinerary and decisions shows Live /
  Connecting / Reconnecting / Not live with tap-to-reconnect while reconnecting.

### 8.6 Native capabilities

| Capability | Plugin | Use | Guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Share sheet | share_plus 12.0.2 | Companion link, CSV export | Invoked only by an explicit button; content is the public link/export |
| Camera / library | image_picker 1.2.2 | Photo memories | Only from Add photo; max width 1600, quality 82, 25 MB cap; MIME inferred |
| Location | geolocator 14.0.2 | Nearby origin | Only on tap; blocked unless profile `location_sharing` is on; low accuracy, 12 s limit; trip base is the default |
| Deep links | app_links 7.0.0 | `safar://companion/<token>` and `https://<web>/companion/<token>` | Parsed to the existing `/companion/:token` route only |
| WebSocket | web_socket_channel 3.0.3 | Trip collaboration | Ticket auth, session-bound |
| Secure storage | flutter_secure_storage 10.3.1 | Cookie jar on native | Pinned down from 11.x for `win32` compatibility; API surface unchanged |

Manifest/plist changes: Android `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION`/`ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION`
and a `safar` scheme intent filter; iOS `CFBundleURLTypes` (scheme `safar`),
`NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`, `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription`,
`NSCameraUsageDescription`.

Push notifications: no APNs/FCM deliverer exists in the backend, so no push
plugin was added. In-app notifications remain the supported channel.

### 8.7 Privacy and security verification

- Companion public routes expose only trip name/destination, target
  title/summary/status, registered vote counts and anonymous answer counts —
  no member identity. Responses carry no user id, IP or user agent (contract
  unchanged; verified live: create → open → respond → single-use 410 → invalid
  422 → revoke).
- Precise location requires the explicit consent toggle; with consent off, a
  nearby request with coordinates returns 403 (verified live). Flutter checks
  the toggle before requesting the OS permission.
- Private memories, budgets and pulse notes are never derived client-side; the
  screens render whatever the API returns to the current member. Media still
  uses signed, expiring URLs.
- No RLS policy, API authorisation rule, endpoint or migration was changed in
  Phase 9; the backend suite is unchanged and still passes.
- Tokens: the access/CSRF tokens stay in memory, cookies in secure storage on
  native; nothing is logged. The only URL credential is the 120 s WS ticket
  required by the server contract.
- Offline queue entries stay in local storage and are sent through the existing
  idempotent sync contract; server-side privacy filtering is unchanged.

### 8.8 Test and build evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `flutter analyze` | No issues found |
| `flutter test` (default) | 25 passed, 7 skipped (live suite) |
| Live API suite (`SAFAR_LIVE_API=http://localhost:8010`) | 7 passed |
| Phase 9 unit tests (`test/phase9_test.dart`) | 10 passed: event parsing, ws/wss URL, backoff cap, deep links, watch value rendering, companion context, offline queue |
| `pytest` (backend, unchanged) | 107 passed |
| `flutter build web --release` | Succeeded |
| `flutter build apk --debug` | Blocked before compilation: Gradle cannot download Kotlin/Maven artifacts through the environment's TLS interception (`PKIX path building failed`); offline mode has no cached artifacts. Android SDK 36.1.0 is installed. |
| iOS build | Not possible on this Windows host (no Xcode) |

Live smoke checks (curl against `localhost:8010`, seeded data): companion
create/public/respond/single-use/revoke; watch create/duplicate-409/check/verify;
task create → done → unassign → summary; offline sync apply → idempotent skip →
queue → snapshot; media upload 201 and photo memory 201; nearby with coordinates
and consent off → 403.

### 8.9 Remaining limitations

1. F04 invitations/member admin and F10 basemap tiles remain web-only.
2. No Android or iOS binary was produced (environment TLS interception; no
   macOS). Plugin native code is not compile-verified on device.
3. No emulator/simulator was available: real-time behaviour was exercised
   through the API-level tests and the transport unit tests, not on-device
   socket drops.
4. WS delivery is in-process (single API instance); multi-instance fan-out is
   unchanged from the backend design.
5. Push notifications are unavailable (no deliverer configured).
6. The web app remains the reference and fallback.

### 8.10 Final Phase 9 report (brief §10)

- **Migrated:** 47 of 49 features complete in Flutter; 2 partial (F04, F10).
  All 22 previously web-only features plus F23 now have real screens.
- **Incomplete:** invitation creation/acceptance, role change and member
  removal (F04); slippy map tiles (F10); printable HTML travel book delivery.
- **Backend changes:** none.
- **New screens:** More hub, Pact, Twin, Negotiator, Plan intelligence
  (effort/fragility/domino/shadowplan/capsule), Opportunity Clock, Branches,
  Nearby, Ground, Missions, Tasks, Watch, Connections, Contributors, Circles
  (+ detail), Thread, Companion (+ public responder), Offline.
- **WebSocket:** ticket-authenticated trip channel with backoff, dedupe,
  lifecycle handling, reconnect reconciliation and UI status.
- **Native:** share sheet, camera/library photo memories, consent-gated
  location, companion deep links, secure storage.
- **Privacy/security:** no authz or RLS change; anonymous companion responses;
  consent-gated coordinates; signed media; session-bound WS.
- **Flutter tests:** 42 passing (25 default + 7 live + 10 Phase 9) with 0
  failing; analyzer clean.
- **Backend tests:** 107 passing.
- **Builds:** web release succeeds; Android/iOS not built for environmental
  reasons stated above.
- **Remaining limitations:** listed in §8.9.

The web frontend and the Flutter client both talk to the same JSON API. The web
app also holds one WebSocket channel per trip; the Flutter client currently
refreshes on pull-to-refresh and after mutations.
The intelligence layer lives inside the API as separate deterministic services;
there is no external LLM, weather, routing or translation provider wired in.
See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full diagram, data model groups and the
enforcement points for every privacy invariant.
---ARCH 112-130---
- **Auth**: native persists only the cookie jar (Keychain on iOS, encrypted
  preferences on Android); access and CSRF tokens are memory-only. Web
  verification uses `withCredentials` so the browser owns the HttpOnly cookies.
  A 401 triggers one single-flight refresh, token rotation and one retry; a
  rejected refresh signs the user out. Logout revokes the session server-side.
- **Boundary**: the Dart layer ranks nothing, extracts nothing, forecasts
  nothing and filters no privacy data. It submits requests and renders labels,
  sources and confidence exactly as the API returns them.
- **Realtime**: the Flutter client does not consume the trip WebSocket yet; it
  refreshes on pull-to-refresh and after its own mutations.
- **Platforms**: Android and iOS are the primary targets; a Flutter web build
  is used only as a visual verification target where no emulator exists.
- Migration status, test evidence and remaining gaps:
  `docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §7.

1	# SAFAR — Flutter client (`apps/mobile`)
2	
3	The Flutter client for SAFAR. It talks directly to the existing FastAPI
4	backend in `services/api`; the API remains the only place where business rules,
5	authorisation, AI/ML inference and privacy filtering live. There is no mock
6	API layer and no client-side recommendation logic.
7	
8	Status: primary screens implemented and verified against the live API (Phase 8,
9	2026-11-20). See [`docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md`](../../docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md)
10	for the screen-by-screen and feature-by-feature status.
11	
12	## Requirements
13	
14	- Flutter 3.41+ (stable) with Dart 3.11+
15	- Android SDK 36 for Android builds
16	- Xcode 15+ on macOS for iOS builds
17	- A running SAFAR API (see the repository README)
18	
19	## Configure the API address
20	
21	The base URL is compile-time configuration, never a hardcoded production value.
22	
23	| Target | Command / default |
24	|---|---|
25	| Android emulator | Debug default `http://10.0.2.2:8010` (the emulator's alias for the host) |
26	| iOS simulator | Debug default `http://localhost:8010` |
27	| Physical device | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://<host-lan-ip>:8010` and add that host to the API `TRUSTED_HOSTS` |
28	| Production | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host` (required; a release build without it fails fast) |
29	
30	Debug builds allow cleartext HTTP on Android through
31	`android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`. Release builds require HTTPS and
32	the main manifest declares `android.permission.INTERNET`.
33	
34	## Run
35	
36	```bash
37	cd apps/mobile
38	flutter pub get
39	flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8010   # Android
40	flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010  # iOS simulator
41	```
42	
43	### Web verification target
44	
45	There is no production web target; the browser build exists only for visual
46	verification in environments without an emulator.
47	
48	```bash
49	# API with the web origin allowed and a seeded database
50	CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080 python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8010
51	
52	cd apps/mobile
53	flutter run -d web-server --web-port=8080 \
54	  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010
55	```
56	
57	On web the client uses `BrowserHttpClientAdapter(withCredentials: true)` so the
58	browser stores and sends the HttpOnly cookies. Native builds persist the cookie
59	jar in Keychain / encrypted preferences instead. Never add the web origin to a
60	production CORS list unless the deployment truly serves a browser client.

62	## Session model
63	
64	- Login/register return an access token, a CSRF token and three cookies:
65	  `safar_access` (HttpOnly, 15 min, `/`), `safar_refresh` (HttpOnly, 30 days,
66	  `/api/auth`) and `safar_csrf` (readable, `/`).
67	- Native: `SafarCookieJar` stores cookies in `flutter_secure_storage` and
68	  `CookieManager` attaches them. The refresh cookie survives app restarts;
69	  access and CSRF tokens stay in memory only.
70	- Web: the browser owns the cookies.
71	- Requests send `Authorization: Bearer` plus `X-CSRF-Token` for unsafe methods.
72	  Cookie-only unsafe requests without CSRF are rejected by the API (403).
73	- A 401 triggers one single-flight `POST /api/auth/refresh`, a token rotation
74	  and an automatic retry. A failed refresh clears the local session and sends
75	  the user to sign-in. Logout calls the API (revoking the session server-side)
76	  and clears local state even if the call fails.
77	- No secrets are bundled in the app; only the public API base URL is configured.
78	
79	## Architecture
80	
81	```
82	lib/
83	  main.dart
84	  app/            app root, GoRouter, bottom-navigation shell
85	  core/
86	    config/       compile-time environment (API base URL)
87	    network/      Dio client, auth interceptor, persisted cookie jar, errors
88	    storage/      JsonStore abstraction (secure storage + in-memory test store)
89	    models/       typed immutable models with explicit fromJson
90	    repositories/ one per domain; transport only, no business rules
91	    theme/        SAFAR design tokens and Material 3 theme (light/dark)
92	    widgets/      shared cards, buttons, headers, chips, states, skeletons
93	    utils/        date, time, currency and text formatting
94	  features/
95	    auth/         splash, onboarding, login, register, session controller
96	    home/         dashboard
97	    discover/     destinations, destination detail, place detail + crowd forecast
98	    trips/        trip list and creation
99	    trip/         overview, itinerary, engine, proposals, expenses, pulse,
100	                  rescue, memories, studio, replay, import
101	    assistant/    grounded travel assistant
102	    profile/      profile, settings, consents, notifications
103	```
104	
105	State: Riverpod 2.6.1 (`StateNotifier` for the session, `FutureProvider.family`
106	for reads, `ref.invalidate` after mutations). Routing: GoRouter with an auth
107	gate and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar (Home, Discover, Trips, Ask, You).
108	HTTP: a single Dio instance with an auth interceptor, timeouts (12 s connect,
109	45 s receive) and typed `ApiException`s.
110	
111	## Tests
112	
113	```bash
114	flutter analyze
115	flutter test                                   # unit + widget tests
116	SAFAR_LIVE_API=http://localhost:8010 \
117	  flutter test test/integration/live_api_test.dart
118	```
119	
120	The live suite needs a seeded database. It performs roughly ten auth calls, so
121	give the verification instance headroom, for example
122	`AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100`. It covers login, refresh-cookie persistence
123	across restarts, transparent token refresh with rotation, logout revocation,
124	CSRF rejection of cookie-only writes, wrong credentials and network failure.
125	
126	## Builds
127	
128	```bash
129	flutter build apk --debug
130	flutter build appbundle --release \
131	  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host
132	```
133	
134	iOS builds require macOS with Xcode: `flutter build ios --release`.
135	
136	## Troubleshooting “Failed to fetch”
137	
138	This error is the browser’s generic network failure; it is not a Flutter
139	exception. The causes found during Phase 8 were:
140	
141	1. The web build called `http://localhost:8000` while the API ran on `:8010`.
142	   Fix: pass `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL` matching the running API.
143	2. The API’s CORS list did not include the Flutter web origin, so the browser
144	   blocked the response. Fix: add the exact origin to `CORS_ORIGINS` (native
145	   apps are unaffected by CORS).
146	3. An Android emulator using `localhost` reached itself instead of the host.
147	   Fix: use `10.0.2.2` (now the debug default) or the LAN IP for a device.
148	4. A plain-HTTP API on Android release builds. The debug overlay permits
149	   cleartext for local development; release must use HTTPS.
150	
151	If the Android build fails while downloading Maven dependencies with
152	`PKIX path building failed`, a TLS-scanning product (for example Avast Web
153	Shield) is intercepting HTTPS and the JDK does not trust its root. Options are
154	to trust that root in a build-only truststore (a security decision that needs
155	explicit approval), temporarily pause TLS scanning, or build on a host without
156	interception. Do not disable TLS verification.
157

## 8. Phase 9 — complete feature migration (2026-11-20)

### 8.1 Method and audit corrections

Phase 9 re-derived the migration status from the code instead of trusting the
Phase 8 table:

- Every router under `services/api/app/routers` was checked for the client
  contract (path, method, request/response shape, permissions) before a Flutter
  screen was written.
- Contracts that differed from the Phase 8 assumption and were corrected:
  - offline sync is a bare JSON array (max 100) with a 6–80 character
    `client_id` and per-item `operation`/`payload`, not an object envelope;
  - the task summary is `{totals:{open,done,total}, …}`, not a flat `total`;
  - companion links are single-use and require an open proposal (vote) or a
    confirmed itinerary item (check-in);
  - the WS endpoint authenticates with a 120-second ticket from
    `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`, not with the access token.
- No backend route, schema, service or migration needed to change. Phase 9 is a
  client migration; `services/api` and `apps/web` were not modified.

@router.get("/{trip_id}/domino")
def get_domino(
    trip_id: str,
    item_id: str = Query(...),
    delay_minutes: int = Query(default=45, ge=0, le=600),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    items = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id, ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed")
        .all()
    )
    result = domino_map(db, items, item_id, delay_minutes)
    if not result:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Disrupted item not found")
    return result

import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

import javax.net.ssl.SSLContext;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeMap;

@NonNullApi
public class DefaultSslContextFactory implements SslContextFactory {
    private static final Set<String> SSL_SYSTEM_PROPERTIES = ImmutableSet.of(
        "ssl.TrustManagerFactory.algorithm",
        "javax.net.ssl.trustStoreType",
        "javax.net.ssl.trustStore",
        "javax.net.ssl.trustStoreProvider",
        "javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword",
        "ssl.KeyManagerFactory.algorithm",
        "javax.net.ssl.keyStoreType",
        "javax.net.ssl.keyStore",
        "javax.net.ssl.keyStoreProvider",
        "javax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword",
        "java.home"
    );

    private final LoadingCache<Map<String, String>, SSLContext> cache = CacheBuilder.newBuilder().softValues().build(
        new SynchronizedSystemPropertiesCacheLoader()
    );

    @Override
    public SSLContext createSslContext() {
        return cache.getUnchecked(getCurrentProperties());
    }

    private static Map<String, String> getCurrentProperties() {
        return SystemProperties.getInstance().withSystemProperties(() -> {
            Map<String, String> currentProperties = new TreeMap<>();
            for (String prop : SSL_SYSTEM_PROPERTIES) {
                currentProperties.put(prop, System.getProperty(prop));
            }
            return currentProperties;
        });
    }

    private static class SynchronizedSystemPropertiesCacheLoader extends CacheLoader<Map<String, String>, SSLContext> {
        @Override
        public SSLContext load(Map<String, String> props) {
            /*
             * NOTE! The JDK code to create SSLContexts relies on the values of the given system properties.
             *
             * To prevent concurrent changes to system properties from interfering with this, we need to synchronize access/modifications
             * to system properties.  This is best effort since we can't prevent user code from modifying system properties willy-nilly.
             *
             * The most critical system property is java.home. Changing this property while trying to create a SSLContext can cause many strange
             * problems:
             * https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/8830
             * https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/8039
             * https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/7842
             * https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/2588
             */
            return SystemProperties.getInstance().withSystemProperties(props, () -> SslContextLoader.load(props));
        }
    }

    @NonNullApi
    private static class SslContextLoader {
        private static final Logger LOGGER = LoggerFactory.getLogger(SslContextLoader.class);

        public static SSLContext load(Map<String, String> props) {
            try {
                return SystemDefaultSSLContextFactory.create();
            } catch (Exception e) {
                LOGGER.error("Could not initialize SSL context. Used properties: {}", props);
                throw new SSLInitializationException(e.getMessage(), e);
            }
        }
    }
}

package org.gradle.internal.resource.transport.http;

import org.gradle.api.NonNullApi;
import org.gradle.api.logging.Logger;
import org.gradle.api.logging.Logging;

import javax.annotation.Nullable;
import javax.net.ssl.KeyManager;
import javax.net.ssl.KeyManagerFactory;
import javax.net.ssl.SSLContext;
import javax.net.ssl.TrustManager;
import javax.net.ssl.TrustManagerFactory;
import java.io.File;
import java.io.FileInputStream;
import java.io.FileNotFoundException;
import java.security.KeyStore;

/**
 * This class contains SSLContext initialization similar to what SSLContext.getDefault() does.
 * Unfortunately, SSLContext.getDefault() can not be used because it is heavily cached by the JVM,
 * including keyStore and trustStore managers.
 * There is no way to reset these caches because they are private and are initialized in static sections.
 */
@NonNullApi
public class SystemDefaultSSLContextFactory {
    private static final String NONE = "NONE";
    private static final String P11KEYSTORE = "PKCS11";

    private static final Logger LOGGER = Logging.getLogger(SystemDefaultSSLContextFactory.class);

    static SSLContext create() throws Exception {
        SSLContext context = SSLContext.getInstance("TLS");
        context.init(getKeyManagers(), getTrustManagers(), null);
        return context;
    }

    private static KeyManager[] getKeyManagers() throws Exception {
        String keyStorePath = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.keyStore", "");
        String keyStoreType = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.keyStoreType", KeyStore.getDefaultType());
        String keyStoreProvider = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.keyStoreProvider", "");
        String keyStorePasswordString = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword", "");

        if (P11KEYSTORE.equals(keyStoreType) && !NONE.equals(keyStorePath)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("if keyStoreType is " + P11KEYSTORE + ", then keyStore must be " + NONE);
        }

        char[] keystorePassword = null;
        if (!keyStorePasswordString.isEmpty()) {
            keystorePassword = keyStorePasswordString.toCharArray();
        }

        KeyStore keyStore = loadKeyStore(
            keyStorePath,
            keyStoreType,
            keyStoreProvider,
            keystorePassword,
            true
        );

        KeyManagerFactory keyManagerFactory = KeyManagerFactory.getInstance(KeyManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm());
        if (P11KEYSTORE.equals(keyStoreType)) {
            keyManagerFactory.init(keyStore, null);
        } else {
            keyManagerFactory.init(keyStore, keystorePassword);
        }
        return keyManagerFactory.getKeyManagers();
    }

    @Nullable
    private static KeyStore loadKeyStore(
        String keyStorePath,
        String keyStoreType,
        String keyStoreProvider,
        @Nullable char[] keyStorePassword,
        boolean errorOnMissingFile
    ) throws Exception {
        if (keyStoreType.isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }

        KeyStore keyStore;
        if (keyStoreProvider.isEmpty()) {
            keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance(keyStoreType);
        } else {
            keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance(keyStoreType, keyStoreProvider);
        }

        if (!keyStorePath.isEmpty() && !NONE.equals(keyStorePath)) {
            try (FileInputStream fis = new FileInputStream(keyStorePath)) {
                keyStore.load(fis, keyStorePassword);
            } catch (FileNotFoundException e) {
                if (errorOnMissingFile) {
                    throw e;
                } else {
                    return null;
                }
            }
        } else {
            keyStore.load(null, keyStorePassword);
        }
        return keyStore;
    }

    private static String getDefaultSecurityPath(){
        return System.getProperty("java.home") + File.separator + "lib" + File.separator + "security";
    }

    private static String getDefaultTrustStore(){
        return getDefaultSecurityPath() + File.separator + "cacerts";
    }

    private static String getDefaultJsseTrustStore(){
        return getDefaultSecurityPath() + File.separator + "jssecacerts";
    }

    private static TrustManager[] getTrustManagers() throws Exception {
        String storePath = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStore", getDefaultJsseTrustStore());
        String storeType = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStoreType", KeyStore.getDefaultType());
        String storeProvider = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStoreProvider", "");
        String storePasswordString = System.getProperty("javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword", "");

        KeyStore keyStore = null;
        if (!NONE.equals(storePath)) {
            String[] fileNames = new String[]{storePath, getDefaultTrustStore()};
            for (String fileName : fileNames) {
                File candidate = new File(fileName);
                if (candidate.isFile() && candidate.canRead()) {
                    storePath = fileName;
                    break;
                } else if (!fileName.equals(getDefaultJsseTrustStore())) {
                    LOGGER.warn("Trust store file {} does not exist or is not readable. This may lead to SSL connection failures.", fileName);
                }
            }

            char[] storePassword = null;
            if (!storePasswordString.isEmpty()) {
                storePassword = storePasswordString.toCharArray();
            }

            keyStore = loadKeyStore(
                storePath,
                storeType,
                storeProvider,
                storePassword,
                false
            );
        }

        TrustManagerFactory trustManagerFactory = TrustManagerFactory.getInstance(TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm());
        trustManagerFactory.init(keyStore);

        return trustManagerFactory.getTrustManagers();
    }
}

Release signing:
In app/build.gradle.kts:
```kotlin
import java.util.Properties
import java.io.FileInputStream

val keystorePropertiesFile = rootProject.file("key.properties")
val keystoreProperties = Properties().apply {
    if (keystorePropertiesFile.exists()) FileInputStream(keystorePropertiesFile).use { load(it) }
}

fun signingValue(env: String, key: String, default: String? = null): String? =
    System.getenv(env) ?: keystoreProperties.getProperty(key) ?: default

android {
  signingConfigs {
    create("release") {
      val storePath = signingValue("SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PATH", "storeFile")
      if (storePath != null) {
        storeFile = file(storePath)
        storePassword = signingValue("SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD", "storePassword")
        keyAlias = signingValue("SAFAR_KEY_ALIAS", "keyAlias")
        keyPassword = signingValue("SAFAR_KEY_PASSWORD", "keyPassword")
      }
    }
  }
  buildTypes {
    release {
      val storePath = System.getenv("SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PATH") ?: keystoreProperties.getProperty("storeFile")
      signingConfig = if (storePath != null) signingConfigs.getByName("release") else null
    }
  }
}
```
If signingConfig null, AGP builds unsigned release APK/AAB (won't install). Better: fail with a clear message when a release task is requested and signing is missing. How to detect release build request in configuration? `gradle.startParameter.taskNames.any { it.contains("Release") }` in build.gradle.kts root or app. If missing, throw GradleException("Release signing not configured..."). That enforces "proper release signing" and prevents debug-signed releases. But `flutter build apk --release` invokes assembleRelease → taskNames includes assembleRelease. `flutter build appbundle --release` invokes bundleRelease. Good.

Env var names: SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PATH, SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, SAFAR_KEY_ALIAS, SAFAR_KEY_PASSWORD. key.properties format standard Flutter:
```
storeFile=...
storePassword=...
keyAlias=...
keyPassword=...
```
Note key.properties is gitignored. Store path may be relative to android/; `file(storePath)` resolves relative to app module (apps/mobile/android/app) — Flutter template uses `file(keystoreProperties['storeFile'])` which resolves relative to app dir. We can resolve relative to rootProject if not absolute. Keep standard behavior; document absolute path recommended.

Generate a local verification keystore at %LOCALAPPDATA%\SafarBuild\verification-release.jks with a random password (via keytool -genkeypair). Do NOT commit. Provide env vars during build. Document clearly that it is a local verification key and production must supply its own.

{
  "content": "from PIL import Image, ImageDraw\nimport os\n\nPAPER = (246, 241, 231, 255)\nEMBER = (176, 74, 8, 255)\nJADE = (10, 110, 102, 255)\nINK = (26, 24, 18, 255)\n\nOUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), \"res\")\n\ndef draw_mark(size, background=True, inset=0.0):\n    scale = 8\n    n = size * scale\n    img = Image.new(\"RGBA\", (n, n), PAPER if background else (0, 0, 0, 0))\n    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)\n    margin = int(n * (0.16 + inset))\n    sun_r = int(n * 0.185)\n    cx = n // 2\n    cy = int(n * 0.46)\n    d.ellipse([cx - sun_r, cy - sun_r, cx + sun_r, cy + sun_r], fill=EMBER)\n    # Paper notch: a small horizon cut inside the sun for depth.\n    notch_r = int(sun_r * 0.42)\n    d.ellipse(\n        [cx - sun_r + int(sun_r * 0.30), cy - notch_r, cx + sun_r - int(sun_r * 0.30), cy + notch_r],\n        fill=PAPER if background else (0, 0, 0, 0),\n    )\n    # Jade horizon line with rounded ends.\n    y = int(n * 0.70)\n    x0 = margin\n    x1 = n - margin\n    thickness = int(n * 0.045)\n    d.rounded_rectangle([x0, y - thickness // 2, x1, y + thickness // 2], radius=thickness // 2, fill=JADE)\n    # A small jade waypoint dot on the line.\n    dot_r = int(n * 0.035)\n    d.ellipse([cx - dot_r, y - dot_r, cx + dot_r, y + dot_r], fill=JADE)\n    return img.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)\n\nfor density, px in {\n    \"mipmap-mdpi\": 48,\n    \"mipmap-hdpi\": 72,\n    \"mipmap-xhdpi\": 96,\n    \"mipmap-xxhdpi\": 144,\n    \"mipmap-xxxhdpi\": 192,\n}.items():\n    path = os.path.join(OUT, density)\n    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)\n    draw_mark(px).save(os.path.join(path, \"ic_launcher.png\"))\n\npreview = draw_mark(1024)\npreview.save(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), \"icon-preview.png\"))\nprint(\"icons written\")\n",
  "file_path": "C:\\Users\\SIDDHA~1\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\safar_icon_gen.py"
}
```

import java.io.FileInputStream

val keystorePropertiesFile = rootProject.file("key.properties")

    if (keystorePropertiesFile.exists()) FileInputStream(keystorePropertiesFile).use { load(it) }
}

fun signingValue(environment: String, property: String): String? =
    System.getenv(environment)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
        ?: keystoreProperties.getProperty(property)?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }

val releaseStorePath = signingValue("SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PATH", "storeFile")
val releaseStorePassword = signingValue("SAFAR_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD", "storePassword")
val releaseKeyAlias = signingValue("SAFAR_KEY_ALIAS", "keyAlias")
val releaseKeyPassword = signingValue("SAFAR_KEY_PASSWORD", "keyPassword")
val hasReleaseSigning = listOf(releaseStorePath, releaseStorePassword, releaseKeyAlias, releaseKeyPassword).all { it != null }
```

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import os
import sys

PAPER = (246, 241, 231, 255)
EMBER = (176, 74, 8, 255)
JADE = (10, 110, 102, 255)
INK = (26, 24, 18, 255)

OUT = sys.argv[1]

def draw_mark(size, background=True, inset=0.0):
    scale = 8
    n = size * scale
    img = Image.new("RGBA", (n, n), PAPER if background else (0, 0, 0, 0))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    margin = int(n * (0.16 + inset))
    sun_r = int(n * 0.185)
    cx = n // 2
    cy = int(n * 0.46)
    d.ellipse([cx - sun_r, cy - sun_r, cx + sun_r, cy + sun_r], fill=EMBER)
    # Paper notch: a small horizon cut inside the sun for depth.
    notch_r = int(sun_r * 0.42)
    d.ellipse(
        [cx - sun_r + int(sun_r * 0.30), cy - notch_r, cx + sun_r - int(sun_r * 0.30), cy + notch_r],
        fill=PAPER if background else (0, 0, 0, 0),
    )
    # Jade horizon line with rounded ends.
    y = int(n * 0.70)
    x0 = margin
    x1 = n - margin
    thickness = int(n * 0.045)
    d.rounded_rectangle([x0, y - thickness // 2, x1, y + thickness // 2], radius=thickness // 2, fill=JADE)
    # A small jade waypoint dot on the line.
    dot_r = int(n * 0.035)
    d.ellipse([cx - dot_r, y - dot_r, cx + dot_r, y + dot_r], fill=JADE)
    return img.resize((size, size), Image.LANCZOS)

for density, px in {
    "mipmap-mdpi": 48,
    "mipmap-hdpi": 72,
    "mipmap-xhdpi": 96,
    "mipmap-xxhdpi": 144,
    "mipmap-xxxhdpi": 192,
}.items():
    path = os.path.join(OUT, density)
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    draw_mark(px).save(os.path.join(path, "ic_launcher.png"))

preview = draw_mark(1024)
preview.save(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "icon-preview.png"))
print("icons written")

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

/// Compile-time configuration. Secrets are never placed in the client.
class Env {
  static const String _definedBaseUrl = String.fromEnvironment(
    'SAFAR_API_BASE_URL',
  );

  /// Dev defaults are explicit and local. A release build must supply the URL
  /// with `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://...`.
  static String get apiBaseUrl {
    final raw = _definedBaseUrl.trim();
    if (raw.isNotEmpty) {
      return raw.endsWith('/') ? raw.substring(0, raw.length - 1) : raw;
    }
    if (kDebugMode) {
      // The Android emulator reaches the host machine through 10.0.2.2;
      // localhost there would be the emulator itself.
      if (!kIsWeb && defaultTargetPlatform == TargetPlatform.android) {
        return 'http://10.0.2.2:8010';
      }
      return 'http://localhost:8010';
    }
    throw StateError(
      'SAFAR_API_BASE_URL was not provided. Release builds must be compiled '
      'with --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host.',
    );
  }

  static const String _definedWebBaseUrl = String.fromEnvironment(
    'SAFAR_WEB_BASE_URL',
  );

  /// Origin of the web fallback that serves public companion pages such as
  /// `/companion/{token}`. Native app links are configured separately.
  static String? get webBaseUrl {
    final raw = _definedWebBaseUrl.trim();
    if (raw.isNotEmpty) {
      return raw.endsWith('/') ? raw.substring(0, raw.length - 1) : raw;
    }
    if (kDebugMode) return 'http://localhost:3000';
    return null;
  }

  static const String appName = 'SAFAR';
  static const String policyLabel = 'Private by default · group approved';
}

@router.get("/{trip_id}/members")
def list_members(
    trip_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    members = (
        db.query(TripMember)
        .filter(TripMember.trip_id == trip.id, TripMember.status == "active")
        .order_by(TripMember.joined_at)
        .all()
    )
    return {"items": [member_out(db, row, user.id) for row in members]}


@router.patch("/{trip_id}/members/me")
def update_my_membership(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: MemberSelfUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    for field, value in data.items():
        setattr(member, field, value)
    audit(
        db,
        action="member.update_self",
        entity_type="trip_member",
        entity_id=member.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"fields": list(data.keys())},
    )
    db.commit()
    return member_out(db, member, user.id)


@router.patch("/{trip_id}/members/{member_id}")
async def update_member_role(
    trip_id: str,
    member_id: str,
    payload: MemberRoleUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, actor = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    target = db.get(TripMember, member_id)
    if not target or target.trip_id != trip.id or target.status != "active":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Member not found")
    if target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Transfer ownership explicitly; it cannot be overwritten")
    if payload.role == "owner":
        if actor.role != "owner":
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Only the owner can transfer ownership")
        actor.role = "admin"
        target.role = "owner"
    else:
        if target.user_id == user.id:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="You cannot change your own role")
        target.role = payload.role
    audit(
        db,
        action="member.role_update",
        entity_type="trip_member",
        entity_id=target.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"role": payload.role},
    )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id,
        event_payload(
            "member.role_updated",
            trip_id=trip.id,
            member_id=target.id,
            role=target.role,
        ),
    )
    return member_out(db, target, user.id)


@router.delete("/{trip_id}/members/{member_id}")
async def remove_member(
    trip_id: str,
    member_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, actor = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    target = db.get(TripMember, member_id)
    if not target or target.trip_id != trip.id or target.status != "active":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Member not found")
    if target.id == actor.id and target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Transfer ownership to another member before leaving the trip.",
        )
    if target.id != actor.id and actor.role not in {"owner", "admin"}:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Only owners and admins can remove members")
    if target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="The owner cannot be removed")
    target.status = "left"
    audit(
        db,
        action="member.remove",
        entity_type="trip_member",
        entity_id=target.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
    )
    if target.user_id and target.id != actor.id:
        db.add(
            Notification(
                user_id=target.user_id,
                trip_id=trip.id,
                kind="member_removed",
                title=f"You were removed from {trip.name}",
                link=f"/dashboard",
            )
        )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id, event_payload("member.removed", trip_id=trip.id, member_id=target.id)
    )
    return {"ok": True}


@router.post("/{trip_id}/invitations", status_code=201)
def create_invitation(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: InviteCreate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
    invitation = TripInvitation(
        trip_id=trip.id,
        token=token,
        email=str(payload.email).lower() if payload.email else None,
        role=payload.role,
        scope=payload.scope,
        created_by=user.id,
        expires_at=utcnow() + timedelta(days=payload.expires_in_days),
    )
    db.add(invitation)
    audit(
        db,
        action="invitation.create",
        entity_type="trip_invitation",
        entity_id=invitation.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"role": payload.role, "scope": payload.scope},
    )
    db.commit()
    data = invitation_out(invitation, trip)
    data["path"] = f"/invite/{token}"
    return data


@router.get("/{trip_id}/invitations")
def list_invitations(
    trip_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    rows = (
        db.query(TripInvitation)
        .filter(TripInvitation.trip_id == trip.id)
        .order_by(TripInvitation.created_at.desc())
        .all()
    )
    now = utcnow()
    items = []
    for row in rows:
        data = invitation_out(row, trip)
        data["expired"] = bool(row.expires_at and row.expires_at < now)
        items.append(data)
    return {"items": items}


@router.delete("/{trip_id}/invitations/{invitation_id}")
def revoke_invitation(
    trip_id: str,
    invitation_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    invitation = db.get(TripInvitation, invitation_id)
    if not invitation or invitation.trip_id != trip.id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Invitation not found")
    db.delete(invitation)
    audit(
        db,
        action="invitation.revoke",
        entity_type="trip_invitation",
        entity_id=invitation_id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    return {"ok": True}
