1	# SAFAR — Flutter client (`apps/mobile`)
2	
3	The Flutter client for SAFAR. It talks directly to the existing FastAPI
4	backend in `services/api`; the API remains the only place where business rules,
5	authorisation, AI/ML inference and privacy filtering live. There is no mock
6	API layer and no client-side recommendation logic.
7	
8	Status: all 49 features have an API-backed Flutter surface (Phase 9,
9	2026-11-20); 47 are complete and 2 are partial (F04 invitation/member admin and
10	F10 basemap tiles remain web-only). See
11	[`docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md`](../../docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md) for the
12	screen-by-screen and feature-by-feature status.
13	
14	## Requirements
15	
16	- Flutter 3.41+ (stable) with Dart 3.11+
17	- Android SDK 36 for Android builds
18	- Xcode 15+ on macOS for iOS builds
19	- A running SAFAR API (see the repository README)
20	
21	## Configure the API address
22	
23	The base URL is compile-time configuration, never a hardcoded production value.
24	
25	| Target | Command / default |
26	|---|---|
27	| Android emulator | Debug default `http://10.0.2.2:8010` (the emulator's alias for the host) |
28	| iOS simulator | Debug default `http://localhost:8010` |
29	| Physical device | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://<host-lan-ip>:8010` and add that host to the API `TRUSTED_HOSTS` |
30	| Production | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host` (required; a release build without it fails fast) |
31	
32	Debug builds allow cleartext HTTP on Android through
33	`android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`. Release builds require HTTPS and
34	the main manifest declares `android.permission.INTERNET`.
35	
36	## Run
37	
38	```bash
39	cd apps/mobile
40	flutter pub get
41	flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8010   # Android
42	flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010  # iOS simulator
43	```
44	
45	### Web verification target
46	
47	There is no production web target; the browser build exists only for visual
48	verification in environments without an emulator.
49	
50	```bash
51	# API with the web origin allowed and a seeded database
52	CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080 python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8010
53	
54	cd apps/mobile
55	flutter run -d web-server --web-port=8080 \
56	  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010
57	```
58	
59	On web the client uses `BrowserHttpClientAdapter(withCredentials: true)` so the
60	browser stores and sends the HttpOnly cookies. Native builds persist the cookie
61	jar in Keychain / encrypted preferences instead. Never add the web origin to a
62	production CORS list unless the deployment truly serves a browser client.
63	
64	## Session model
65	
66	- Login/register return an access token, a CSRF token and three cookies:
67	  `safar_access` (HttpOnly, 15 min, `/`), `safar_refresh` (HttpOnly, 30 days,
68	  `/api/auth`) and `safar_csrf` (readable, `/`).
69	- Native: `SafarCookieJar` stores cookies in `flutter_secure_storage` and
70	  `CookieManager` attaches them. The refresh cookie survives app restarts;
71	  access and CSRF tokens stay in memory only.
72	- Web: the browser owns the cookies.
73	- Requests send `Authorization: Bearer` plus `X-CSRF-Token` for unsafe methods.
74	  Cookie-only unsafe requests without CSRF are rejected by the API (403).
75	- A 401 triggers one single-flight `POST /api/auth/refresh`, a token rotation
76	  and an automatic retry. A failed refresh clears the local session and sends
77	  the user to sign-in. Logout calls the API (revoking the session server-side)
78	  and clears local state even if the call fails.
79	- No secrets are bundled in the app; only the public API base URL is configured.
80	
81	## Architecture
82	
83	```
84	lib/
85	  main.dart
86	  app/            app root, GoRouter, deep-link listener, bottom-navigation shell
87	  core/
88	    config/       compile-time environment (API base URL, web base URL)
89	    network/      Dio client, auth interceptor, persisted cookie jar, errors
90	    storage/      JsonStore abstraction, device-local offline capture queue
91	    models/       typed immutable models with explicit fromJson
92	    repositories/ one per domain; transport only, no business rules
93	    realtime/     ticket-authenticated trip WebSocket, dedupe, reconnect
94	    native/       share sheet and deep-link parsing helpers
95	    theme/        SAFAR design tokens and Material 3 theme (light/dark)
96	    widgets/      shared cards, buttons, headers, chips, states, skeletons
97	    utils/        date, time, currency and text formatting
98	  features/
99	    auth/         splash, onboarding, login, register, session controller
100	    home/         dashboard
101	    discover/     destinations, destination detail, place detail + crowd forecast
102	    trips/        trip list and creation
103	    trip/         overview, itinerary, engine, proposals, expenses, pulse,
104	                  rescue, memories, studio, replay, import, pact, twin,
105	                  negotiate, plan intelligence, opportunity, branches, nearby,
106	                  ground, missions, tasks, watch, companion, offline, circles,
107	                  contributors, connections, thread, More hub
108	    companion/    public One-Link Companion responder
109	    assistant/    grounded travel assistant
110	    profile/      profile, settings, consents, notifications
111	```
112	
113	State: Riverpod 2.6.1 (`StateNotifier` for the session, `FutureProvider.family`
114	for reads, `ref.invalidate` after mutations). Routing: GoRouter with an auth
115	gate and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar (Home, Discover, Trips, Ask, You).
116	HTTP: a single Dio instance with an auth interceptor, timeouts (12 s connect,
117	45 s receive) and typed `ApiException`s.
118	
119	## Real-time trips
120	
121	Each open trip holds one WebSocket. The client requests a 120-second ticket
122	from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`, then connects to
123	`GET /ws/trips/{trip_id}?token=<ticket>`. Events for itinerary, proposals,
124	expenses, engine, pulse, members and the trip itself invalidate the matching
125	Riverpod providers. The channel reconnects with exponential backoff
126	(1/2/4/8/15/30 s), pauses while the app is in the background, dedupes repeated
127	frames and re-fetches all trip-scoped providers after a reconnection.
128	Pull-to-refresh and post-mutation invalidation still work without the socket.
129	The Live/Reconnecting chip appears on the trip overview, itinerary and
130	decisions screens.
131	
132	## Native capabilities
133	
134	| Capability | Behaviour |
135	|---|---|
136	| Companion deep links | `safar://companion/<token>` and `https://<web-host>/companion/<token>` open the public responder. Android intent filter and iOS URL type are declared. |
137	| Share | The companion link and CSV expense export use the platform share sheet. |
138	| Photos | Memory photos come from the camera or library only when the user taps Add photo; 25 MB cap, scaled to 1600 px. |
139	| Location | Nearby can use the current position only when the profile's location-sharing consent is on; otherwise the trip base is used. Permission is requested only on tap. |
140	| Offline | Offline captures are stored on the device and synced idempotently when back online. |
141	
142	Push notifications are not implemented because the backend has no APNs/FCM
143	deliverer; in-app notifications remain the supported channel.
144	
145	## Tests
146	
147	```bash
148	flutter analyze
149	flutter test                                   # 25 passed, live suite skipped
150	SAFAR_LIVE_API=http://localhost:8010 \
151	  flutter test                                  # adds the 7 live API tests
152	```
153	
154	The live suite needs a seeded database. It performs roughly ten auth calls, so
155	give the verification instance headroom, for example
156	`AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100`. It covers login, refresh-cookie persistence
157	across restarts, transparent token refresh with rotation, logout revocation,
158	CSRF rejection of cookie-only writes, wrong credentials and network failure.
159	`test/phase9_test.dart` covers the realtime envelope/URL/backoff, companion
160	deep links, watch value rendering, companion context parsing and the offline
161	queue.
162	
163	## Builds
164	
165	```bash
166	flutter build apk --debug
167	flutter build appbundle --release \
168	  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host
169	```
170	
171	iOS builds require macOS with Xcode: `flutter build ios --release`.
172	
173	## Troubleshooting “Failed to fetch”
174	
175	This error is the browser’s generic network failure; it is not a Flutter
176	exception. The causes found during Phase 8 were:
177	
178	1. The web build called `http://localhost:8000` while the API ran on `:8010`.
179	   Fix: pass `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL` matching the running API.
180	2. The API’s CORS list did not include the Flutter web origin, so the browser
181	   blocked the response. Fix: add the exact origin to `CORS_ORIGINS` (native
182	   apps are unaffected by CORS).
183	3. An Android emulator using `localhost` reached itself instead of the host.
184	   Fix: use `10.0.2.2` (now the debug default) or the LAN IP for a device.
185	4. A plain-HTTP API on Android release builds. The debug overlay permits
186	   cleartext for local development; release must use HTTPS.
187	
188	If the Android build fails while downloading Maven dependencies with
189	`PKIX path building failed`, a TLS-scanning product (for example Avast Web
190	Shield) is intercepting HTTPS and the JDK does not trust its root. Options are
191	to trust that root in a build-only truststore (a security decision that needs
192	explicit approval), temporarily pause TLS scanning, or build on a host without
193	interception. Do not disable TLS verification.
194

"""Local XYZ tile server used only to verify SAFAR's slippy-map layer.

Run:  python safar_tile_server.py 8000
Then: adb reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000
and build Flutter with
  --dart-define=SAFAR_MAP_TILE_URL=http://localhost:8000/{z}/{x}/{y}.png
"""

import io
import math
import sys
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

CACHE = {}
SIZE = 256

PAPER = (246, 241, 231)
GRID = (227, 218, 201)
INK = (26, 24, 18)
MUTED = (115, 107, 92)
JADE = (10, 110, 102)
EMBER = (176, 74, 8)


def tile_png(z: int, x: int, y: int) -> bytes:
    key = (z, x, y)
    if key in CACHE:
        return CACHE[key]
    img = Image.new("RGB", (SIZE, SIZE), PAPER)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    # A pale checker plus grid so neighbouring tiles are visually distinct.
    level = z % 3
    tint = [(248, 244, 235), (242, 238, 227), (238, 233, 220)][level]
    for cx in range(0, SIZE, 64):
        for cy in range(0, SIZE, 64):
            if (cx // 64 + cy // 64) % 2 == 0:
                d.rectangle([cx, cy, cx + 63, cy + 63], fill=tint)
    for k in range(0, SIZE + 1, 64):
        d.line([(k, 0), (k, SIZE)], fill=GRID)
        d.line([(0, k), (SIZE, k)], fill=GRID)
    d.rectangle([0, 0, SIZE - 1, SIZE - 1], outline=(214, 204, 186))
    # A stylised "river" that varies with the tile index.
    wave = int(30 * math.sin((x + z) * 0.9))
    d.line(
        [(0, 128 + wave), (64, 120 + wave), (128, 140 + wave), (192, 118 + wave), (SIZE, 132 + wave)],
        fill=(188, 214, 208),
        width=10,
    )
    d.line(
        [(0, 128 + wave), (64, 120 + wave), (128, 140 + wave), (192, 118 + wave), (SIZE, 132 + wave)],
        fill=(150, 190, 182),
        width=2,
    )
    try:
        font = ImageFont.truetype("arial.ttf", 18)
        small = ImageFont.truetype("arial.ttf", 12)
    except OSError:
        font = ImageFont.load_default()

If the stored refresh token is stale because the *server* rotated it on a previous refresh and the client failed to persist the new one after a crash... rotate-on-refresh means a crash between server rotation and local persist → old token revoked → forced login. This could be exactly what happened when the emulator died mid-run (app had performed refreshes).

This is worth noting for docs: single-use refresh rotation combined with an abrupt process kill can force re-login; that's expected security behavior, not data loss (captures are device-local in JsonStore; unsynced captures persist).

client surface to Flutter (`apps/mobile`) without changing any backend route,
schema, service or migration. The Next.js app stays available as reference and
fallback. Method, evidence and limitations: `docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §8.

(a named capability is still web-only) · **W** web-only · **B** blocked.

### 8.9 Remaining limitations

1. F04 invitations/member admin and F10 basemap tiles remain web-only.
2. No Android or iOS binary was produced (environment TLS interception; no
   macOS). Plugin native code is therefore not compile-verified on a device.
3. No emulator/simulator was available: real-time behaviour is covered by
   transport unit tests and API-level checks, not on-device socket drops.
4. WS delivery is in-process (single API instance); multi-instance fan-out is
   unchanged from the backend design.
5. Push notifications are unavailable (no deliverer configured).

Design system reference: `docs/UI_DESIGN.md` (tokens in `app/globals.css` and

### 2.1 Flutter client (`apps/mobile`)

```
apps/mobile/lib/
  app/            GoRouter (auth gate, StatefulShellRoute bottom bar), root
  core/
    config/       compile-time API base URL (no production localhost default)
    network/      Dio, auth interceptor, SafarCookieJar, ApiException
    storage/      JsonStore abstraction (secure storage / in-memory tests)
    models/       typed immutable models with explicit fromJson
    repositories/ per-domain transport only
    theme/        SAFAR tokens + Material 3 light/dark
    widgets/      shared primitives and states
  features/       auth · home · discover · trips · trip · assistant · profile
```

- **State**: Riverpod 2.6 (`StateNotifier` session controller,
  `FutureProvider.family` reads, invalidation after mutations).
- **Auth**: native persists only the cookie jar (Keychain on iOS, encrypted
  preferences on Android); access and CSRF tokens are memory-only. Web
  verification uses `withCredentials` so the browser owns the HttpOnly cookies.
  A 401 triggers one single-flight refresh, token rotation and one retry; a
  rejected refresh signs the user out. Logout revokes the session server-side.
- **Boundary**: the Dart layer ranks nothing, extracts nothing, forecasts
  nothing and filters no privacy data. It submits requests and renders labels,
  sources and confidence exactly as the API returns them.
- **Realtime**: one ticket-authenticated WebSocket per open trip
  (`POST /api/auth/ws-ticket` → `/ws/trips/{id}?token=`), with exponential
  backoff, event dedupe, lifecycle pause/resume and a catch-up invalidation on
  reconnect. Pull-to-refresh and post-mutation refresh remain the fallback.
- **Platforms**: Android and iOS are the primary targets; a Flutter web build
  is used only as a visual verification target where no emulator exists.
- Migration status, test evidence and remaining gaps:
  `docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md` §8.

platform matrix and troubleshooting):

```bash
cd apps/mobile
flutter pub get
flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8010   # Android emulator
flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010  # iOS simulator
```

The base URL is compile-time configuration. Debug builds default to the host
address for the emulator (`10.0.2.2` on Android, `localhost` elsewhere); release
builds must pass `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL` and fail fast without it.

Production build:

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 npm run build
npm run start        # http://localhost:3000
```

# SAFAR — Flutter client (`apps/mobile`)

The Flutter client for SAFAR. It talks directly to the existing FastAPI
backend in `services/api`; the API remains the only place where business rules,
authorisation, AI/ML inference and privacy filtering live. There is no mock
API layer and no client-side recommendation logic.

Status: all 49 features have an API-backed Flutter surface (Phase 9,
2026-11-20); 47 are complete and 2 are partial (F04 invitation/member admin and
F10 basemap tiles remain web-only). See
[`docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md`](../../docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md) for the
screen-by-screen and feature-by-feature status.

## Requirements

- Flutter 3.41+ (stable) with Dart 3.11+
- Android SDK 36 for Android builds
- Xcode 15+ on macOS for iOS builds
- A running SAFAR API (see the repository README)

## Configure the API address

The base URL is compile-time configuration, never a hardcoded production value.

| Target | Command / default |
|---|---|
| Android emulator | Debug default `http://10.0.2.2:8010` (the emulator's alias for the host) |
| iOS simulator | Debug default `http://localhost:8010` |
| Physical device | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://<host-lan-ip>:8010` and add that host to the API `TRUSTED_HOSTS` |
| Production | `--dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host` (required; a release build without it fails fast) |

Debug builds allow cleartext HTTP on Android through
`android/app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`. Release builds require HTTPS and
the main manifest declares `android.permission.INTERNET`.

## Run

```bash
cd apps/mobile
flutter pub get
flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8010   # Android
flutter run --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010  # iOS simulator
```

### Web verification target

There is no production web target; the browser build exists only for visual
verification in environments without an emulator.

```bash
# API with the web origin allowed and a seeded database
CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8080 python -m uvicorn app.main:app --port 8010

cd apps/mobile
flutter run -d web-server --web-port=8080 \
  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010
```

On web the client uses `BrowserHttpClientAdapter(withCredentials: true)` so the
browser stores and sends the HttpOnly cookies. Native builds persist the cookie
jar in Keychain / encrypted preferences instead. Never add the web origin to a
production CORS list unless the deployment truly serves a browser client.

## Session model

- Login/register return an access token, a CSRF token and three cookies:
  `safar_access` (HttpOnly, 15 min, `/`), `safar_refresh` (HttpOnly, 30 days,
  `/api/auth`) and `safar_csrf` (readable, `/`).
- Native: `SafarCookieJar` stores cookies in `flutter_secure_storage` and
  `CookieManager` attaches them. The refresh cookie survives app restarts;
  access and CSRF tokens stay in memory only.
- Web: the browser owns the cookies.
- Requests send `Authorization: Bearer` plus `X-CSRF-Token` for unsafe methods.
  Cookie-only unsafe requests without CSRF are rejected by the API (403).
- A 401 triggers one single-flight `POST /api/auth/refresh`, a token rotation
  and an automatic retry. A failed refresh clears the local session and sends
  the user to sign-in. Logout calls the API (revoking the session server-side)
  and clears local state even if the call fails.
- No secrets are bundled in the app; only the public API base URL is configured.

## Architecture

```
lib/
  main.dart
  app/            app root, GoRouter, deep-link listener, bottom-navigation shell
  core/
    config/       compile-time environment (API base URL, web base URL)
    network/      Dio client, auth interceptor, persisted cookie jar, errors
    storage/      JsonStore abstraction, device-local offline capture queue
    models/       typed immutable models with explicit fromJson
    repositories/ one per domain; transport only, no business rules
    realtime/     ticket-authenticated trip WebSocket, dedupe, reconnect
    native/       share sheet and deep-link parsing helpers
    theme/        SAFAR design tokens and Material 3 theme (light/dark)
    widgets/      shared cards, buttons, headers, chips, states, skeletons
    utils/        date, time, currency and text formatting
  features/
    auth/         splash, onboarding, login, register, session controller
    home/         dashboard
    discover/     destinations, destination detail, place detail + crowd forecast
    trips/        trip list and creation
    trip/         overview, itinerary, engine, proposals, expenses, pulse,
                  rescue, memories, studio, replay, import, pact, twin,
                  negotiate, plan intelligence, opportunity, branches, nearby,
                  ground, missions, tasks, watch, companion, offline, circles,
                  contributors, connections, thread, More hub
    companion/    public One-Link Companion responder
    assistant/    grounded travel assistant
    profile/      profile, settings, consents, notifications
```

State: Riverpod 2.6.1 (`StateNotifier` for the session, `FutureProvider.family`
for reads, `ref.invalidate` after mutations). Routing: GoRouter with an auth
gate and a `StatefulShellRoute` bottom bar (Home, Discover, Trips, Ask, You).
HTTP: a single Dio instance with an auth interceptor, timeouts (12 s connect,
45 s receive) and typed `ApiException`s.

## Real-time trips

Each open trip holds one WebSocket. The client requests a 120-second ticket
from `POST /api/auth/ws-ticket`, then connects to
`GET /ws/trips/{trip_id}?token=<ticket>`. Events for itinerary, proposals,
expenses, engine, pulse, members and the trip itself invalidate the matching
Riverpod providers. The channel reconnects with exponential backoff
(1/2/4/8/15/30 s), pauses while the app is in the background, dedupes repeated
frames and re-fetches all trip-scoped providers after a reconnection.
Pull-to-refresh and post-mutation invalidation still work without the socket.
The Live/Reconnecting chip appears on the trip overview, itinerary and
decisions screens.

## Native capabilities

| Capability | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Companion deep links | `safar://companion/<token>` and `https://<web-host>/companion/<token>` open the public responder. Android intent filter and iOS URL type are declared. |
| Share | The companion link and CSV expense export use the platform share sheet. |
| Photos | Memory photos come from the camera or library only when the user taps Add photo; 25 MB cap, scaled to 1600 px. |
| Location | Nearby can use the current position only when the profile's location-sharing consent is on; otherwise the trip base is used. Permission is requested only on tap. |
| Offline | Offline captures are stored on the device and synced idempotently when back online. |

Push notifications are not implemented because the backend has no APNs/FCM
deliverer; in-app notifications remain the supported channel.

## Tests

```bash
flutter analyze
flutter test                                   # 25 passed, live suite skipped
SAFAR_LIVE_API=http://localhost:8010 \
  flutter test                                  # adds the 7 live API tests
```

The live suite needs a seeded database. It performs roughly ten auth calls, so
give the verification instance headroom, for example
`AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=100`. It covers login, refresh-cookie persistence
across restarts, transparent token refresh with rotation, logout revocation,
CSRF rejection of cookie-only writes, wrong credentials and network failure.
`test/phase9_test.dart` covers the realtime envelope/URL/backoff, companion
deep links, watch value rendering, companion context parsing and the offline
queue.

## Builds

```bash
flutter build apk --debug
flutter build appbundle --release \
  --dart-define=SAFAR_API_BASE_URL=https://your-api-host
```

iOS builds require macOS with Xcode: `flutter build ios --release`.

## Troubleshooting “Failed to fetch”

This error is the browser’s generic network failure; it is not a Flutter
exception. The causes found during Phase 8 were:

1. The web build called `http://localhost:8000` while the API ran on `:8010`.
   Fix: pass `SAFAR_API_BASE_URL` matching the running API.
2. The API’s CORS list did not include the Flutter web origin, so the browser
   blocked the response. Fix: add the exact origin to `CORS_ORIGINS` (native
   apps are unaffected by CORS).
3. An Android emulator using `localhost` reached itself instead of the host.
   Fix: use `10.0.2.2` (now the debug default) or the LAN IP for a device.
4. A plain-HTTP API on Android release builds. The debug overlay permits
   cleartext for local development; release must use HTTPS.

If the Android build fails while downloading Maven dependencies with
`PKIX path building failed`, a TLS-scanning product (for example Avast Web
Shield) is intercepting HTTPS and the JDK does not trust its root. Options are
to trust that root in a build-only truststore (a security decision that needs
explicit approval), temporarily pause TLS scanning, or build on a host without
interception. Do not disable TLS verification.

## 8. Production readiness assessment

Honest verdict: **the application is security-hardened and PostgreSQL-ready,
but not production-certified.** The core controls are implemented and tested;
the unverified items are deployment-path items that require Docker, TLS and an
external review.

| Area | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Session/auth security | **Ready** | HttpOnly cookies, rotation, reuse detection, revocation, CSRF, session checks; tests + browser evidence |
| Authorization (API) | **Ready** | 121 paths exercised across phases; private trips 404 for outsiders; admin gating; mass-assignment and IDOR tests |
| Database isolation (RLS) | **Ready on PG** | 220 policies, FORCE RLS, fail-closed; direct SQL probes and a full suite as the non-owner role |
| Privacy & user control | **Ready with limits** | Consent, export, erasure, retention, location toggle, memory permissions, blocking/reporting; no analytics pipeline ships, so no analytics-PII path exists |
| Uploads & input handling | **Ready** | Magic-byte checks, 25 MB cap, validated schemas, no SQL injection or 5xx on malicious probes |
| Secrets & configuration | **Ready** | No committed secrets (repo has no commits); env-only configuration; production guards for `SECRET_KEY`, CORS, cookies, docs, seeding; accurate `.env.example` |
| Logging & monitoring | **Conditional** | Structured JSON, request ids, redaction and error hook exist; no monitor/log sink is configured in this environment |
| Rate limiting / abuse | **Conditional** | Per-bucket limits and `Retry-After` work; single-process only (R5) |
| Backup & recovery | **Conditional** | Logical dump/restore verified end to end; no PITR and no Docker-volume drill (R9) |
| Infrastructure (Docker/CI) | **Not verified** | Images not built here (R2); CI/CD steps documented but not executed |
| TLS / proxy / HSTS | **Not verified** | Plain HTTP localhost only (R3) |
| Scale / performance | **Not verified** | No load testing (R7) |
| External security review | **Not performed** | R1 |

**Conditions for a public deployment**

1. Build and smoke-test the images with Docker, non-root users and the
   `alembic upgrade head` startup step.
2. Terminate TLS at a proxy; set `ENVIRONMENT=production`, a 32+ character
   `SECRET_KEY`, explicit `CORS_ORIGINS`/`TRUSTED_HOSTS`,
   `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true`, `SAFAR_SEED=false`.
3. Run the database as the non-owner `safar_app` role and apply
   `d9e4f1b2c305`; verify `SELECT count(*) FROM trips` is 0 with no context.
4. Schedule the retention job and backups; test a restore into a clean
   database.
5. Put rate limiting at the gateway if more than one API instance runs.
6. Attach an error monitor and log sink.
7. Commission an external penetration test and a small load test before
   opening registration.

Until those are done, the correct claim is “hardened and verified on this
environment”, not “production ready”.

### 9. Remaining limitations

1. AOSP LatinIME can hold a stale back callback and swallow the first BACK; force-stopping the IME resets it. Emulator image bug.
2. `geolocator` can block in `NmeaClient.stop` on this GMS-less API 36 image and trigger an ANR; Nearby recovers after its timeout. A Play-services device is the recommended location target.
3. Host emulator crashed twice; final rebuild not reinstalled post-crash.
4. An abrupt kill during refresh-token rotation can force a fresh sign-in (single-use refresh replay protection), not data loss.
5. Release artifacts use a throwaway verification key; production needs the real upload key.
6. iOS was not built (no macOS host).
7. Live suite stays opt-in; push notifications are not implemented.
8. Map tiles were verified against a local test tile server; production provider terms/credentials are not bundled.

# PHASE 11 — SAFAR FINAL PRODUCT-WIDE VALIDATION & RELEASE READINESS

SAFAR has completed Phases 1–10. The Flutter migration is complete according to the feature registry (49 complete, 0 partial), Android debug and release builds have been generated, and the automated test suites are passing.

Now begin Phase 11.

## PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Perform a complete product-wide audit of SAFAR and bring the existing application to a reliable, release-ready state.

This phase is about VALIDATION, BUG FIXING, INTEGRATION, PERFORMANCE, SECURITY AND RELEASE PREPARATION.

Do not unnecessarily add new features. Do not redesign working screens. Do not replace real implementations with mock data. Preserve the existing architecture and functionality.

## STEP 1 — COMPLETE FEATURE VALIDATION

Inspect all 49 features (F01–F49) using:

- docs/FEATURE_REGISTRY.md
- docs/FLUTTER_MIGRATION_PLAN.md
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- Backend API documentation and implementation
- Flutter screens, repositories and services

For every feature, verify:

1. The UI is connected to the correct backend endpoint.
2. Data is loaded from the actual database.
3. Create, read, update and delete operations work wherever applicable.
4. Loading, empty, error and success states work.
5. Authentication and authorization are enforced.
6. Data remains consistent after navigation and app restart.
7. The feature works with other related features.

Create a feature validation matrix with evidence for every feature.

Do not mark a feature complete simply because its screen exists.

## STEP 2 — END-TO-END WORKFLOW TESTING

Test complete user journeys, not isolated API calls.

Include:

- User registration, login, session restoration and logout.
- Discovering destinations and creating a trip.
- Inviting members and managing permissions.
- Collaborative itinerary creation and editing.
- Group Experience Engine recommendation and decision-making.
- Voting and proposal approval.
- Group expense creation and settlement.
- Journey DNA and personalised recommendations.
- Memory creation, Dream Import, Memory Studio and Journey Replay.
- Trip Twin, Trip Rescue and Plan Intelligence.
- Travel Circles, Missions, Tasks, Watch and Companions.
- Nearby places, location consent and map interactions.
- Offline capture, reconnection and synchronization.
- Ground requests, Opportunity Clock and other planning tools.

Test successful, unsuccessful, duplicate and conflicting operations.

## STEP 3 — MULTI-USER AND CONCURRENCY TESTING

Use multiple independent test accounts.

Verify:

- Multiple users editing the same trip.
- Simultaneous votes and proposal updates.
- Invitation acceptance and revocation.
- Role changes and member removal.
- Concurrent expense updates.
- WebSocket synchronization.
- Duplicate offline synchronization.
- Conflicting itinerary changes.
- Unauthorized access to another user's trips and memories.

Check for race conditions, duplicate records, stale data and inconsistent state.

## STEP 4 — SECURITY AND PRIVACY REGRESSION

Revalidate the security work completed in Phase 5.

Test:

- Session expiry and refresh-token rotation.
- Logout and token revocation.
- CSRF protection.
- PostgreSQL FORCE RLS and tenant isolation.
- File upload validation.
- Rate limiting.
- Data export and deletion.
- Location-sharing consent and expiry.
- Private-by-default trips and memories.
- Social connection consent.
- Sensitive information in logs and API responses.

Do not weaken existing security controls to make tests pass.

## STEP 5 — PERFORMANCE AND RELIABILITY

Measure actual performance.

Investigate:

- Slow API endpoints.
- Slow database queries.
- Unnecessary repeated API requests.
- Large image and media loading.
- Excessive Flutter widget rebuilds.
- Memory consumption.
- Long-running background operations.
- WebSocket reconnection behaviour.
- Offline queue reliability.

Run realistic concurrent API tests where the environment permits.

Record actual measurements. Do not invent performance numbers.

## STEP 6 — FLUTTER UI AND DEVICE VALIDATION

Audit every major screen on the Flutter application.

Test:

- Small and large Android screen sizes.
- Different text scaling settings.
- Light and dark themes.
- Keyboard and system navigation.
- Loading, error and empty states.
- Forms and validation.
- Scroll behaviour.
- Back navigation.
- Accessibility and touch target sizes.

Check that the app does not overflow, freeze or crash.

Do not claim physical-device verification if only an emulator was used.

## STEP 7 — PRODUCTION CONFIGURATION

Review:

- Environment variables.
- API base URL configuration.
- Database configuration.
- CORS and trusted hosts.
- HTTPS and secure cookies.
- Map tile provider configuration and attribution.
- Media storage.
- Backup and restoration.
- Logging and monitoring.
- Rate limiting across multiple workers.
- Production secrets and signing configuration.

Clearly identify what is implemented and what still requires external infrastructure.

Never commit real credentials, signing keys or API secrets.

The temporary Phase 10 verification signing key must NOT be treated as the production upload key.

## STEP 8 — FINAL RELEASE VALIDATION

After fixing verified issues:

Run:

- flutter analyze
- flutter test
- Backend pytest
- Flutter web release build
- Android debug APK build
- Android release APK build
- Android AAB build

Run the live API test suite where configured.

Do not count skipped tests as passed.

Verify APK/AAB signatures and release configuration. Do not claim production signing unless the actual production upload key is used.

## STRICT RULES

- Inspect before changing.
- Fix root causes rather than hiding symptoms.
- Do not fabricate test results.
- Do not silently skip failing tests.
- Do not remove existing features to make tests pass.
- Do not introduce mock implementations.
- Preserve backward compatibility wherever possible.
- Do not deploy publicly or publish an app without explicit authorization.
- Keep documentation aligned with the actual implementation.

import os
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

API_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
REPO_ROOT = API_DIR.parents[1]

load_dotenv(API_DIR / ".env")
load_dotenv(REPO_ROOT / ".env")


def _bool(name: str, default: bool) -> bool:
    raw = os.getenv(name)
    if raw is None:
        return default
    return raw.strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}


class Settings:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        default_db = f"sqlite:///{(API_DIR / 'safar.db').as_posix()}"
        self.database_url: str = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", default_db)
        self.environment: str = os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "development")
        default_secret = "safar-dev-secret-change-me-in-production"
        self.secret_key: str = os.getenv("SECRET_KEY", default_secret)
        if self.environment == "production" and (
            self.secret_key == default_secret or len(self.secret_key) < 32
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(
                "SECRET_KEY must be set to a unique value of at least 32 characters in production."
            )
        self.access_token_expire_minutes: int = int(
            os.getenv("ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES", "15")
        )
        self.refresh_token_expire_days: int = int(
            os.getenv("REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS", "30")
        )
        self.cookie_secure: bool = _bool("COOKIE_SECURE", self.environment == "production")
        self.cookie_samesite: str = os.getenv("COOKIE_SAMESITE", "lax").strip().lower()
        if self.cookie_samesite not in {"lax", "strict", "none"}:
            raise RuntimeError("COOKIE_SAMESITE must be one of: lax, strict, none")
        if self.cookie_samesite == "none" and not self.cookie_secure:
            raise RuntimeError("COOKIE_SAMESITE=none requires COOKIE_SECURE=true")
        self.cookie_domain: str | None = os.getenv("COOKIE_DOMAIN") or None
        self.access_cookie = "safar_access"
        self.refresh_cookie = "safar_refresh"
        self.csrf_cookie = "safar_csrf"
        self.csrf_header = "X-CSRF-Token"
        self.request_id_header = "X-Request-Id"
        # 10.0.2.2 is the Android emulator's alias for the host machine.
        self.trusted_hosts = [
            host.strip()
            for host in os.getenv(
                "TRUSTED_HOSTS", "localhost,127.0.0.1,testserver,10.0.2.2"
            ).split(",")
            if host.strip()
        ]
        self.max_request_bytes: int = int(os.getenv("MAX_REQUEST_BYTES", "26214400"))
        self.log_level: str = os.getenv("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO").upper()
        self.release: str = os.getenv("RELEASE", "safar-1.0.0")
        self.sentry_dsn: str | None = os.getenv("SENTRY_DSN") or None
        self.trust_proxy_headers: bool = _bool("TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS", False)
        self.api_docs_enabled: bool = _bool(
            "ENABLE_API_DOCS", self.environment != "production"
        )
        self.auth_rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(
            os.getenv("AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE", "10")
        )
        self.companion_rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(
            os.getenv("COMPANION_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE", "20")
        )
        self.upload_rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(
            os.getenv("UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE", "30")
        )
        origins = os.getenv("CORS_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:3000")
        self.cors_origins = [o.strip() for o in origins.split(",") if o.strip()]
        if self.environment == "production" and "*" in self.cors_origins:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "CORS_ORIGINS must list explicit origins in production; '*' is not allowed "
                "because cookie authentication requires credentials."
            )
        # The OpenAI settings are intentionally inert. No service reads them;
        # wiring an LLM requires a separate change and explicit approval.
        self.openai_api_key: str | None = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") or None
        self.openai_model: str = os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini")
        # Optional providers. Everything defaults to off or local so the
        # default deployment makes no outbound AI calls.
        self.weather_provider: str = os.getenv(
            "SAFAR_WEATHER_PROVIDER", "disabled"
        ).strip().lower()
        if self.weather_provider not in {"disabled", "open-meteo"}:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "SAFAR_WEATHER_PROVIDER must be 'disabled' or 'open-meteo'."
            )
        self.link_fetch_enabled: bool = _bool("SAFAR_LINK_FETCH_ENABLED", False)
        self.ocr_enabled: bool = _bool("SAFAR_OCR_ENABLED", True)
        self.provider_timeout_seconds: float = float(
            os.getenv("SAFAR_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", "3")
        )
        self.link_cache_ttl_seconds: int = int(
            os.getenv("SAFAR_LINK_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS", "900")
        )
        self.weather_cache_ttl_seconds: int = int(
            os.getenv("SAFAR_WEATHER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS", "1800")
        )
        self.link_rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(

        )
        self.weather_rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(

        )
        self.ocr_max_image_bytes: int = int(
            os.getenv("SAFAR_OCR_MAX_IMAGE_BYTES", "10485760")
        )
        self.auto_seed: bool = _bool("SAFAR_SEED", self.environment != "production")
        self.create_schema: bool = _bool("SAFAR_CREATE_SCHEMA", self.environment != "production")
        self.rate_limit_per_minute: int = int(os.getenv("RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE", "240"))
        self.retention_session_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_SESSION_DAYS", "30"))
        self.retention_invitation_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_INVITATION_DAYS", "30"))
        self.retention_companion_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_COMPANION_DAYS", "30"))
        self.retention_notification_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_NOTIFICATION_DAYS", "180"))
        self.retention_audit_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_AUDIT_DAYS", "365"))
        self.retention_offline_days: int = int(os.getenv("RETENTION_OFFLINE_DAYS", "7"))
        self.policy_version: str = "2026-01"

    @property
    def is_production(self) -> bool:
        return self.environment == "production"

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request, Response, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.cookies import clear_auth_cookies, set_auth_cookies
from app.core.deps import bearer, csrf_valid, get_current_user, get_db
from app.core.security import (
    create_access_token,
    create_ws_ticket,
    decode_access_token,
    hash_password,
    new_csrf_token,
    verify_password,
)
from app.db.context import auth_context, set_user_context
from app.models import ConsentRecord, JourneyDNA, Profile, User
from app.schemas.schemas import LoginIn, RegisterIn
from app.services.auth_sessions import (
    create_session,
    revoke_session,
    rotate_refresh_token,
)
from app.services.common import default_dna
from app.services.serializers import user_out

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/auth", tags=["auth"])


def _start_session(
    response: Response, db: Session, user: User, request: Request
) -> dict:
    set_user_context(db, user.id, user.is_admin)
    session, refresh_token = create_session(db, user, request)
    access_token = create_access_token(user.id, user.email, session_id=session.id)
    csrf_token = new_csrf_token()
    db.commit()
    set_auth_cookies(response, access_token, refresh_token, csrf_token)
    return {
        "access_token": access_token,
        "token_type": "bearer",
        "expires_in": settings.access_token_expire_minutes * 60,
        "csrf_token": csrf_token,
        "user": user_out(user),
    }


@router.post("/register", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
def register(
    payload: RegisterIn,
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    auth_context(db)
    email = payload.email.lower().strip()
    if db.query(User).filter(User.email == email).first():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="An account with this email already exists")
    user = User(
        email=email,
        password_hash=hash_password(payload.password),
        display_name=payload.display_name.strip(),
    )
    db.add(user)
    db.flush()
    set_user_context(db, user.id)
    db.add(Profile(user_id=user.id, interests=[]))
    db.add(JourneyDNA(user_id=user.id, scores=default_dna(), source="explicit"))
    db.add(
        ConsentRecord(
            user_id=user.id,
            kind="terms",
            granted=True,
            policy_version=settings.policy_version,
        )
    )
    for kind in ("personalization", "analytics", "location", "marketing"):
        db.add(
            ConsentRecord(
                user_id=user.id,
                kind=kind,
                granted=False,
                policy_version=settings.policy_version,
            )
        )
    db.commit()
    return _start_session(response, db, user, request)


@router.post("/login")
def login(
    payload: LoginIn,
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    auth_context(db)
    email = payload.email.lower().strip()
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.email == email).first()
    if not user or not verify_password(payload.password, user.password_hash):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Incorrect email or password"
        )
    if not user.is_active or user.deleted_at:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="This account is no longer active")
    set_user_context(db, user.id, user.is_admin)
    return _start_session(response, db, user, request)


@router.post("/refresh")
def refresh(request: Request, response: Response, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    auth_context(db)
    token = request.cookies.get(settings.refresh_cookie)
    if not token:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="No refresh session"
        )
    session, new_refresh, user = rotate_refresh_token(db, token, request)
    if not session or not user:
        clear_auth_cookies(response)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Session expired or revoked. Sign in again.",
        )
    set_user_context(db, user.id, user.is_admin)
    access_token = create_access_token(user.id, user.email, session_id=session.id)
    csrf_token = new_csrf_token()
    set_auth_cookies(response, access_token, new_refresh, csrf_token)
    return {
        "access_token": access_token,
        "token_type": "bearer",
        "expires_in": settings.access_token_expire_minutes * 60,
        "csrf_token": csrf_token,
        "user": user_out(user),
    }


@router.get("/me")
def me(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    return user_out(user)


@router.post("/ws-ticket")
def ws_ticket(
    request: Request,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(bearer),
):
    from app.core.deps import _token_from_request

    token, _ = _token_from_request(request, credentials)
    payload = decode_access_token(token or "")
    session_id = payload.get("sid") if payload else None
    if not session_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Sign in again to open live updates")
    return {"ticket": create_ws_ticket(user.id, session_id), "expires_in": 120}


@router.post("/logout")
def logout(
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(bearer),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    from app.core.deps import _token_from_request

    auth_context(db)
    token, source = _token_from_request(request, credentials)
    if source == "cookie" and not csrf_valid(request):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="CSRF validation failed")

    revoked = False
    refresh_token = request.cookies.get(settings.refresh_cookie)
    if refresh_token:
        session_id = refresh_token.partition(".")[0]
        if session_id:
            revoke_session(db, session_id)
            revoked = True
    if token:
        payload = decode_access_token(token)
        session_id = payload.get("sid") if payload else None
        if session_id:
            revoke_session(db, session_id)
            revoked = True
    clear_auth_cookies(response)
    # Idempotent on purpose: logging out an already-cleared browser must not fail.
    return {"ok": True, "revoked": revoked}

import hmac
from collections.abc import Callable

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request, status
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.security import decode_access_token
from app.db.context import set_context, set_user_context
from app.db.session import SessionLocal
from app.models import Trip, TripMember, User
from app.services.auth_sessions import session_is_active

bearer = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)

SAFE_METHODS = {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"}


def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()


def _token_from_request(
    request: Request, credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    if credentials and credentials.scheme.lower() == "bearer":
        return credentials.credentials, "bearer"
    cookie = request.cookies.get(settings.access_cookie)
    if cookie:
        return cookie, "cookie"
    return None, None


def csrf_valid(request: Request) -> bool:
    cookie = request.cookies.get(settings.csrf_cookie)
    header = request.headers.get(settings.csrf_header)
    if not cookie or not header:
        return False
    return hmac.compare_digest(cookie, header)


def _resolve_user(
    request: Request,
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None,
    db: Session,
) -> User | None:
    token, source = _token_from_request(request, credentials)
    if not token:
        return None
    if (
        source == "cookie"
        and request.method not in SAFE_METHODS
        and not csrf_valid(request)
    ):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="CSRF validation failed")
    payload = decode_access_token(token)
    if not payload or not payload.get("sub"):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Invalid or expired session",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    # Set the RLS identity from the verified token before reading any row.
    set_user_context(db, payload["sub"])
    user = db.get(User, payload["sub"])
    if not user or not user.is_active or user.deleted_at:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Account unavailable"
        )
    if user.is_admin:
        set_context(db, app_admin="on")
    session_id = payload.get("sid")
    if session_id and not session_is_active(db, session_id, user.id):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Session expired or revoked",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    return user


def get_current_user(
    request: Request,
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(bearer),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> User:
    user = _resolve_user(request, credentials, db)
    if user is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
            detail="Authentication required",
            headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
        )
    return user


def get_optional_user(
    request: Request,
    credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None = Depends(bearer),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> User | None:
    try:
        return _resolve_user(request, credentials, db)
    except HTTPException:
        return None


def require_admin(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
    if not user.is_admin:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Administrator access required")
    return user


def get_trip_and_member(
    trip_id: str,
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    roles: set[str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[Trip, TripMember]:
    trip = db.get(Trip, trip_id)
    if not trip or trip.deleted_at:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Trip not found")
    member = (
        db.query(TripMember)
        .filter(
            TripMember.trip_id == trip_id,
            TripMember.user_id == user.id,
            TripMember.status == "active",
        )
        .first()
    )
    if not member:
        # Deliberately 404 rather than 403 so private trip existence is not leaked.
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Trip not found")
    if roles and member.role not in roles:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403, detail="Your trip role does not allow this action"
        )
    return trip, member


def trip_dependency(roles: set[str] | None = None) -> Callable:
    """Build a FastAPI dependency that resolves trip + membership."""

    def dependency(
        trip_id: str,
        db: Session = Depends(get_db),
        user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    ) -> tuple[Trip, TripMember]:
        return get_trip_and_member(trip_id, db, user, roles)

    return dependency

Auth seems solid. CSRF applies to all unsafe cookie requests, good.

Now inspect trips.py for member/invite/role edge cases; itinerary proposals for concurrency; memories privacy; expenses; WS.

def _trip(db, trip_id, user, roles=None):

def _validate_dates(start: date, end: date) -> None:

    return (

        .all()
    )
    result = []
    for membership in memberships:
        trip = db.get(Trip, membership.trip_id)
        if not trip or trip.deleted_at:

        result.append(trip_out(db, trip, membership))
    result.sort(key=lambda item: (item["start_date"] or date.max))

@router.post("", status_code=201)
async def create_trip(
    payload: TripCreate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    _validate_dates(payload.start_date, payload.end_date)
    destination = db.get(Destination, payload.destination_id) if payload.destination_id else None
    if payload.destination_id and not destination:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Destination not found")
    trip = Trip(
        name=payload.name.strip(),
        description=payload.description,
        destination_id=destination.id if destination else None,
        destination_name=(destination.name if destination else payload.destination_name or "").strip(),
        start_date=payload.start_date,
        end_date=payload.end_date,
        group_size=payload.group_size,
        budget_total=payload.budget_total,
        currency=payload.currency.upper()[:8],
        base_lat=destination.lat if destination else 0.0,
        base_lon=destination.lon if destination else 0.0,
        created_by=user.id,
        privacy="private",
    )
    db.add(trip)
    db.flush()
    membership = TripMember(
        trip_id=trip.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        role="owner",
        status="active",
        display_name=user.display_name,
    )
    db.add(membership)
    db.flush()
    db.add(Itinerary(trip_id=trip.id, confirmed_version=0))
    audit(
        db,
        action="trip.create",
        entity_type="trip",
        entity_id=trip.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"name": trip.name},
    )
    db.commit()
    return trip_out(db, trip, membership)

):
    trip, member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})

        _validate_dates(

    for field, value in data.items():

        entity_id=trip.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,

    await manager.broadcast(

@router.patch("/{trip_id}/members/{member_id}")
async def update_member_role(
    trip_id: str,
    member_id: str,
    payload: MemberRoleUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, actor = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    target = db.get(TripMember, member_id)
    if not target or target.trip_id != trip.id or target.status != "active":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Member not found")
    if target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Transfer ownership explicitly; it cannot be overwritten")
    if payload.role == "owner":
        if actor.role != "owner":
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Only the owner can transfer ownership")
        actor.role = "admin"
        target.role = "owner"
    else:
        if target.user_id == user.id:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="You cannot change your own role")
        target.role = payload.role
    audit(
        db,
        action="member.role_update",
        entity_type="trip_member",
        entity_id=target.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"role": payload.role},
    )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id,
        event_payload(
            "member.role_updated",
            trip_id=trip.id,
            member_id=target.id,
            role=target.role,
        ),
    )
    return member_out(db, target, user.id)


@router.delete("/{trip_id}/members/{member_id}")
async def remove_member(
    trip_id: str,
    member_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, actor = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    target = db.get(TripMember, member_id)
    if not target or target.trip_id != trip.id or target.status != "active":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Member not found")
    if target.id == actor.id and target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Transfer ownership to another member before leaving the trip.",
        )
    if target.id != actor.id and actor.role not in {"owner", "admin"}:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Only owners and admins can remove members")
    if target.role == "owner":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="The owner cannot be removed")
    target.status = "left"
    audit(
        db,
        action="member.remove",
        entity_type="trip_member",
        entity_id=target.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
    )
    if target.user_id and target.id != actor.id:
        db.add(
            Notification(
                user_id=target.user_id,
                trip_id=trip.id,
                kind="member_removed",
                title=f"You were removed from {trip.name}",
                link=f"/dashboard",
            )
        )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id, event_payload("member.removed", trip_id=trip.id, member_id=target.id)
    )
    return {"ok": True}


@router.post("/{trip_id}/invitations", status_code=201)
def create_invitation(
    trip_id: str,
    payload: InviteCreate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, {"owner", "admin"})
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
    invitation = TripInvitation(
        trip_id=trip.id,
        token=token,
        email=str(payload.email).lower() if payload.email else None,
        role=payload.role,
        scope=payload.scope,
        created_by=user.id,
        expires_at=utcnow() + timedelta(days=payload.expires_in_days),
    )
    db.add(invitation)
    audit(
        db,
        action="invitation.create",
        entity_type="trip_invitation",
        entity_id=invitation.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"role": payload.role, "scope": payload.scope},
    )
    db.commit()
    data = invitation_out(invitation, trip)
    data["path"] = f"/invite/{token}"
    return data

@invitations_router.get("/{token}")
def preview_invitation(
    token: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    set_context(db, app_invitation_token=token)
    invitation = (
        db.query(TripInvitation).filter(TripInvitation.token == token).first()
    )
    if not invitation:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Invitation not found")
    now = utcnow()
    if invitation.expires_at and invitation.expires_at < now:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=410, detail="This invitation has expired")
    trip = db.get(Trip, invitation.trip_id)
    if not trip or trip.deleted_at:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Trip not available")
    with system_context(db):
        member_count = (
            db.query(TripMember)
            .filter(TripMember.trip_id == trip.id, TripMember.status == "active")
            .count()
        )
    return {
        "trip": {
            "id": trip.id,
            "name": trip.name,
            "destination_name": trip.destination_name,
            "start_date": trip.start_date,
            "end_date": trip.end_date,
            "group_size": trip.group_size,
            "member_count": member_count,
        },
        "role": invitation.role,
        "scope": invitation.scope,
        "invited_by": db.get(User, invitation.created_by).display_name if db.get(User, invitation.created_by) else None,
        "expires_at": invitation.expires_at,
        "already_member": _active_member(db, trip.id, user.id) is not None,
        "accepted": invitation.accepted_at is not None,
        "accepted_by_you": invitation.accepted_by == user.id,
        "email_bound": invitation.email is not None,
    }


@invitations_router.post("/{token}/accept")
async def accept_invitation(
    token: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    set_context(db, app_invitation_token=token)
    invitation = (
        db.query(TripInvitation).filter(TripInvitation.token == token).first()
    )
    if not invitation:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Invitation not found")
    now = utcnow()
    if invitation.expires_at and invitation.expires_at < now:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=410, detail="This invitation has expired")
    if invitation.email and invitation.email != (user.email or "").lower():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=403,
            detail="This invitation was issued to a different email address",
        )
    if invitation.accepted_at and invitation.accepted_by != user.id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=409,
            detail="This invitation has already been used",
        )
    trip = db.get(Trip, invitation.trip_id)
    if not trip or trip.deleted_at:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Trip not available")
    member = _active_member(db, trip.id, user.id)
    if not member:
        existing = (
            db.query(TripMember)
            .filter(TripMember.trip_id == trip.id, TripMember.user_id == user.id)
            .first()
        )
        if existing:
            existing.status = "active"
            existing.role = invitation.role
            member = existing
        else:
            member = TripMember(
                trip_id=trip.id,
                user_id=user.id,
                role=invitation.role,
                status="active",
                display_name=user.display_name,
                invited_by=invitation.created_by,
            )
            db.add(member)
    if not invitation.accepted_at:
        invitation.accepted_at = now
        invitation.accepted_by = user.id
    audit(
        db,
        action="invitation.accept",
        entity_type="trip_invitation",
        entity_id=invitation.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
    )
    notify_trip_members(
        db,
        trip,
        kind="member_joined",
        title=f"{user.display_name} joined {trip.name}",
        link=f"/trips/{trip.id}/members",
        exclude_user_id=user.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id,
        event_payload("member.joined", trip_id=trip.id, display_name=user.display_name),
    )
    return trip_out(db, trip, member)


def _next_action(db: Session, trip: Trip, member: TripMember, user: User) -> dict:
    """Decision Load Governor (F49): one clear next action for this stage."""
    today = date.today()
    items = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id, ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed")
        .count()
    )
    today_items = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(
            ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id,
            ItineraryItem.day == today,
            ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed",
        )
        .count()
    )
    pulse = (
        db.query(TripPulse)
        .filter(
            TripPulse.trip_id == trip.id,
            TripPulse.user_id == user.id,
            TripPulse.pulse_date == today,
        )
        .first()
    )
    open_proposals = (
        db.query(ItineraryProposal)
        .filter(ItineraryProposal.trip_id == trip.id, ItineraryProposal.status == "open")
        .count()
    )
    has_batch = (
        db.query(RecommendationBatch)
        .filter(RecommendationBatch.trip_id == trip.id)
        .first()
        is not None
    )

    if trip.start_date <= today <= trip.end_date:
        if not pulse:
            action = {
                "title": "Share today's Trip Pulse",
                "reason": "The plan for today adapts to your energy, time and interests.",
                "href": f"/trips/{trip.id}/pulse",
                "kind": "pulse",
            }
        elif today_items:
            action = {
                "title": "Open today's plan",
                "reason": "Your confirmed items for today are ready.",
                "href": f"/trips/{trip.id}/itinerary",
                "kind": "today",
            }
        else:
            action = {
                "title": "Find something for today",
                "reason": "No confirmed items today — let the group engine suggest options.",
                "href": f"/trips/{trip.id}/engine",

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/trips", tags=["itinerary"])

ADMIN_ROLES = {"owner", "admin"}


def _trip(db, trip_id, user, roles=None):
    return get_trip_and_member(trip_id, db, user, roles)


def _get_itinerary(db: Session, trip: Trip) -> Itinerary:
    itinerary = db.query(Itinerary).filter(Itinerary.trip_id == trip.id).first()
    if not itinerary:
        itinerary = Itinerary(trip_id=trip.id, confirmed_version=0)
        db.add(itinerary)
        db.flush()
    return itinerary


def _serialize_items(db: Session, items: list[ItineraryItem], viewer_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    activity_ids = [item.activity_id for item in items if item.activity_id]
    activities = (
        db.query(Activity).filter(Activity.id.in_(activity_ids)).all() if activity_ids else []
    )
    activity_map = {activity.id: activity for activity in activities}
    place_ids = [activity.place_id for activity in activities if activity.place_id]
    places = db.query(Place).filter(Place.id.in_(place_ids)).all() if place_ids else []
    place_map = {place.id: place for place in places}
    destination_ids = {activity.destination_id for activity in activities}
    destinations = (
        db.query(Destination).filter(Destination.id.in_(destination_ids)).all()
        if destination_ids
        else []
    )
    destination_map = {destination.id: destination for destination in destinations}

    attendance_rows = (
        db.query(ItineraryAttendance)
        .filter(ItineraryAttendance.item_id.in_([item.id for item in items]))
        .all()
        if items
        else []
    )
    attendance: dict[str, list[ItineraryAttendance]] = {}
    for row in attendance_rows:
        attendance.setdefault(row.item_id, []).append(row)

    result = []
    for item in items:
        activity = activity_map.get(item.activity_id) if item.activity_id else None
        payload = item_out(item)
        payload["activity"] = (
            activity_out(
                activity,
                place_map.get(activity.place_id),
                destination_map.get(activity.destination_id),
            )
            if activity
            else None
        )
        rows = attendance.get(item.id, [])
        payload["attendance"] = {
            "in": len([row for row in rows if row.status == "in"]),
            "out": len([row for row in rows if row.status == "out"]),
            "join_later": len([row for row in rows if row.status == "join_later"]),
            "my_status": next(
                (row.status for row in rows if row.user_id == viewer_id), "in"
            ),
        }
        result.append(payload)
    return result


@router.get("/{trip_id}/itinerary")
def get_itinerary(
    trip_id: str,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, member = _trip(db, trip_id, user)
    itinerary = _get_itinerary(db, trip)
    items = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(
            ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id,
            ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed",
        )
        .order_by(ItineraryItem.day, ItineraryItem.sort_order, ItineraryItem.start_time)
        .all()
    )
    versions = (
        db.query(ItineraryVersion)
        .filter(ItineraryVersion.itinerary_id == itinerary.id)
        .order_by(ItineraryVersion.version.desc())
        .limit(15)
        .all()
    )
    open_proposals = (
        db.query(ItineraryProposal)
        .filter(ItineraryProposal.trip_id == trip.id, ItineraryProposal.status == "open")
        .all()
    )
    total_cost = sum(item.cost_estimate for item in items)
    return {
        "itinerary_id": itinerary.id,
        "confirmed_version": itinerary.confirmed_version,
        "my_role": member.role,
        "items": _serialize_items(db, items, user.id),
        "versions": [version_out(version) for version in versions],
        "open_proposals": len(open_proposals),
        "totals": {
            "items": len(items),
            "cost": round(total_cost, 2),
            "currency": trip.currency,
            "days": len({item.day for item in items}),
            "protected_items": len([item for item in items if item.is_protected]),
        },
    }


def _next_sort_order(db: Session, trip_id: str, item_day: date) -> int:
    last = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip_id, ItineraryItem.day == item_day)
        .order_by(ItineraryItem.sort_order.desc())
        .first()
    )
    return (last.sort_order + 1) if last else 0


def _within_trip(trip: Trip, day: date) -> None:
    if day < trip.start_date or day > trip.end_date:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail=(
                f"{day.isoformat()} is outside the trip dates "
                f"({trip.start_date.isoformat()} to {trip.end_date.isoformat()})."
            ),
        )


def _validate_times(
    start_time: str,
    end_time: str | None,
    *,
    has_activity: bool,
    is_protected: bool,
) -> None:
    start = parse_hhmm(start_time)
    end = parse_hhmm(end_time)
    if start is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="start_time must use HH:MM")
    if end is not None and end <= start:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="end_time must be later than start_time")
    if is_protected and not has_activity and end is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail="Protected time without an activity needs an end_time so the reservation is unambiguous.",
        )


def _protected_conflict(
    db: Session,
    trip: Trip,
    day: date,
    *,
    start_minutes: int,
    duration_minutes: int,
    exclude_item_id: str | None = None,
) -> dict | None:
    conflicts = (
        db.query(ItineraryItem)
        .filter(
            ItineraryItem.trip_id == trip.id,
            ItineraryItem.day == day,
            ItineraryItem.status == "confirmed",
        )
        .all()
    )
    conflict = find_conflict(
        db,
        conflicts,
        start_minutes=start_minutes,
        duration_minutes=duration_minutes,
        ignore_item_ids={exclude_item_id} if exclude_item_id else None,
    )
    return conflict if conflict and conflict["protected"] else None


def _raise_protected_conflict(conflict: dict) -> None:
    raise HTTPException(
        status_code=409,
        detail={
            "message": "This time overlaps protected time. Choose another slot or change the protected block explicitly.",
            "conflict": conflict,
        },
    )

@router.patch("/{trip_id}/itinerary/items/{item_id}")
async def update_item(
    trip_id: str,
    item_id: str,
    payload: ItemUpdate,
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    trip, _member = _trip(db, trip_id, user, ADMIN_ROLES)
    item = db.get(ItineraryItem, item_id)
    if not item or item.trip_id != trip.id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Itinerary item not found")
    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    if "day" in data:
        _within_trip(trip, data["day"])
    if {"start_time", "end_time", "day", "is_protected"} & data.keys():
        activity = db.get(Activity, item.activity_id) if item.activity_id else None
        prospective_day = data.get("day", item.day)
        prospective_start = data.get("start_time", item.start_time)
        prospective_end = data.get("end_time", item.end_time)
        prospective_protected = data.get("is_protected", item.is_protected)
        _validate_times(
            prospective_start,
            prospective_end,
            has_activity=activity is not None,
            is_protected=prospective_protected,
        )
        if data.get("status", item.status) == "confirmed":
            start = parse_hhmm(prospective_start)
            end = parse_hhmm(prospective_end)
            duration = (
                end - start
                if end is not None and start is not None
                else (activity.duration_minutes if activity else 90)
            )
            conflict = _protected_conflict(
                db,
                trip,
                prospective_day,
                start_minutes=start,
                duration_minutes=duration,
                exclude_item_id=item.id,
            )
            if conflict:
                _raise_protected_conflict(conflict)
    for field, value in data.items():
        setattr(item, field, value)
    db.flush()
    itinerary = _get_itinerary(db, trip)
    record_itinerary_version(
        db, itinerary, user_id=user.id, note=f"Updated {item.title}"
    )
    audit(
        db,
        action="itinerary.item_update",
        entity_type="itinerary_item",
        entity_id=item.id,
        user_id=user.id,
        trip_id=trip.id,
        detail={"fields": list(data.keys())},
    )
    notify_trip_members(
        db,
        trip,
        kind="itinerary_updated",
        title=f"{user.display_name} updated {item.title}",
        link=f"/trips/{trip.id}/itinerary",
        exclude_user_id=user.id,
    )
    db.commit()
    await manager.broadcast(
        trip.id, event_payload("itinerary.updated", trip_id=trip.id)
    )
    return _serialize_items(db, [item], user.id)[0]
